# Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects

## Problem statement

The `test-churn` / TDD-value analysis skill only runs when an agent remembers to
invoke it, so test-suite growth and rewrite trends across the managed projects
are not monitored continuously. The herdr downtime dispatcher already runs
per-project scheduled prompts (`/skill:refactor`, `/skill:standup`) from
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, but `test-churn` is not registered anywhere,
so no project produces periodic test-health evidence.

## Users

- **Maintainer / producer** — "I want weekly test-churn evidence for every
  managed project without asking an agent to run it."
- **Agent starting refactor or planning work** — "I want the latest test-health
  report to already exist when I start, so I can spot a suite growing without
  benefit."
- **Dispatcher operator** — "I want the schedule to fail closed, be visible
  when a project cannot be analysed, and never block the host with simultaneous
  heavy scans, so a stale or missing report never looks healthy."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `/skill:test-churn` entry is registered in SorraAgents'
   `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` using the existing schema (`id`, non-empty
   `prompt`, positive `intervalDays`, valid `HH:MM` `time`, and
   `lastTriggeredAt`), with the first provision setting a deterministic,
   staggered `lastTriggeredAt` seed and a distinct `time` (see AC3);
   re-running provisioning neither duplicates the entry, re-staggers it, nor
   changes any other entry's `lastTriggeredAt`.
2. Every configured managed project root receives the same entry via
   create-if-absent provisioning of its own
   `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`; this explicitly includes
   **Tableau-Card-Engine**, which currently has no scheduled-prompts file, so
   the command must create one. Absent or non-existent roots are skipped with a
   logged warning; the provisioning command supports `--dry-run` and is
   idempotent (a second run reports "already present" and writes nothing).
3. **Staggering (no CPU blocking):** provisioned entries are spread
   deterministically across the managed set so no two projects are due in the
   same idle cycle. Each entry gets a unique `time` within a documented window
   (away from the 06:05 standup slot), and its `lastTriggeredAt` seed offsets its
   `intervalDays` cycle by a project-index-derived amount. The scheme is
   deterministic for a given managed-root list and clock (injectable `--now`
   for tests), documented, and covered by tests asserting no duplicate `time`
   values and evenly spread day offsets.
4. Each scheduled run writes
   `<project-root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md` and
   `test_churn_data.json`; a re-run on the same date deterministically
   overwrites those two files and creates no duplicate files or directories.
5. Failures are surfaced: an inaccessible, non-git, or analyser-error root
   produces a non-zero exit code and a per-root error line on stderr (plus a
   run summary), and is never reported as a silent success.
6. The interval is configurable per entry in `scheduled-prompts.json` and via a
   provisioning `--interval-days` flag; the default (**7 days, weekly**) is
   documented in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` with its rationale.
7. Automated tests cover: entry provisioning (insert, preserve other entries,
   idempotent re-run, create-if-absent including an absent file, malformed or
   invalid config), staggering (unique `time`, spread day offsets, no
   re-stagger on re-run), managed-root iteration (existing, absent and non-git
   roots), date-partitioned output and idempotent overwrite, and non-zero
   failure propagation.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md`, `README.md`, and
   `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` (default interval, staggering and
   rationale).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Decisions (producer, 2026-11-01)

- **Q1 — fan-out shape: Option A.** One `/skill:test-churn` entry in each
  managed project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, with start times varied
  per project to prevent CPU blocking.
- **Q2 — managed-root source: Option A.** A checked-in managed-root list in
  SorraAgents. Tableau-Card-Engine must be given a schedule file
  (create-if-absent). The stale `open_source_llm` root is removed by a separate
  work item, **SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ**.
- **Q3 — default interval: Option A (7 days, weekly)**, with the day and time
  varied per project.

## Constraints

- `.worklog/` is ignored via `.worklog/*` in SorraAgents (the
  `scheduled-prompts.json` file is tracked despite that); the file lives
  per-project. The worktree-isolation rule forbids editing sibling projects'
  files from the SorraAgents worktree, so cross-project provisioning must be a
  tracked helper executed at dispatch time (or an explicit operator step), not
  a set of sibling-file edits in the implementation commit.
- The herdr downtime worker reads the file per root, dispatches one due entry
  per idle slot in config order, and only during a local-LLM idle window. The
  schedule is best-effort, not a hard cron. No changes to the external
  `worklog`/herdr package are in scope.
- The dispatcher has a host-CPU gate; several `test-churn` runs starting
  together would each scan long git histories and could block dispatch.
  Staggering (AC3) is required, not optional.
- The `time` window should avoid the existing `/skill:standup` slot (06:05) and
  stay inside a documented off-peak window.
- Dispatcher-managed roots currently recorded in
  `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` are: AI_Hell,
  ContextHub, SorraAgents, Tableau-Card-Engine, open_source_llm (stale — no
  longer exists), tce-main-street, ToneForge, tce-the-rising,
  podcast-building-games. The checked-in managed-root list is authoritative for
  this item; stale-root cleanup is SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ.
- The scheduled-prompt config is fail-closed in the consumer: absent or
  malformed config yields no dispatch and invalid entries are skipped.
  Provisioning must preserve unknown/invalid entries rather than rewrite the
  file.
- The analyser is read-only against each analysed repository but runs `git`
  per root, which can be slow on long histories; a run must bound itself
  (`--since` / `--max-commits`) or accept the cost.
- Tests must be run through the test skill (`/skill:test`); direct `pytest` or
  `node --test` invocations are prohibited.

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/` exists with `SKILL.md`,
  `scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` and `tests/`. The analyser already supports
  `--project-root`, `--output-dir`, `--report-name`, `--json-name`, `--since`,
  `--max-commits`, `--branch`, `--format`, `--stdout`, `--quiet`, and returns 1
  on `GitError`.
- SorraAgents `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` currently has `/skill:refactor`
  (3 days) and `/skill:standup` (1 day, 06:05).
- Scheduled-prompt ownership: schema and dispatch semantics live in the
  external `worklog` package (`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`;
  documented in its `CONFIG.md` § Scheduled-prompts config). `wl init`
  provisions a base file create-if-absent.
- Tableau-Card-Engine has a `.worklog/` directory but **no**
  `scheduled-prompts.json`.
- The stale `open_source_llm` root exists only as a cursor entry in
  `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`; its directory is gone.
- No scheduling, fan-out, or managed-root config exists for `test-churn`, and
  no documentation mentions periodic test-churn runs.
- `reports/` already exists at the SorraAgents repo root.

## Desired change

1. Add a tracked managed-root list (e.g. `skill/test-churn/managed-roots.json`)
   seeded from the dispatcher roots, excluding the stale `open_source_llm`.
2. Add
   `skill/test-churn/scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py`, which for each
   configured root inserts
   `{ "id": "/skill:test-churn", "prompt": "/skill:test-churn",
   "intervalDays": 7 }` create-if-absent into its
   `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, preserving all existing entries and
   `lastTriggeredAt`. It assigns a unique `time` per project (documented
   off-peak window, e.g. 02:00 + 40-minute steps) and a staggered
   `lastTriggeredAt` seed derived from the project index and the interval, so
   projects fall due on different days and times. It supports `--root`
   (repeatable), `--interval-days`, `--dry-run` and `--now` (tests).
3. Add `/skill:test-churn` to SorraAgents' `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`
   with the same staggering rules.
4. Add a thin wrapper (or documented invocation) so a scheduled run writes
   `<root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md` and
   `test_churn_data.json`, overwriting the same date idempotently and exiting
   non-zero on failure.
5. Tests and docs per the acceptance criteria.
6. Reference **SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ** for removing the stale `open_source_llm`
   cursor entry (out of scope here).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — add a "Scheduled runs" section (enable/disable,
  interval, staggering, output path, failure behaviour).
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/run_scheduled.py` — NEW wrapper: resolve the root,
  write the dated output directory, propagate the analyser exit code.
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py` — NEW idempotent
  provisioning with deterministic staggering.
- `skill/test-churn/managed-roots.json` — NEW authoritative managed-root list.
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_scheduled_runs.py` — NEW tests for provisioning,
  staggering, root iteration, dated output/idempotency and failure propagation.
- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — add the SorraAgents entry.
- `README.md` — mention/link the scheduled-run setup.
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — default interval, staggering
  scheme and rationale.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: CPU blocking.** Simultaneous whole-history scans across roots could
  trip the dispatcher's host-CPU gate. *Mitigation:* mandatory deterministic
  staggering of day and time per project (AC3), plus optional
  `--max-commits`/`--since` bounds.
- **Risk: worktree isolation.** Committing sibling projects' `.worklog` files
  from the SorraAgents worktree is forbidden. *Mitigation:* ship a tracked
  helper; do not edit sibling worklogs in the implementation commit.
- **Risk: silent staleness.** A project with no report looks healthy.
  *Mitigation:* per-root failure summary, non-zero exit, and the date in the
  output path.
- **Risk: schedule is best-effort.** It depends on an idle window, so reports
  may be late. *Mitigation:* document as best-effort; the interval gate
  prevents over-firing.
- **Risk: staggering drift.** A new project appended to the list could shift
  every entry's assigned slot. *Mitigation:* never re-stagger an existing entry;
  assign new roots the next free slot deterministically.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Integrating test-churn into `/skill:refactor` is a
  separate item (SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC). *Mitigation:* keep this item to
  registration, provisioning and scheduled execution only.
- **Assumption:** the managed-root list is the authoritative "all projects" set
  for this item; the live dispatcher root set may differ until the stale root
  is cleaned up.

## Related work

### Prerequisites / precedent

- **SA-0MV28WNFY009DF6Y** (completed epic) — migrated test-churn into
  SorraAgents and made reporting reproducible. The stated dependency is met.
- **SA-0MV28WS5G004YNNS** (completed) — created the reproducible test-churn
  reporting skill and its entry point.
- **SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW** (completed) — fixed status detection and the
  rewrite-ratio denominator.
- **SA-0MV28WXPA003EHJC** (completed) — added the tests-added/deleted growth
  metric that the scheduled report carries.
- **SA-0MV28WROY007NAB4** (completed) — ported the analysis tooling and data.

### Discovered / out of scope

- **SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ** (open, discovered-from this item) — remove the stale
  `open_source_llm` root from the herdr downtime round-robin cursor.
- **SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC** (open) — integrate test-churn into the refactor
  skill and its report. Separate scope; this item only schedules the skill.
- **SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO** (open) — complete the test-value refactor (prune
  tests that do not earn their runtime). Consumes the same growth metrics.
- **SA-0MTYIMWQP0020ZUC** (completed) — test execution policy; scheduled runs
  and tests must respect it.

### Automated related-work report

The `find-related` sweep added: SA-0MTWO7HFW001N9QJ (standup report title),
SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG (rebuild step in implement SKILL), SA-0MUMHH4BB000WEM9
(refactor report title). These are weak/report-formatting matches, not
duplicates. No completed item satisfies this item's acceptance criteria, so no
duplicate close was performed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

### Q1 — Fan-out shape

**Question:** Should the schedule use (A) one `/skill:test-churn` entry in each
managed project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, or (B) a single SorraAgents
entry whose prompt runs a fan-out command across all managed roots?

**Recommended:** A — per-project entries match the existing `/skill:refactor`
and `/skill:standup` pattern, spread analysis load across each root's idle
window, and avoid one very long-running pane.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-01):** **A** — per-project entries, and be sure to
vary the start time per project to prevent CPU blocking. Source: interactive
reply. Recorded as AC3 (staggering) and the CPU-blocking risk.

### Q2 — Managed-root source

**Question:** Which set of projects counts as "all projects": (A) a new checked-in
managed-root list in SorraAgents, (B) the dispatcher's live
`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`, or (C) auto-discover every
git repository under `~/projects` that has a `.worklog/`?

**Recommended:** A — a checked-in list is deterministic, reviewable and testable;
the live round-robin file is runtime state that includes a stale/missing root
and can change without review.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-01):** **A** — checked-in managed-root list; give
Tableau-Card-Engine a schedule file, and create a work item to remove the stale
item (`open_source_llm`). Source: interactive reply. Tableau-Card-Engine
create-if-absent is AC2; the stale-root removal is
**SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ**.

### Q3 — Default interval

**Question:** What default `intervalDays` should the entry ship with: (A) 7
(weekly), (B) 30 (monthly), or (C) 1 (daily)?

**Recommended:** A (weekly) — the report trends test growth per calendar quarter,
so weekly captures a regression promptly without consuming an idle slot every
day; it is overridable per entry and via `--interval-days`.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-01):** **A (7 days, weekly)**, with the day and time
varied per project. Source: interactive reply. Recorded in AC3/AC6 and the
default-interval documentation requirement (AC8).

### Duplicate check

Duplicate-work detection was performed (`wl search test-churn`,
`wl search "scheduled prompts"`, `wl search "test churn"`). No completed item
satisfies this item's acceptance criteria; the closest overlapping item,
SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC, integrates test-churn into the refactor report and is
explicitly out of scope here.
## Plan (2026-11-13)

Five vertical-slice children, each delivering code + tests + docs for its slice,
in dependency order (test-first within each slice; see `wl dep list`).

| # | Child | Issue | Delivers | Parent ACs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Dated scheduled-run wrapper for test-churn** (SA-0MWFLJXIF008RQ4D) | feature | `scripts/run_scheduled.py` + tests + `SKILL.md` § Scheduled runs | AC4, AC5 |
| 2 | **Checked-in managed-root list for test-churn** (SA-0MWFLK30Q004W0WZ) | feature | `managed-roots.json` + `scripts/managed_roots.py` + tests + reference doc | AC2 (root set), AC7 (iteration) |
| 3 | **Idempotent scheduled-prompt provisioning with staggering** (SA-0MWFLK8A60070MFH) | feature | `scripts/provision_scheduled_prompts.py` + tests + docs | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6, AC7 |
| 4 | **Register SorraAgents schedule and document roll-out** (SA-0MWFLKCWL007NS9U) | feature | `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` entry, roll-out evidence, README + reference docs, schema regression test | AC1, AC2, AC6, AC8 |
| 5 | **Verify scheduled test-churn delivery end to end** (SA-0MWFLKIUL004R0PZ) | task | AC traceability, full-suite evidence, audit | AC9 |

Dependency edges: 3 → 2; 4 → 1, 3; 5 → 4.

Phasing decision: the item is small (Small/Medium, ~13 h recommended) but spans
three new scripts, a tracked config, cross-project roll-out and documentation,
so it is sliced rather than implemented as one run. Each slice is a vertical
cut (code + tests + documentation) and is independently reviewable; slice 5 is
an explicit verification increment with no production code.

### Plan decisions (implementation detail resolved during planning)

The three producer decisions (Q1 fan-out, Q2 managed-root source, Q3 seven-day
interval) were settled at intake and are unchanged. Four implementation
details were under-specified; they are resolved here conservatively in favour
of the brief's binding constraints and recorded so the producer can override
them cheaply:

1. **Staggering window/step.** AC3's binding constraint is "away from the 06:05
   standup slot" inside a documented off-peak window; its "e.g. 02:00 +
   40-minute steps" is illustrative, and a 40-minute step would place the 7th
   and 8th slots at 06:00 and 06:40 — contradicting the binding constraint.
   Adopted: **02:00 + 30-minute steps** (02:00 … 05:30 for eight roots).
2. **Day staggering.** `lastTriggeredAt = --now − (index % intervalDays)` days:
   spread across the 7-day cycle; the eighth root shares a day with the first
   but has a unique `time`, so no two roots are due in the same idle cycle.
   Existing entries are never re-staggered (parent risk: staggering drift).
3. **Dispatch priority.** New entries carry `priority: "low"` (schema default
   is `high`) so a whole-history scan yields to the project's maintenance
   routines — the CPU-blocking mitigation complementing AC3.
4. **History bound.** Scheduled runs stay whole-history (`--max-commits 0`);
   the growth metrics are whole-history by definition, so a default bound
   would silently change the trend. `--since`/`--max-commits` remain available
   for constrained operator runs.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-13 — Planned by `plan` skill: created five child items (C1–C5) in
  test-first/dependency order, wired dependency edges (3→2; 4→1,3; 5→4),
  recorded the four implementation decisions above, and advanced the item to
  `plan_complete`. Duplicate check re-run (`wl search scheduled-prompts` /
  `provisioning` / `stagger`) — no overlapping completed item; SA-0MVXUGT4N0007YDQ
  (stale root removal) and SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC (refactor integration) remain
  out of scope.

## Appendix (planning, 2026-11-13)

### Q4 — Staggering window and step size (planning detail)

**Question:** AC3 names an off-peak window but gives the example "02:00 +
40-minute steps", which would place slots at 06:00 and 06:40 for the eighth
root — inside/adjacent to the 06:05 `/skill:standup` slot that AC3 also says to
avoid. Which wins?

**Resolution (plan, 2026-11-13):** the binding constraint wins; the "e.g." is
illustrative. Provisioning uses **02:00 + 30-minute steps**, ending at 05:30
for the eight managed roots — a 35-minute margin before 06:05. Evidence:
`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` (eight live roots after
excluding `open_source_llm`) and
`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` (`time` = local wall-clock
at-or-after gate). Overridable in one line if the producer prefers 01:00 +
40-minute steps.

### Q5 — Dispatch priority of the new entry

**Question:** the schema defaults an absent `priority` to `high`; a
whole-history git scan is the heaviest scheduled prompt in the set. Should the
test-churn entry declare `low`?

**Resolution (plan, 2026-11-13):** yes — `priority: "low"`, as the documented
complement to AC3's staggering (heavy scans yield to `/skill:test`,
`/skill:standup` and `/skill:refactor`). Evidence: `scheduled-prompts.ts`
(`SCHEDULED_PROMPT_DEFAULT_PRIORITY = 'high'`, polite values `low`/`medium`
per WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q AC3).

### Q6 — Bounded or unbounded history in scheduled runs

**Question:** the risks section allows "`--since` / `--max-commits` or accept
the cost". Does a scheduled run bound its history?

**Resolution (plan, 2026-11-13):** unbounded by default. The documented growth
metrics are whole-history; a default commit bound would make the weekly series
non-comparable. CPU cost is instead handled by staggering (AC3) and
`priority: "low"`. Evidence: `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md`
("deliberately uses a whole-history definition").

## Context

`skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.test.js` uses the `vitest`
framework, which SorraAgents does not depend on (`vitest` appears nowhere in
`package.json`). The full suite resolves node tests only from
`tests/{unit,node,cli}/**/*.mjs` via `node --test` (`NODE_SUITE_DIRS` in
`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`), so this file is never executed — it is the
only stray `*.test.js` left in the tree.

The file holds the CHANGELOG call-to-action (CTA) assertions authored for
SA-0MV5HRQFT0061NKH. That item's AC5 ("Tests cover: CTA present, CTA absent
(`null` and omitted), ordering relative to changelog items and release focus,
Markdown preservation, empty categories, and multiline CTA") is therefore
**currently unfulfilled in the executed suite**.

## Verified coverage gap

Grepping the executed suites confirms the assertions are **not** redundant, so
removal would silently drop a parent AC:

- `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-focus.mjs` covers `generateReleaseSection`
  release-focus rendering only — it never passes a `cta` argument.
- `tests/node/test-generate-changelog.mjs` mirrors internal logic in a local
  `testGenerateReleaseSection()` helper that has no `cta` parameter.
- `tests/unit/test-discord-notify.mjs` covers `resolveCta()` precedence (CTA
  *resolution*), not `generateReleaseSection` CTA *rendering*.

**Decision: port the assertions; do not delete the file.**

## Chosen placement

Port into a new `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-cta.mjs` using `node:test`,
mirroring the sibling `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-focus.mjs` (same
module-path constant, same `await import(MODULE_PATH)` style, same UK English
headers). `tests/unit/` is where `generateReleaseSection` pure-logic tests
already live; porting into `tests/node/test-generate-changelog.mjs` would mix a
real-module import into a file whose sections deliberately mirror logic and
whose hand-rolled `test()` runner is a different, out-of-scope style.

## Plan

Single atomic slice (documented decision: **no phasing, no children** — the
change is one file added, one file deleted; a vertical-slice split would be
artificial).

1. Create `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-cta.mjs` importing
   `generateReleaseSection` from `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js`
   with `describe`/`test` from `node:test` and `assert` from `node:assert/strict`.
2. Port all nine vitest assertions one-for-one (see AC2).
3. Delete `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.test.js`.
4. Run the changed-scope gate through the test skill (`/skill:test`), which
   picks the new file up via `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"`.

No documentation references `generate-changelog.test.js` (verified by grep), so
no docs change is required.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-cta.mjs` — new node:test file (ported assertions)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.test.js` — deleted (vitest, never executed)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` — unchanged source under test (exports `generateReleaseSection`)
- `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-focus.mjs` — unchanged style precedent (sibling `node:test` file)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-cta.mjs` exists and imports
   `generateReleaseSection` from
   `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js`, using `node:test`
   (`describe`/`test`) and `node:assert/strict` — no `vitest` import and no
   hand-rolled runner.
2. All nine assertions from the vitest file are carried over and pass: CTA
   rendered as a `> <cta>` blockquote when present; CTA emitted after the
   categorised entries; CTA omitted for `null`; CTA omitted when the argument is
   omitted (default parameter); Markdown link syntax preserved verbatim; CTA
   emitted after the `> **Release focus:**` marker; `cta=null` output
   byte-identical to omitting the argument; empty categories with a CTA render
   the version heading plus the blockquote and no category headings; a
   link-rich multiline CTA is preserved verbatim.
3. `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.test.js` is deleted, so
   `git ls-files | grep '\.test\.js$'` returns no matches.
4. The new file is genuinely picked up by the canonical suite:
   `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` executes and reports the new CTA tests as
   passing (a green run of the test skill records the evidence).
5. No production change: `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` is
   byte-identical to its pre-change state (`git diff` touches only the two test
   paths).
6. The changed-scope gate passes via the test skill (`/skill:test`) before the
   commit; the commit records the work-item id.

## Impact

Anyone reading a generated `CHANGELOG.md` can rely on the release call-to-action
rendering correctly, because those assertions now run in the real suite instead
of sitting in a vitest file the repository never executes.

## Risky assumptions

- **Porting over removal.** Assumes AC5 of SA-0MV5HRQFT0061NKH is still wanted.
  Evidence: the parent item lists it as an acceptance criterion and no executed
  test covers CTA rendering. If the producer instead wants the assertions
  dropped, this becomes a one-line deletion — cheap to reverse.
- **`tests/unit/` over `tests/node/`.** Both are in `NODE_SUITE_DIRS`, so either
  is executed; the choice is stylistic, following the sibling focus test.

discovered-from:AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0

## Problem statement

The test skill's runner (`test/scripts/run_tests.py`) reports a **false PASS** when invoked with the name-based ``--suite node`` flag on a repo whose real suite is vitest driven through an npm ``test`` script. The resolver returns an empty command list, executes nothing, exits 0, and (in the caching paths) records a green entry — so callers believe the Node/vitest suite ran when it did not.

This was found while investigating the AI_Hell repo (an npm/vitest project with co-located `src/**/*.test.ts` and no `tests/{node,cli,unit}` directories).

## Reproduction

From an npm/vitest repo (AI_Hell):

```bash
python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --suite node --force --json
```

Result:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "suites": {
    "node": {
      "success": true,
      "returncode": 0,
      "command": "",
      "failures": [],
      "cached": false,
      "scope": "full"
    }
  }
}
```

The real suite for the same repo resolves correctly only via the default `all` suite:

```bash
python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --suite all --force --json   # command: "npm --silent test"
```

## Root cause

In `run_suite()` (default test type), name-based resolution is:

- `name == "pytest"` → `[pytest_command()]`
- `name == "node"` → `node_suite_commands(cwd)`
- `name == "all"` → `full_suite_commands(cwd)`

`node_suite_commands()` only emits commands for existing `tests/{node,cli,unit}` directories and never consults the `.pi/test-config.json` extension file nor the npm-test convention. `full_suite_commands()` is the documented single source of truth and resolves extension `suiteCommands` → pytest → node dirs → **npm-test convention**; the `node` name path bypasses all of that.

Related coupling: `filter_commands_for_suite("node", …)` only keeps commands containing the substring `"node"`, so a declared `suiteCommands: ["npx vitest run"]` is also filtered out on the type-profile path.

## Impact

- Any explicit `--suite node` run on such a repo is a silent no-op reported as green (false verification evidence).
- `run_summary --suite node` reports a cache miss even after the full suite has run.
- Lower impact than the `all` path because the default `--suite all` and the audit/implement consumers use `full_suite_commands` and are correct; no known in-repo consumer invokes `--suite node`.

## Expected behaviour

A request for the `node` suite on a repo that has a Node/vitest suite must execute that suite (never an empty command set). Concretely, name-based `node` resolution should fall back in the same order as `full_suite_commands` when `node_suite_commands()` yields nothing, and `filter_commands_for_suite("node", …)` should treat declared non-`node`-substring commands (e.g. `npx vitest run`) as Node-suite commands, or the resolution order should be centralised so all suite names share one convention path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `--suite node` on an npm/vitest repo with no `tests/{node,cli,unit}` dirs resolves the same command as the npm-test convention (`npm --silent test`) or the declared `suiteCommands` (e.g. `npx vitest run`), and executes it.
2. An empty resolved command set is never reported as `success: true` for an explicitly requested suite that the repo can support; it either runs the fallback or fails with a clear diagnostic.
3. Regression tests cover: node-suite fallback to the npm-test convention; node-suite fallback to declared `suiteCommands`; `filter_commands_for_suite("node", ["npx vitest run"])` behaviour.
4. Existing full-suite / audit / implement cache-key contracts are unchanged (the `all` path behaviour is preserved).
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Evidence / references

- Originating work item: `AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0` (AI_Hell worklog).
- Test skill: `test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `run_suite()`, `node_suite_commands()`, `full_suite_commands()`, `filter_commands_for_suite()`.
- Documented resolution order: `test/SKILL.md` § "Suite-command resolution order (F2)".
- Related: `SA-0MSF8KNE3003JDVD` (node --test directory invocation), `SA-0MSJELL44009XYIL` (skip missing suite dirs).

## Implementation Plan

**Planning decision:** auto-complete (plan skill Process Step 1). This is a `chore` (not an epic) with five measurable acceptance criteria and a minimal implementation sketch, so it is planned for direct implementation rather than decomposed into child features. Splitting a single-file fix across child worktrees/sessions would add overhead without reducing risk.

### Chosen approach (documented assumption)

Centralise suite resolution so every suite name shares the convention path (the second option offered in *Expected behaviour*), rather than adding a Node-only fallback that leaves `run_summary` broken:

1. **`filter_commands_for_suite()`** — classify a command as `pytest` when it invokes pytest (align with `parse_failures()`, which already routes pytest vs everything-else), and as `node` for every other command in the resolved set. This keeps `npm --silent test`, `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`, `npx vitest run` and `node --test "tests/**/*.mjs"` as Node-suite commands and never silently drops a declared command. `all` still returns the list unchanged.
2. **Name-based `--suite node` resolution** (`run_suite`, full-scope legacy path) — when `node_suite_commands()` yields nothing, resolve through `full_suite_commands()` filtered by name, so the npm-test convention (`npm --silent test`) and a declared `suiteCommands` entry (`npx vitest run`) both execute. The `pytest` and `all` paths keep their current resolution.
3. **`run_summary()`** — already resolves through `full_suite_commands()`; the `filter_commands_for_suite` fix makes `--suite node` find the recorded `npm --silent test` entry instead of reporting a cache miss.
4. **Fail closed on empty** — an explicitly requested suite that resolves to an empty set raises the existing `unknown suite`-style `ValueError`/`TypeResolutionError` (exit 2), never `success: true` with `command: ""`.

**Assumption recorded:** classifying every non-pytest command as Node-suite is deliberately conservative and mirrors the runner's own failure-parser routing (`parse_failures()` uses the pytest parser for pytest commands and the node/vitest parser otherwise). It may include a declared non-test command (e.g. `npm --silent run lint`) when `--suite node` is explicitly requested; that is preferable to silently executing nothing. The alternative (a `node`-only fallback with `filter_commands_for_suite` unchanged) is rejected because it leaves the `run_summary` cache-miss path in AC-relevant behaviour broken.

### Test-first ordering

1. **Regression tests first** (add to `skill/test/tests/test_suite_resolution.py` and/or `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`):
   - `filter_commands_for_suite("node", ["npx vitest run"]) == ["npx vitest run"]`; `("node", ["pytest ...", "npm --silent test"])` keeps only the npm command; `all` is unchanged.
   - `--suite node` on an npm/vitest repo (package.json `test`, no `tests/{node,cli,unit}`) resolves and executes `npm --silent test` (mock `_run_cmd`, assert one spawn and `command`).
   - `--suite node` on a repo with `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands: ["npx vitest run"]` resolves and executes that command.
   - An explicit suite resolving to an empty set fails (raises) rather than reporting `success: true`/`command: ""`.
   - `run_summary(("node",))` looks up the npm/vitest command (no cache miss).
2. **Implement** the resolver/filter changes in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
3. **Docs** — update `skill/test/SKILL.md` (suite-command resolution order) and `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (`filter_commands_for_suite` semantics and the explicit-suite fallback) to state that all suite names share one convention path.
4. **Verify** the framework's full suite is green (test skill; never ad-hoc pytest).

### Affected files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `filter_commands_for_suite()`, `run_suite()` name-based resolution, `run_summary()`.
- `skill/test/tests/test_suite_resolution.py` — resolver/filter regression tests.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — explicit-suite/`run_summary` regression tests (if placed there).
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — resolution-order documentation.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — `filter_commands_for_suite` / explicit-suite fallback documentation.

### Constraints / non-goals

- The `all` path and the cached full-suite key contract must stay byte-identical (AC4); no change to `full_suite_commands()` ordering or to command strings.
- Do not alter changed-scope selection semantics beyond the shared name filter.
- Keep the fix surgical; no unrelated refactors.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were asked. Planning auto-completed per Process Step 1 because the item is a non-epic `chore` with measurable acceptance criteria and a minimal implementation sketch. The design choice between the two options in *Expected behaviour* is recorded above as a documented assumption (centralise + classify), with the rejected alternative and rationale.

# Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically (shared /tmp report path / concurrent agents)

## Problem statement

The ship skill's post-release branch cleanup (`runPostReleaseCleanup` in
`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) fails non-deterministically in a
multi-agent (herdr) environment because it reads and writes a **fixed shared
temp path** (`${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json`): when two release/cleanup
processes run concurrently, one clobbers the other's report, so the run logs
"Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.", then silently
reports "Found 0 merged local branch(es)" and "Pruned 0 local branch(es)" as
if the repository were clean, and the follow-on remote prune also fails.
Observed during the AI_Hell v0.1.10 dev→main release; the same scripts succeed
when re-run standalone.

## Users

- **Agents (Map / herdr):** run automated releases and must not be misled by a
  false "clean" cleanup results.
- **Operators:** trust that post-release cleanup either happened or produced an
  actionable, non-silent warning.
- **Other projects consuming the shared ship/cleanup skills** (AI_Hell, etc.):
  any project can hit the race when releases coincide.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a **unique temp path per run** (e.g. derived from
   `mkdtempSync`) for the summarize report; a unit test with two
   concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py` run or report read no longer silently
   reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct,
   actionable warning naming the deterministic remediation (unique temp path).
3. The cleanup stays **non-blocking**: a cleanup failure never changes the
   release exit code (existing AC3 preserved).
4. A transient failure (summarize run / report read / remote prune) is
   **retried once** before the actionable warning is emitted.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **SorraAgents** repo (ship/cleanup skills are symlinked
  from `~/.pi/agent/skills` into `SorraAgents/skill/`); AI_Hell does not vendor
  these files.
- Cleanup scripts' standalone behaviour (`summarize_branches.py`,
  `prune_local_branches.py`, `delete_remote_branches.py`) must not change.
- Non-blocking guarantee must be preserved (existing AC3 of
  SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG).
- Tests run under `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json` to
`summarize_branches.py --report` (~L1110) and reads it back (~L1135). On read
failure it sets `reportData = { branches: [] }` and logs only the generic
"skipping local cleanup" warning, then proceeds to report "Found 0 merged local
branch(es)". The branches-to-delete file already uses `mkdtempSync`
(`cleanup-branches-*`), so only the report path is shared.

## Desired change

- Derive a unique report path per run (mkdtemp-based) used for both the
  `--report` argument and the read-back, so concurrent runs cannot clobber.
- Distinguish a real "no merged branches" result from a failed enumerate/read:
  log an actionable warning (unique-path remediation) instead of the misleading
  "0 merged branches".
- Add a single retry with small backoff for the transient step(s) before
  emitting the warning, preserving non-blocking behaviour.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` with the concurrency-clobber
  test and report-failure-warning test.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `runPostReleaseCleanup` (report path
  L1110/L1135, retry logic, warning text)
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` — new AC1 concurrency fake test,
  AC2 warning test, AC4 retry test

## Risks & assumptions

- **Retry must not mask real errors** — the single retry is for transient
  failures only; the actionable warning must still be emitted on the second
  failure (assumption: failures are quiet enough to retry once without
  doubling wall-clock time; mitigation: small backoff).
- **Scope creep** — deeper cleanup-skill refactoring, branch-deletion policy
  changes, or fixing `delete_remote_branches.py`/`summarize_branches.py`
  behaviour are out of scope; if such work is discovered, record it as new
  linked work items (not here).
- **Test isolation** — the concurrency test must not touch the real
  `/tmp/cleanup-summary.json` or run real git commands; fakes only
  (assumption: existing `setupRunReleaseFixture` harness is reused/adapted).
- **Cross-repo tracking** — item originated in the AI_Hell worklog
  (AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU, moved here per producer decision Q1c); AI_Hell leaves
  no orphan reference after deletion.
- **Non-blocking guarantee** — AC3 must survive the retry addition; the retry
  must also be non-blocking.

# Audit: add a max re-ask convergence guard to the verdict workflow

## Problem statement

The audit verdict workflow can enter unbounded re-ask loops — sessions have produced four `verdict_reask` calls and three `phase2_deep` reruns without converging — causing the pipeline to burn repeated deep-analysis runs. A convergence guard must cap re-asks and fall back to a deterministic resolution strategy.

## Users

- **Audit pipeline operators**: The automated audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) that processes work items and produces verdicts.
- **Producers reviewing audit results**: Stakeholders who rely on the pipeline terminating within a reasonable time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A configurable max re-ask cap (default 2) limits the total number of `verdict_reask` retries per AC within a single audit pass.
2. When the re-ask cap is exhausted, the pipeline falls back to a majority/ensemble verdict from the set of previously obtained verdicts (including the initial call), or escalates to `partial` if verdicts are split.
3. The fallback mechanism is configurable via environment variable (`AUDIT_MAX_VERDICT_REASKS`) with a default of 2, and the current value is logged in the reliability summary.
4. All re-ask attempts (including the final fallback) are counted in the `verdict_reasks` reliability metric so operators can monitor convergence rates.
5. Phase-2 deep analysis runs are also capped: if a deep analysis re-ask fails, the pipeline does not re-launch a second deep analysis for the same AC within the same pass.

## Impact

Users running audits will see reliable termination of the verdict workflow instead of unbounded retry loops that waste compute.

## Constraints

- Must not change the verdict semantics — the fallback is a last-resort, not a preferred path.
- The guard applies per-AC within a single audit pass; it does not affect cross-pass behaviour.
- Must preserve existing JSON-contract re-ask logic (`_reask_json_array_once`) — the cap is additive.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Core verdict re-ask logic at lines ~11347–11450 (`_reask_verdict_array_once`) and ~7021–7070 (`_reask_json_array_once`)

# Worklog: stale-lock detection and bounded backoff for wl mutations

## Problem statement

`wl comment add`, `wl update`, and `wl create` repeatedly fail when `worklog-data.jsonl.lock` is held by a stale process. Agents were forced to inspect PIDs manually and sleep before retrying — a brittle, manual workaround that wastes time and can mask real contention.

## Users

- **All agents**: Any agent running `wl` commands (every agent session uses worklog).
- **Automated dispatchers**: herdr downtime worker, dispatcher sessions that run `wl` commands at scale.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl` commands detect a stale lock when the holder PID is not running, and automatically clear the lock file with a warning message.
2. `wl` commands implement bounded exponential backoff (initial 1s, max 8s, max 4 retries) when a lock is actively held by a live process, with clear diagnostic output showing the holder PID and elapsed time.
3. A new CLI flag `--force-lock` (hidden by default) allows bypassing the lock for emergency recovery, with an explicit safety warning.
4. All lock acquisition failures include a machine-parseable exit code (`exit 42` for stale lock, `exit 43` for lock timeout) for automated retry logic.
5. A diagnostic command `wl lock-status` shows the current lock state, holder PID, liveness status, and age — enabling quick troubleshooting without manual PID inspection.

## Impact

Agents will no longer need to manually investigate stale locks or guess backoff timings — wl handles contention gracefully with clear diagnostics and automatic recovery.

## Constraints

- Must not change the JSONL file format or existing lock semantics.
- The stale-lock detection must be conservative: only clear a lock if the PID is definitively dead (no process tree matches).
- Backoff parameters must be configurable via environment variable (`WORKLOG_BACKOFF_BASE=1`, `WORKLOG_BACKOFF_MAX=8`, `WORKLOG_BACKOFF_RETRIES=4`).

## Key Files

- `command/worklog.py` — Main wl CLI entry point
- `command/worklog_lock.py` (new) — Lock management module
- `.worklog/` — Lock file location

## Related work

- SA-0MVCF4NKA00484JF — Parent epic: global skill-improvement recommendations
- SA-0MVCF5TF9000KP87 — Worklog: validate/document wl CLI argument forms (related chore)
data.title: Worklog: stale-lock detection and bounded backoff for wl mutations

# Implement: pre-flight worktree existence check in parent orchestration

## Problem statement

When the parent `implement` skill spawns or resumes a child session, it references child worktrees by path. If a child worktree has been removed or pruned (e.g., from a failed previous run, manual cleanup, or `implement.py finish`), the parent falls through to `cd` and `read` failures with cryptic error messages and retry loops over stale paths.

## Users

- **Implement skill orchestrator**: The parent session that manages child worktree lifecycle.
- **Agents using `/skill:implement <epic-id>`**: Agents implementing epics with multiple children.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Before spawning or resuming a child session, the parent orchestration runs `git worktree list` (or checks the worktree path exists) and verifies the child worktree is still valid.
2. If the worktree does not exist or is invalid, the parent fails fast with a clear, actionable message: the worktree path, what was expected, and a suggestion to run `implement.py start <child-id>` to recreate it.
3. The validation happens before any `cd` into the worktree path — preventing cascading errors from stale paths.
4. A new reliability metric `stale_worktree_checks` is incremented per audit pass, logging pass/fail status.

## Impact

Agents implementing epics will see immediate, actionable error messages instead of cryptic file-not-found failures when child worktrees are stale, saving time and reducing confusion.

## Constraints

- Must not change the `implement.py` CLI contract or existing worktree lifecycle.
- The check must be lightweight: a single `git worktree list` or path existence check.
- Must work correctly when the parent and child are in different directories (worktree isolation).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Parent orchestration logic
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement_child.py` (or equivalent) — Child session entry point

## Related work

- SA-0MVCF4NKA00484JF — Parent epic: global skill-improvement recommendations

# Implement: document canonical pre-push bypass policy and push-verification step

## Problem statement

Agents discovered the `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` environment variable and the practice of pushing directly from worktrees through trial and error, then manually verified changes with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`. This ad-hoc discovery leads to inconsistent practices, missed verification steps, and guesswork about the sanctioned workflow.

## Users

- **Agents using `implement` skill**: Any agent working within a worktree who needs to push changes.
- **Reviewers**: Need to understand how work was pushed and verified.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The implement skill documentation includes a dedicated section documenting the sanctioned pre-push bypass workflow: when to use it, how to use `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`, and how to push from the worktree.
2. The documentation includes the verification recipe: `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD <base-ref>` to confirm changes are a subset of what will be merged.
3. The implement skill includes a `verify-push` helper step (or CLI flag) that performs the merge-base check automatically and reports pass/fail.
4. A clear warning is added explaining why direct pushes from worktrees are normally discouraged, and when the bypass is appropriate (e.g., the main checkout is dirty or locked).

## Impact

Agents will have a clear, documented recipe for pre-push bypass and verification — removing guesswork and ensuring consistent, auditable practices.

## Constraints

- This is primarily a documentation change; code changes are limited to a new optional verification helper.
- Must align with existing `.gitignore` and branch policies (push to `dev` only).

# Test/implement: standardize long-suite protocol (background launch + poll) and fix test_cache import path

## Problem statement

Full test suites regularly exceed the 3500s tool timeout (exit 143), requiring agents to manually relaunch with `nohup`. Additionally, the `test_cache` module import path mismatch (`skill.test_cache` vs `test_cache`) caused one retry to fail silently because cache introspection could not resolve from within a worktree.

## Users

- **Agents running test suites**: All agents that invoke the test skill or run the full suite.
- **Automated gates**: Pre-push hooks, `implement.py finish`, audit F3 cache miss.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test skill documentation includes a standard protocol for running long suites: launch with `nohup` in the background, record the PID, and poll using `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` with progress output.
2. The `test_cache` module is importable from any worktree by ensuring the shared skill directory is on `sys.path` before import — fix the import path so `test_cache` resolves correctly regardless of working directory.
3. A new CLI flag `--nohup` for the test skill launches the suite in the background and returns the PID immediately, with a follow-up flag `--status <pid>` to check progress.
4. All existing test-running scripts adopt the new protocol; the old ad-hoc `nohup` pattern is deprecated in documentation.

## Impact

Agents running full test suites will have a reliable, documented background protocol and the test_cache import will work from any worktree — no more lost retries or manual nohup invocations.

## Constraints

- Must not change the test suite itself — only the launch/poll protocol and import path.
- The `--nohup` flag must be opt-in to avoid changing existing behaviour for short suites.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — Test skill documentation
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Test runner (import path fix)
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` — Polling utility (already exists)

## Related work

- SA-0MVCF4NKA00484JF — Parent epic: global skill-improvement recommendations

# Worklog: validate/document wl CLI argument forms (create --title, comment add flags)

## Problem statement

`wl create` rejected a positional title argument and required `--title` — discovered only via failure and retry. Similarly, `wl comment add` flag forms were ambiguous. Agents had to discover the correct invocation through trial and error, wasting time on what should be trivial CLI usage.

## Users

- **All agents**: Every agent session uses `wl` for task tracking.
- **New agents**: Agents just starting with the worklog system are especially affected.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl create` accepts both `--title "..."` and a positional title argument (`wl create "Title" --parent ...`), with consistent validation across all subcommands.
2. `wl comment add` flags are documented with examples showing the canonical invocation: `wl comment add <id> --comment "..." --author "..." --json`.
3. A `wl --help` or `wl <subcommand> --help` output includes clear examples for the most commonly used commands (`create`, `update`, `comment add`, `dep add`).
4. If positional arguments are not supported, `wl create` provides a clear, actionable error message suggesting the correct flag form rather than a generic parse error.

## Impact

Agents will use the correct `wl` invocation on the first attempt, reducing friction and wasted time on CLI usage errors.

## Constraints

- Must maintain backwards compatibility with existing scripts that use `--title`.
- If accepting both positional and flag forms, the flag form takes precedence when both are provided.

## Key Files

- `command/worklog.py` — wl CLI argument parsing

## Related work

- SA-0MVCF4NKA00484JF — Parent epic: global skill-improvement recommendations
- SA-0MVCF5RKF0099K4R — Worklog: stale-lock detection (related worklog improvement)

# Test-cache key ignores environment identity: canonical post-push verification can silently cache-serve (SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L)

## Problem statement

The per-repo test cache keys entries on command + git fingerprint (HEAD + dirty-path content, or the pushed tree SHA) only. A green full-suite run recorded **inside a worktree** whose runtime environment differs from the canonical checkout — an unpopulated submodule (observed on RISE-0MVBEJ3S8006YFHK: `core` failed to clone, 'transport file not allowed', populated manually), a symlinked `node_modules`, a different interpreter — is byte-identical in key to a canonical-checkout run of the same tree, and is deliberately mirrored into `<main>/.worklog/cache` by `.githooks/pre-push` (`mirror_suite_cache`, "an identical key is an identical run"). Post-push verification, the dev-push gate's cached reuse and the audit skill can therefore report a green verdict that never executed (or never executed correctly) in the environment the verdict claims to evidence. The environment-blind key silently violates the cache's own correctness guarantee: identical key does not imply identical runtime environment.

## Users

- **Build agents using the implement skill**: an agent finishing a work item trusts "full suite green" as evidence the pushed tree passes; today a worktree-recorded run can masquerade as canonical-checkout evidence.
- **Auditors/reviewers (audit skill F3/F4)**: read-only full-suite evidence must describe the canonical checkout's environment, not a drifted worktree.

User stories:

- As a build agent, I want the post-push verification to be green only when the pushed tree is provably green in the canonical environment (fresh run or provably equivalent-environment cached run), so a drifted worktree's run cannot silently satisfy my verification.
- As an auditor, I want a cached full-suite entry to carry the environment that produced it, so I can distinguish "run in the canonical environment at this tree" from "run in a differently-provisioned worktree".

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — After `implement.py finish` pushes from a worktree, a post-push verification for the canonical (main) checkout cannot be served a full-suite entry recorded in an environment that differs from the canonical environment (submodule completeness, `node_modules` resolution, interpreter). When no canonical-environment entry exists for the pushed tree, the post-push step escalates: it executes a forced run in the canonical checkout — `--scope changed --force` as the default for narrow changes, escalating to a forced full run (`--scope full --force`) when the change is broad, a refactor, or environment drift (missing submodule, `node_modules` divergence) is detected — and uses that run as the verdict.
- AC2 — A cache-servable invocation in the canonical checkout no longer returns green from an entry recorded in a differently-provisioned worktree without executing: the environment fingerprint part of the key makes such an entry a miss, so the run executes fresh (no silent cache-serve).
- AC3 — The per-repo test cache key captures a **coarse, path-independent environment fingerprint** — submodule checkout completeness (`git submodule status`), `node_modules` resolution state (symlink target / installed lockfile state), interpreter identity — folded into the fingerprint alongside the existing git/tree state. An in-worktree run and a main-checkout run for the same commit produce distinct entries when their environments differ, and **share** entries when their environments are equivalent (path-independent reuse preserved). The environment fingerprint is computed cheaply and deterministically at lookup and store time, in the consumer's own checkout.
- AC4 — Fast iteration is preserved: targeted forced changed-scope runs remain the default post-push escalation for narrow changes; the forced full suite runs only for broad/refactor changes or detected environment drift. Same-tree + equivalent-environment cross-checkout sharing continues to work unchanged.
- AC5 — Each entry records the environment fingerprint (and its component descriptor: submodule status, `node_modules` resolution, interpreter) as provenance metadata alongside `fingerprint_kind`/`interpreter`; the pre-push mirroring either skips entries whose environment fingerprint cannot be matched to the canonical environment or records them so consumers can reject them. Documented in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (exact escalation commands, when a forced full run is required vs a targeted one), with audit skill F3/F4 notes where relevant.
- AC6 — Regression tests in `tests/` where the cache layer and gates are tested: (a) drift-keyed entries are never served to a canonical-environment consumer — the canonical lookup misses and executes; (b) equivalent-environment entries still share across checkouts (finish gate ↔ pre-push ↔ audit); (c) the escalation path runs `--scope changed --force` for narrow changes and `--scope full --force` on detected drift/refactor; (d) existing cache provenance tests stay green.
- AC7 — Validation and docs: at least one automated test exercises each changed code path above; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, module docstrings, and any relevant wiki or docs entries; the full project test suite passes with the new changes (CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).

## Impact

Agents can trust that a green post-push verification was executed against (or provably recorded in) the canonical environment — a silently cache-served verdict from a differently-provisioned worktree can no longer masquerade as proof the shipped tree passes.

## Constraints

- Do not break the audit skill's read-only full-suite verification: the 2 h TTL caching and tree-keyed reuse stay functional for entries recorded in an environment equivalent to the querying checkout.
- **Coarse and path-independent** environment identity only (producer decision Q2a): never the git common dir or absolute worktree path — that would kill the cross-checkout reuse that SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 and SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI (audit tree-keyed cache reuse, both open) rely on. Reconcile with those items rather than duplicate or block them.
- The environment fingerprint must be cheap (sub-second, no full `node_modules` tree hashing) and deterministic, so it does not add measurable overhead to the hot cache path and does not produce spurious misses on innocuous churn (npm reinstall touching mtimes without changing installed state).
- Do not break the pre-push gate's in-place worktree execution model (SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH): a fresh detached checkout has no dependencies, so the gate keeps measuring a clean checkout of the pushed commit; only the entry's bindability to canonical-environment evidence changes.
- Reconcile with SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (document pre-push bypass + verification recipe) and SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (live-repo guard) rather than duplicating.
- Escalation executes suites inside `finish`, which holds the exclusive main-checkout lock: keep the escalated run targeted by default (AC4) and route it through the existing paced/locked test runner when running in the main checkout; a dirty/locked main checkout must degrade to a documented recovery rather than a silent green.

## Existing state

- Post-push verification is read-only and tree-keyed: `_resolve_post_push_verification()` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` executes nothing; it queries the pushed commit's tree SHA (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`) in the worktree, then the main checkout (SA-0MVXUSED6008J04R; cross-check SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN). `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 has no bare `/skill:test` post-push step.
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --gate-commit <sha>` (worktree in place by design), then `mirror_suite_cache()` copies entries into `<main>/.worklog/cache` assuming content-addressed identity (SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3).
- Cache key = normalized command + git fingerprint + scope/type namespace; `store()` metadata records only `interpreter` as environment provenance. Verified against `dev` HEAD: `skill/test_cache.py` (`compute_git_state`/`compute_tree_state`, `cache_key`, `lookup`/`store`), `.githooks/pre-push` `mirror_suite_cache`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` ("Cache keys stay path-independent… an identical key is an identical run").

## Desired change

1. Add a cheap, deterministic, **path-independent environment fingerprint** (submodule completeness via `git submodule status`, `node_modules` resolution state, interpreter identity) to `skill/test_cache.py`, folded into the cache fingerprint so store and lookup bind git/tree state + environment. Record the environment descriptor as provenance metadata in each entry.
2. Update `run_tests.py` and the gate/finish call sites to compute the environment fingerprint in the checkout they measure/query, so tree-keyed and worktree-keyed lookups include it.
3. Extend `_resolve_post_push_verification()` in `implement.py` with the producer-chosen escalation (Q3a): when no canonical-environment entry exists for the pushed tree, execute `--scope changed --force` in the canonical checkout (targeted default), escalating to a forced full run on broad/refactor/drift; the escalated run's verdict replaces the read-only miss.
4. Make `mirror_suite_cache` environment-aware: only mirror (or label) entries whose environment fingerprint matches the canonical checkout, so a drifted-worktree entry cannot be served by main-checkout consumers.
5. Document the exact commands and escalation policy in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, and audit F3/F4 notes; add regression tests (AC6).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` — environment fingerprint computation + folding into `compute_git_state`/`compute_tree_state`/`cache_key`/`lookup`/`store`; provenance metadata (submodule status, `node_modules` resolution, interpreter).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — env fingerprint for gate runs (`--gate-commit`) and cache lookup/store; `--scope/--force` escalation support.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_post_push_verification()` escalation to forced targeted/full run in the canonical checkout when no canonical-environment entry exists.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — `mirror_suite_cache` environment-awareness (skip or label drift-keyed entries).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Step 9 post-push escalation wording and exact commands.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — cache-compatibility and post-push verification documentation.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — F3/F4 notes on environment-provenance-aware evidence where needed.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_*.py`, `tests/test_finish_*` (e.g. `test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py`) — regression tests for drift-miss, equivalent-env sharing, and escalation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Environment-fingerprint instability** — npm reinstall / submodule updates could churn the fingerprint and cause spurious misses (re-execution). Mitigation: use stable markers (installed-lockfile content hash, `git submodule status` output, interpreter identity) — never mtimes or a full `node_modules` tree hash.
- **Sequencing with the audit-reuse items** — SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 / SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI assume path-independent reuse; a coarse env fingerprint preserves that for equivalent environments but changes the lookup surface they build on. Mitigation: coordinate; land the fingerprint as backward-compatible (equiv-env sharing proven by tests) and cross-reference both items.
- **Escalation cost inside `finish`** — a forced run holds the exclusive main-checkout lock and competes for test slots. Mitigation: targeted `--scope changed --force` default; escalate to forced full only on broad/refactor/drift; reuse the existing paced/locked runner.
- **Dirty or locked main checkout at escalation** — the canonical checkout may not be runnable when the post-push step fires. Mitigation: documented, explicit degradation (never a silent green): report missing with a recovery recipe rather than accepting the drifted entry.
- **Scope creep** — this item must not grow into a general cache redesign (per-host caches, env pinning, cross-machine invalidation). Record such opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption** — `git submodule status` and the installed `node_modules` state are adequate coarse proxies for runtime environment; a submodule whose checkout is complete and `node_modules` whose resolution matches are equivalent for cache-reuse purposes.

## Related work

- SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN / SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG (completed) — tree-keyed gate verdicts and `fingerprint_kind="tree"`; the environment fingerprint extends this namespace.
- SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (completed) — verdict provenance ("which tree ran, cached or executed"); the environment descriptor extends provenance.
- SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3 (pre-push cache mirroring, completed) — mirroring must become environment-aware.
- SA-0MVTRBT50005DUEH (completed) — `--gate-commit` clean-checkout gate; unchanged, only entry bindability changes.
- SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 / SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI (open) — audit tree-keyed cache reuse: their path-independent-reuse assumption must stay satisfiable for equivalent environments; coordinate sequencing.
- SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (open) — pre-push bypass documentation; reconcile, do not duplicate.
- SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG (completed) — live-repo guard + push timeout; reconcile.

### Related work (automated find-related report, SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L)

- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** (completed) — push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit: the worktree-push premise behind this item.
- **SA-0MSGNUXT3009LV7S** (completed) — wire cache into `run_tests.py`: the cache integration this item extends.
- **SA-0MW6VXSF8004X1PK** (completed) — [test-failure] "post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry": evidence of the verification's cache-miss/refusal behaviour this item refines.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which half (or both) should close the gap? (a) evidence policy only; (b) key integrity only; (c) both (provenance recorded and keyed, plus a forced targeted escalation when no canonical-environment entry exists)." — Answer (producer, rgardler): **"(c) Both"** (selected option letter c). Source: interactive reply on the work item (comment SA-C0MWFYLQ9A005IQWN, 2026-11-14).
- Q2: "What counts as environment identity if the key changes? (a) coarse, path-independent environment fingerprint (submodule completeness, node_modules resolution, interpreter); (b) full checkout identity (git common dir + worktree path); (c) provenance metadata only, key unchanged." — Answer (producer, rgardler): **"(a) coarse, path-independent environment fingerprint"**. Source: interactive reply (same comment thread).
- Q3: "Post-push behaviour when the only entry is drift-keyed? (a) escalate once, targeted (`--scope changed --force` in the canonical checkout; full force for broad/refactor/drift); (b) refuse the transition and recover manually; (c) accept with an `environment_drift` note." — Answer (producer, rgardler): **"(a) escalate once, targeted"**. Source: interactive reply (same comment thread).

All three answers arrived together as "1. c / 2. a / 3. a" in reply to the recorded question comment; the recommended options were adopted as chosen. Research summary (recorded in the question comment): post-push verification is read-only + tree-keyed today; pre-push runs the gate in a clean checkout (worktree in place) and mirrors entries into the main cache assuming content-address identity; the residual hazard is an environment-blind key (identical key ≠ identical runtime environment).

## Plan (SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L)

Decomposed into six children in test-first, dependency order. Every child is a
vertical slice (code + tests + docs) except the first, which is the deliberate
TDD slice that pins the environment-bound cache contract before any production
change.

| # | Child | Type | Delivers | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|----------|------------|
| 1 | Env-key cache regression tests: drift and equivalence (SA-0MWIH8Q7H005H3XG) | task | Failing-first tests: drift miss, equivalent-environment sharing, path-independence, provenance + cheapness/determinism (AC6a,b,d at the cache layer) | — |
| 2 | test_cache environment fingerprint and provenance (SA-0MWIH8RNJ006DU4D) | feature | `compute_environment_state()`, key folding, provenance metadata, fail-closed indeterminate environment (AC3, AC5 provenance half) | 1 |
| 3 | run_tests env-aware cache keys and gate provenance (SA-0MWIH8SOL008YZB9) | feature | Environment fingerprint computed in the measured checkout for gate/summary/typed runs; provenance in the result JSON (AC2) | 2 |
| 4 | pre-push: skip environment-drifted cache mirrors (SA-0MWIH8TT4000X0T2) | feature | Env-aware `mirror_suite_cache()`: drift-keyed entries skipped with a notice, equivalent entries mirrored (AC5 mirroring half) | 3 |
| 5 | finish: escalate post-push verification in canonical env (SA-0MWIH8V0R002YH77) | feature | Canonical-environment queries + forced escalation (`--scope changed --force` default, `--scope full --force` on broad/refactor/drift), documented degradation (AC1, AC4) | 3, 4 |
| 6 | Cross-consumer env-key equivalence and audit evidence notes (SA-0MWIH8W4200205V5) | task | Finish gate ↔ pre-push ↔ audit integration test; audit F3/F4 notes; docs consistency; full suite green (AC6b end-to-end, AC7) | 4, 5 |

### Sequencing

1 → 2 → 3 → (4, then 5) → 6. Child 3 unblocks both 4 and 5, but 5 is
sequenced after 4 so the post-push verification is built on top of
mirroring semantics that already refuse drifted entries. Child 6 is the final
validation/docs slice and must not start before both consumers are in place.

### Vertical slice phasing

Each implementation child cuts through cache layer → runner wiring → docs and
tests in one deliverable increment. There is no horizontal "all code, then all
tests" phase: the production change and the test that proves it land together,
and the only test-only slice (child 1) exists because test-first ordering was
required.

### Decisions and assumptions recorded at plan time

- **Escalation subject.** The forced run executes in the canonical (main)
  checkout, as the parent requires, but only when that checkout provably holds
  the pushed tree (pushed commit's tree SHA equals the checkout's tree and it
  is clean). Otherwise the verdict stays `missing` with a recovery recipe —
  never a green attributed to a tree the checkout does not hold. This follows
  the cache's own provenance contract and the parent's "explicit degradation,
  never a silent green" mitigation.
- **Changed-scope base after the push.** Post-push, `origin/dev` already
  contains the pushed commit, so the default changed-file base would select no
  files and fall back to the full suite. The escalation therefore passes
  `--target-branch <pushed>^`, keeping the targeted default genuinely
  targeted (AC4).
- **Node_modules equivalence.** `node_modules` resolution is keyed on the
  installed-state hash (`node_modules/.package-lock.json` content), never on a
  symlink's target path. A symlinked `node_modules` pointing at an identical
  install is therefore equivalent (audit F3/worktree reuse keeps working),
  while a missing/empty install is a distinct marker. This keeps the
  fingerprint path-independent and immune to npm churn that leaves installed
  state unchanged.
- **Legacy entries.** Entries without `environment_fingerprint` are a miss for
  environment-aware lookups (fail closed, never an environment-blind green).
  The 2 h cache TTL (5 min for red runs) bounds the transition; no migration
  is written.
- **"Broad" / "refactor" / "drift".** Broad = changed-scope selection cannot
  resolve a subset (the runner's documented full fallback); refactor = the
  finish refactor step altered files; drift = the worktree's environment
  descriptor differs from the canonical checkout's.
- **No producer questions were needed at plan time.** Q1 (c), Q2 (a) and
  Q3 (a) in the Appendix resolve the design; the choices above are
  implementation decisions inside those answers, recorded here rather than
  re-asked.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-15 — `plan` skill (session `herdr-1794785803-2397772-12622`):
  created six children (test-first), wired seven dependency edges, ran the six
  automated review stages and the AC coverage review (parent ACs 100 %
  covered). No existing children were modified or duplicated; duplicate-work
  search found no overlapping completed item.

# Audit timeout constants: single source of truth shared across audit/test skills

## Problem statement

AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT (90s), AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT (90s) and TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT (600s) are each independently defined and tuned in their owning skill, with only a comment tying AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT to AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT. Tuning one budget silently diverges from its documented twin, so the two host and queue budgets drift apart and the intended invariant (host wait stays inside the parent bash-tool ~120s execution timeout, queue admission stays inside it too) is only enforced by comments.

## Users

- **Agent operators** — when they tune timeout values via environment variables, they expect related timeouts to remain consistent.
- **Contributors** — when they need to adjust a timeout, they want a single place to change it and know the implications.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 - Shared timeout module**: a single source of truth for audit/test wait budgets lives in a shared module (e.g. `skill/shared/wait_budgets.py` or an extension of `process_semaphore.py`), consumed by both `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
2. **AC2 - No behavioural change**: default values are unchanged (AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT=90, AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=90, TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT=600) and env-var overrides still win; existing tests pass unchanged.
3. **AC3 - Drift impossible**: the documented 'host timeout matches queue timeout / stays inside parent bash-tool timeout' invariant is enforced by the shared definition, not by a comment.
4. **AC4 - Docs**: audit-skill reference and test-skill reference point at the shared module for wait-budget tuning.

## Impact

Audit and test timeout values are defined in one shared module, eliminating the risk of silent drift when tuning individual budgets.

## Constraints

- Keep wait budgets configurable via env vars only (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`); no config-file changes.
- Surgical change: audit/test concurrency semantics (priority queue, bounded wait, fail-fast on `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT=0`, cache-hit bypass) are unchanged.
- Full project test suite must pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/wait_budgets.py` — New shared module exporting timeout defaults, env-var names, and helper functions.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Import and use shared constants instead of local definitions.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Import and use shared constants instead of local definitions.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Update references to point at shared module.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — Update references to point at shared module.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — Update references.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — Update references.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — Update imports to use shared constants.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — Update imports to use shared constants.

## Related work

- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM (audit priority queue integration) — defined AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT
- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG (test skill shared concurrency primitive) — TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT
- SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE (right-size audit concurrency ceilings) — AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT default 90s
- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG (test skill shared concurrency primitive)
- SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE (right-size audit concurrency ceilings)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Test imports**: existing tests import `*_DEFAULT` and `*_ENV` directly from their owning modules. After consolidation, tests must import from the shared module. Mitigation: update all test imports.
- **Scope creep**: the refactor could accidentally touch unrelated parts. Mitigation: surgical edits only, target only timeout constant definitions.
- **Env-var override consistency**: all callers must continue to honour the same env var names. Mitigation: shared module exports env-var names as constants alongside defaults.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions — the work item provides sufficient detail to proceed.
