# Refactor skill: detect files > 1000 lines, evaluate refactor need, and file work items

## Problem statement

The refactor skill detects `god_class` and `long_method` purely through LLM
judgement and has **no deterministic file-size signal**, so files grow far past
a readable size unnoticed. The ContextHub repo sweep that produced
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (`downtime-worker.ts`, 8,205 lines) found **15 production
files over 1,000 lines** — `worklist.ts` 7,792, `database.ts` 3,684,
`index.ts` 2,784 and eleven more — none of which the skill had ever flagged.
File length is a cheap, objective, language-independent maintainability proxy
and belongs in the skill's default rule set, not in ad-hoc producer sweeps.

## Users

- **Producers/agents running `/skill:refactor`** want oversized files surfaced
  automatically instead of discovered by manual `wc -l` sweeps.
- **Maintainers** want a consistent 1,000-line ceiling applied across every
  project without re-deriving the rule each time.
- **Reviewers** want refactor work items to exist before a file becomes
  unmaintainable, with an explicit "is refactoring appropriate?" judgement
  recorded.

User stories:

- As a producer running a full-project refactor scan, I want every file over
  1,000 lines listed so that I can decide which to decompose.
- As an agent, I want a work item filed automatically when a large file
  genuinely warrants decomposition, so that the finding is not lost.

## Goal

Add a deterministic **file-length** smell to the refactor skill: any source file
over 1,000 lines is flagged, evaluated by the existing LLM smell-detection pass
for whether refactoring is appropriate, and — when appropriate — a Worklog work
item is created through the existing `workitem_creation` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A deterministic pre-LLM scan flags every tracked source file whose line count exceeds a configurable threshold (default 1,000), reporting path, line count and excess.
- The threshold is configurable via `.refactor.json` (`"file_length": {"enabled": true, "threshold": 1000}`) and disabled when set to `0`/`false`; the default applies with no config present.
- Over-threshold files are passed to the LLM evaluation step, which decides whether decomposition is appropriate and records a one-line rationale; files judged not to warrant decomposition are reported but create no work item.
- For appropriate files, exactly one Worklog work item is created (tags `Refactor`), idempotently — re-running the scan does not create a duplicate (existing REFACTOR-comment and `wl list --tags Refactor` dedup guards apply).
- Generated test files, vendored and generated paths are excluded from the threshold check, and the exclusion list is configurable.
- Unit tests cover: over/under threshold, config override/disable, LLM "not appropriate" suppression, dedup on re-run, and exclusion patterns.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` smell-type table and the `.refactor.json` example.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers running a full-project refactor scan now see every file over 1,000
lines surfaced automatically, so oversized modules get a tracked decomposition
decision before they become unmaintainable instead of being discovered in ad-hoc
sweeps.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing rule/config plumbing (`smell_detection.DEFAULT_RULES`,
  `scripts/config.py`, `workitem_creation.create_smell_work_item`) rather than
  adding a parallel mechanism.
- Deterministic and offline: the line-count scan must work with the LLM
  disabled (report-only) and must not require a network call.
- No behavioural change to existing smell types or their severities.
- The detection step must remain conservative: only flag genuine separability,
  not merely an inevitable size (e.g. a single-purpose generated constant
  module) — recorded as a rationale on the finding.

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/smell_detection.py` — `DEFAULT_RULES` lists 11 smell types,
  all of which are linter-detected (`ruff`/`eslint`) or LLM-detected. There is
  **no** deterministic line-count or file-length detector.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/config.py` — `RefactorConfig` dataclass wraps rule
  loading; supports `enabled`, `linter`, `llm`, `severity_mapping`,
  `smell_types`, `path_exclude`/`path_include`. No `file_length` section.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `refactor_pipeline` runs
  `detect_session_files` → `auto_fix_files` → `run_smell_detection` →
  `remediate_pre_existing`. `run_smell_detection` currently passes
  `llm_client=None`, so LLM detection is not wired here yet.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — `create_smell_work_item` carries the
  full dedup guards (REFACTOR comment, `Refactor-Finding-Key` exact identity,
  audit-twin suppression). File-length findings will flow through this
  unchanged path.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — smell-type table at ~line 242 and
  `.refactor.json` example at ~line 203 need the new type/config key.
- Tests live in `tests/test_refactor/` (e.g. `test_smell_detection.py`,
  `test_workitem_creation.py`), not `skill/refactor/tests/`.

## Desired change

- New `file_length` rule + deterministic detector feeding the existing smell
  pipeline; severity `medium` by default (high above ~2× threshold).
- LLM prompt extension: for `file_length` findings, answer "does this file
  have multiple separable concerns that warrant decomposition?" with a
  one-line rationale.
- Work-item title format consistent with existing generated titles, e.g.
  `Refactor: File Length in <path>` (the deterministic finding name) with the
  decomposition rationale recorded in the description.
- Report-only mode when LLM is disabled: print the over-threshold list, create
  no items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/smell_detection.py` — add `file_length` to `DEFAULT_RULES`
  smell types and a deterministic line-count detector.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/config.py` — default config entry and threshold
  plumbing in `RefactorConfig` (`file_length_config` / threshold property).
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — wire the detector into the scan
  (`run_smell_detection` / `refactor_pipeline`) and pass findings to the LLM
  evaluation.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — ensure `file_length` titles/
  descriptions and dedup behave correctly.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document the new smell type, config key and
  exclusion defaults.
- `tests/test_refactor/` — unit tests for the ACs (over/under threshold,
  config override/disable, LLM suppression, dedup, exclusions).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** 1,000 lines is the default ceiling; projects may override it
  per repo.
- **Assumption:** "evaluated for refactoring and if appropriate a work item
  should be created" is implemented as an LLM judgement gate, not an
  unconditional filing, so the scan does not flood backlogs with items for
  unavoidably large generated or data-heavy modules.
- **Assumption:** test files are in scope by default (large test suites also
  warrant decomposition); generated/vendored paths are excluded.
- **Risk:** a naive line count would flag minified/one-line bundles and data
  fixtures; mitigation is the exclusion list plus the LLM separability gate.
- **Risk:** LLM wiring is currently `llm_client=None` in the pipeline, so the
  evaluation gate needs a client to be supplied (or must degrade to
  report-only). Mitigation: keep determinism when no client is present.
- **Scope-creep risk:** other file-metric smells (comment ratio, max nesting
  depth) are out of scope — record as linked work items if surfaced, not here.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** (ContextHub) — the `downtime-worker.ts` god-class
  item whose manual sweep exposed the gap: 15 production files over 1,000
  lines, prompting the producer directive that every such file be evaluated
  and, if appropriate, given a refactor work item.
- ContextHub follow-up refactor items created from that sweep (`worklist.ts`,
  `database.ts`, `persistent-store.ts` ×2, `index.ts`, `fetcher.ts`,
  `dispatcher-anchor.ts`, `downtime-log.ts`, `sync.ts`, `github.ts`,
  `github-sync.ts`, `interview.ts`, `doctor.ts`, `init.ts`).
- **SA-0MQSFWF9Y000S5LO** (completed) — an unrelated refactor-skill cleanup
  item (`auto_fix_files()`); checked, not overlapping.
- **SA-0MQJK1594008U1O7** (completed) — unrelated audit-skill item; checked,
  not overlapping.

Automated find-related report:

- **SA-0MVVF468O009TAIF** (open) — Refactor skill: never inject marker blocks
  above a shebang or encoding line. Adjacent refactor-skill item; distinct
  concern (comment-injection placement) but linked as related work.
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** (completed) — Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness.
- **SA-0MQEEOK5N003ILYB** (completed) — lint finding in
  `tests/test_refactor/test_smell_detection.py` (F841).

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `wl search "file length smell refactor skill"` and
`wl search "god class file length line count smell"`. No completed item
overlaps this item's acceptance criteria — the only hit describing this work is
the item itself. **Duplicate check performed — no overlapping completed item
found.**

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

The seed context for this work item (producer directive + ContextHub sweep
evidence) was sufficient to draft the brief; no interview questions were
required. Recorded for auditability:

- Q: "Which threshold and config shape should drive the file-length check?" —
  Answer (producer directive, WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 sweep): default 1,000 lines,
  overridable per repo. Source: item description.
- Q: "Should an over-threshold file always get a work item?" — Answer
  (producer directive): no — evaluate whether refactoring is appropriate and
  only file when it is. Source: item description assumptions.
- Q: "Are test and generated files in scope?" — Answer: tests in scope by
  default; generated/vendored paths excluded and configurable. Source: item
  description assumptions.

> **Migrated from the `llm` worklog:** this item was originally filed there as `LP-0MVF4OPC1001RYX6` (deleted after migration on 2026-10-20). The `llm` repo remains the sweep target for its markers listed below; all skill-code changes live here in `SorraAgents`.

# Remove stale REFACTOR markers when their work item closes

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `REFACTOR-<id>` marker comments into source files to suppress duplicate work-item creation, but there is no removal path: once the referenced smell is fixed (or judged a false positive) and its work item closes, the marker persists and — because `has_existing_comment(file_path, smell_type)` matches on *smell type* only — permanently suppresses detection of that smell type in that file.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement pipeline's refactor step — they trust duplicate suppression to be accurate; a stale marker silently hides a real regression.
- **Developers reading source files** — stale markers are noise that misrepresents outstanding work.
- **Producers triaging the Refactor backlog** — a closed work item should leave no trace in the codebase.

Example user stories:

- "As an agent running the refactor step, when a marker's work item is already closed, I want the marker gone (or ignored) so I do not skip a smell that has regressed."
- "As a developer, when a refactor item is completed or judged a false positive, I want its comment removed from the file without touching surrounding code or line endings."
- "As a producer, I want a single command that reports every stale marker in the project and can clean them up."

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` provides `inject_refactor_comment()`, `has_existing_comment()`, `get_comment_style()` and `_build_comment_block()`; there is **no removal function**.
- Two slightly different regexes parse markers: `comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` (`REFACTOR-(\S+).*?smell:\s*(\S+)`, DOTALL) and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` (multi-line, expects a comment prefix before `smell:`).
- Markers are written in two shapes: line-prefixed (`# <!-- REFACTOR-…` … `# -->` for Python/YAML/shell, `// <!-- …` for JS/TS) and native block (`<!-- … -->` for Markdown/HTML). CSS-family files use `/* … */` with ` * ` prefixes.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` reads and writes text mode without `newline=""`, so injected files are normalised; removal must not repeat that mistake.
- `StatusLifecycle.show()` and `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()` already provide safe work-item lookup and prefix-to-sibling worklog-store resolution. Verified: a bare `wl show <foreign-prefix-id>` fails ("Work item not found"), so a sweep **must** inject `--worklog-dir` from the shared resolver.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` `remediate_pre_existing()` injects markers only for smells it just filed items for; the pipeline syncs the worklog first (`wl sync --if-idle`) and has no post-close hook.
- The canonical source of the skill is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/` (symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor`); its tests live in `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`, with `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (1251 lines) covering the current API.
- Stale markers confirmed at HEAD in the `llm` repo (work-item state checked 2026-10-20):

| File | Marker | Item stage |
|---|---|---|
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` | open / `intake_complete` — reported false positive |
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:8` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR` | completed / `done` |

- The same defect is visible in the `SorraAgents` repo itself: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (2 markers), `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` (3), `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (2), `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` — 4 of these reference `completed` items, the rest reference `open / idea` items.

## Desired change

1. **Removal API** in `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`: `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> dict` (or a small dataclass) that locates the whole marker block for that id — line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes — and deletes it, leaving the remainder of the file byte-identical (including CRLF/LF and the file's original trailing newline). Absent marker → `{"removed": False, "reason": "absent"}`; repeated runs are no-ops.
2. **Sweep module** (new `skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py`): discover markers in repo-tracked files (exclude `.worklog/`, `node_modules`, binaries), group by referenced work-item id to one `wl show` per distinct id (worklog dir resolved via `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`), classify each marker as `stale` (stage `in_review`/`done`/`completed` or status `completed`), `active` (any other resolved stage) or `unknown` (lookup failed), and return a structured report.
3. **Trigger** from the refactor pipeline: run the sweep after the `wl sync` and **before** smell detection, so `has_existing_comment` never observes a stale marker. Non-fatal on `wl` failure (log a warning, keep markers). Standalone CLI entry point (`--sweep-markers`, report-only by default, `--apply` to delete) and a skip flag (`--no-marker-sweep`).
4. **`has_existing_comment` correctness**: keep it a pure file predicate by default, but accept an optional `is_active` resolver/callback so a caller can exclude terminal items; the pipeline's sweep-before-detect ordering is what makes the default path correct. `unknown` markers keep suppressing (conservative) and are reported as warnings.
5. **False-positive path**: a marker whose item is still open but was judged a false positive must be removable explicitly (`--remove-marker <work-item-id>` or `remove_refactor_marker()` called directly), independent of item stage.
6. **Unit tests** in `tests/test_refactor/`: removal for `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes; block and line-prefix styles; CRLF preservation; absent-marker no-op; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file touching only the target block; classification of `in_review`/`done`/`completed`/`open`; `unknown` id kept and reported; dry-run performs no writes; cross-store id resolution.
7. **Sweep the existing stale markers** in `llm` (6 stale; the false positive needs an explicit decision) and in `SorraAgents` (4 stale), so `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` afterwards shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
8. **Documentation**: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (§ REFACTOR Comments + flags table + report keys), `docs/refactor.md` (§ 4 Work Item Creation, troubleshooting "Duplicate work items created", module reference), and module docstrings. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (ship pipeline owns it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- [ ] Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- [ ] A sweep reports every marker in the project with its referenced item's stage and a classification of `stale` / `active` / `unknown`; removal is triggered for markers whose work item is at a terminal stage (`in_review`, `done`, `completed`).
- [ ] Sweep work-item lookups resolve the correct worklog store via the shared resolver (a foreign-prefix id resolves; failure is non-fatal and keeps the marker as `unknown`).
- [ ] `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- [ ] An explicit false-positive removal path exists for markers whose work item is still open, with `--dry-run` making no writes.
- [ ] Running the sweep (apply mode) removes the 6 stale `llm` markers listed above and the 4 stale `SorraAgents` markers; a follow-up `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles; absent marker; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file; terminal vs non-terminal classification; unknown id; dry-run no-write.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/`; never edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/...` (the installer replaces it) and never hand-edit markers in `llm` outside an authorised implementation run.
- Standard library only — no new third-party dependencies.
- One `wl show` per distinct referenced work-item id (cached per run); the sweep must stay in the same sub-second-to-low-seconds envelope as the existing pipeline rather than spawning per marker.
- Sweep is read-only unless `--apply` (or the default pipeline policy) removes stale markers; `--dry-run` must never write.
- Never remove a marker for an item that is not terminal unless explicitly requested by id.
- Only scan git-tracked files in the repo root (skip `.worklog/`, worktrees, `node_modules`, binary files).
- Work-item ids may belong to sibling project stores; always route `wl` through the shared resolver, not the cwd default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — add `remove_refactor_marker()`, a single tolerant marker parser covering both existing regexes, `is_active` filter hook on `has_existing_comment()`, and `newline=""` IO.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py` (new) — marker discovery, per-id work-item lookup via `shared.status_lifecycle`, classification and report structure.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — sweep step after `wl sync` / before detection, `--sweep-markers`, `--apply`, `--remove-marker`, `--no-marker-sweep` flags, report keys.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reuse the unified marker pattern instead of its own `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker lifecycle and new flags.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/refactor.md` — § 4, troubleshooting, module reference.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — extend with removal tests.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_marker_sweep.py` (new) — sweep classification, dry-run, unknown ids, non-fatal wl failures.
- `llm`: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py`, `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — sweep targets only (no hand edits).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repository placement (assumption A1):** the skill's source of truth is `SorraAgents`, so the code change belongs here (this `SA-` item) and owns the `llm` marker sweep alongside the `SorraAgents` sweep; Q1 is resolved by this migration.
- **No close hook:** `wl` exposes no plugin/hook on close (only `wl plugins` for discovery), so "triggered when the item reaches a terminal stage" is implemented as a sweep at refactor-run time plus a standalone command — not an event. Assumption A2.
- **False-positive regression loop:** removing the marker for a closed false-positive item re-enables detection, so the next scan re-files the same item. Mitigation: false positives must be closed with a reason *and* either fixed or excluded via `.refactor.json`/per-file ignore; the sweep should report (not silently hide) this case. Scope-creep risk — an ignore-list mechanism is a separate work item.
- **Mixed answers to `unknown`:** unresolvable ids (deleted items, wrong store) could hide real work. Conservative default: keep + warn.
- **Formatting churn:** a naive implementation strips a leading blank line or rewrites CRLF files, producing whole-file diffs. Byte-preserving IO (`newline=""`, explicit trailing-newline handling) plus a CRLF fixture test is mandatory.
- **Regex divergence:** the two existing patterns disagree on block styles; unifying them is required or Markdown/CSS markers will be missed by the sweep.
- **Scope creep:** generalising to a lifecycle framework for all agent-injected comments is out of scope; record as a separate item if it surfaces.

## Open questions

1. **Repository and work-item placement** — ~~implement in `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor` under a new `SA-` item (this `LP-` item keeps the `llm` sweep and records the blocker), or keep everything under this `LP-` item and treat the SorraAgents edits as out-of-worktree?~~ **RESOLVED** by migration: this `SA-` item hosts the skill change; the `llm` marker list below stays the sweep target.
2. **Trigger surface** — sweep automatically inside the refactor pipeline (default) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers --apply`, or standalone-only (manual/cron)?
3. **False positives and unresolvable ids** — should `has_existing_comment` keep suppressing on `unknown` ids (conservative) while a manual `--remove-marker <id>` handles false positives, or should both be dropped automatically?

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which repository should host the skill change — `SorraAgents/skill/refactor` (canonical source, its own `SA-` item) or this `LP-` item in `llm`? (moot — item migrated to `SorraAgents` as `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`)" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor`; the skill's tests live in `SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`; `implement.py` creates worktrees from the cwd's `.worklog`, so an `LP-` item cannot legally host edits under `SorraAgents`. **Recommended:** new `SA-` item in `SorraAgents` for the skill change, `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` scoped to the `llm` marker sweep and recording the blocker.
- Q: "How should the terminal-stage trigger be implemented, given `wl` exposes no close hook?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `wl plugins` only lists plugins; no event/hook surface found; the refactor pipeline already runs at the end of implementation and syncs first. **Recommended:** sweep inside the refactor pipeline (after `wl sync`, before detection) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers` report/`--apply` CLI.
- Q: "Should markers referencing unresolvable work items, and false-positive markers whose item is still open, be removed automatically?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: all `llm` markers resolve today except none; `LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` is open at `intake_complete` while the marker is documented as a false positive. **Recommended:** keep `unknown` markers and warn; require an explicit `--remove-marker <id>` for open-item false positives.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE** – Refactor: Formatting in a test file of the (since-deleted) `proxy-usage-analysis` skill (open)
- **LP-0MQ5NI704006WINH** – Unit tests: cooldown behavior (completed)
- **LP-0MROYEVL3004Y04Z** – Manually fix remaining 5 non-auto-fixable lint errors (4 F401, 1 F811) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)

# Add an `--instructions` switch to the speak CLI for tone/style control

## Impact

Operators and pi agents can now request a delivery tone (e.g. excited, calm, whisper) on any cloned voice via `speak.sh --instructions "..."`, without changing the voice or breaking existing callers who omit the switch.

## Problem statement

The local CosyVoice 3 TTS server supports an optional `instructions` field on
`POST /v1/audio/speech` that routes to `inference_instruct2`, enabling
natural-language delivery control (excited, calm, warm, slow, whisper, etc.)
while preserving the cloned voice's timbre. That capability is delivered in
the `tts` project as **TTS-0MVGT2B2L003Y22X** (completed, merged to
`origin/dev`).

The `speak` CLI cannot use it:

- `skill/speak/scripts/speak.sh` accepts only `--stream`, `--voice` and
  `--help`; the JSON payload hardcodes `model`, `input` and `voice`.
- `speak.py` is a pure pass-through timing wrapper, so it inherits the gap.
- Consequently pi agents and the operator cannot ask for a different delivery
  for a given voice (e.g. an excited tone on the `sorra` clone).

Discovered while verifying the `sorra` voice and the tone-instruction API
(TTS-0MVDZIS0O0060SRF, `tts` project).

## Users

- **Operator** — wants `speak.sh --instructions "excited and energetic" ...`.
- **pi agents / `/skill:speak`** — pass a tone instruction per invocation.
- **Maintainers** — keep default behaviour byte-identical; the field must be
  additive.

### User stories

- As the **operator**, I want to add a delivery instruction to a speak call so
  the same cloned voice can sound excited, calm, warm, etc.
- As an **existing caller**, I want calls that omit the instruction to behave
  exactly as today (no `instructions` key in the payload).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New CLI switch**: `speak.sh --instructions <text>` adds
   `"instructions": "<text>"` to the `/v1/audio/speech` JSON payload in both
   save-to-file and `--stream` modes. Verification: unit test with the mock
   curl payload capture asserts the exact value.
2. **Omitted → unchanged**: when `--instructions` is not supplied (and
   `TTS_INSTRUCTIONS` unset), the payload contains **no** `instructions` key
   and every existing test passes unchanged. Verification: payload-capture
   test asserts key absence; existing suite green.
3. **Safe JSON encoding**: instruction text containing quotes, backslashes or
   newlines round-trips through the payload exactly as supplied (reuse the
   existing `python3 -c 'json.dumps'` approach). Verification: payload-capture
   test parses the JSON and compares strings.
4. **Blank treated as omitted**: `--instructions ""` or whitespace-only is
   ignored (no key sent), never sent as an empty string. Verification: test.
5. **Length guard**: instructions longer than 500 characters fail fast with a
   clear error and non-zero exit **before** any network call (the server
   enforces the same limit with HTTP 400). Verification: test asserts curl was
   not invoked.
6. **Precedence + env default**: explicit `--instructions` wins over
   `TTS_INSTRUCTIONS`, which acts as the default when the flag is absent —
   mirroring the existing `--voice`/`TTS_VOICE` design. Verification: tests for
   the precedence and env-only paths.
7. **Consistent argument parsing**: `--instructions=<text>` is rejected with
   the same actionable hint already used for `--voice=<name>`; a bare
   `--instructions` with a missing or next-option value errors out with usage.
   Verification: tests for both error paths.
8. **Help + docs**: `speak.sh --help` lists the new option and the
   `TTS_INSTRUCTIONS` env var; `skill/speak/SKILL.md` documents usage with a
   tone example and notes the server-side dependency (endpoints without the
   extension ignore or reject the field). Verification: help-output test and
   doc-content test (mirroring the existing `test_skill_doc_exists`).
9. **No regressions**: full SorraAgents test suite passes; the wrapper
   `speak.py` continues to forward arguments untouched (no code change
   expected) and its tests pass.

## Constraints

- **Canonical location**: the skill is versioned at `skill/speak/` in this
  repository (`~/.pi/agent/skills/speak` is a symlink). Edit here.
- **Server dependency**: `instructions` is a non-standard extension. The
  server must run a build that includes TTS-0MVGT2B2L003Y22X; older servers
  silently ignore the unknown field, so the CLI cannot verify that the
  instruction was applied. Document this.
- **No API changes to `speak.py`**: it must remain a pass-through.
- **Backwards compatibility**: default payload shape and behaviour are
  unchanged when no instruction is supplied.
- **Transport**: plain `curl` with a JSON body; no new runtime dependencies.

## Key Files

- `skill/speak/scripts/speak.sh` — add option parsing + payload field.
- `skill/speak/SKILL.md` — document the switch, env var and dependency.
- `tests/test_speak.py` — payload-capture tests (the mock curl already records
  the `-d` body to `payload.json`).

## Related work

- **TTS-0MVGT2B2L003Y22X** (`tts` project) — server-side `instructions` field
  routed to `inference_instruct2`; completed and merged to `origin/dev`.
  This item consumes that contract.
- **TTS-0MVDZIS0O0060SRF** (`tts` project) — `sorra` voice clone; discovered
  from this verification session.
- Cross-project dependency edges cannot be recorded in this Worklog store;
  recorded here instead.

## Risks & assumptions

# Intake Brief: Audit skill — mandatory detached launch procedure

## Problem statement

When an agent runs `audit_runner.py issue <id>` in the foreground (e.g. via a tool command with a timeout), the runner can be killed mid-audit — for example when the agent's tool timeout (600 s) fires during Phase 1 or Phase 2 LLM calls which each have 600–1800 s budgets. A hard kill (SIGKILL, tool timeout) skips the runner's abort-recovery handlers, leaving the work item stranded in `in_progress` and requiring manual state restoration before a relaunch.

## Users

- **Agents (Map / Ralph / herdr workers)** that invoke the audit runner — they need a deterministic, safe launch→monitor workflow that prevents state corruption.
- **Operators** who oversee long audits and need a documented recovery path when something goes wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The audit skill's `Monitored Run Execution` section includes a **mandatory launch procedure** that explicitly states: "ALWAYS launch detached; NEVER run `audit_runner.py issue` in the foreground."
2. A short **recovery procedure** is documented for the case where the agent is already mid-audit and must restore state before relaunching (restore pre-audit status/stage, remove abort-state file, relaunch detached).
3. The `Monitored Run Execution` summary is cross-linked to or mirrors the shared background-job etiquette (`skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md`) so agents see the same guidance in both places.

## Impact

Agents can run audits without fear of corrupting work-item state, eliminating a class of manual recovery steps.

## Constraints

- Documentation-only change; no code modifications required.
- Must not contradict or duplicate the existing background-job etiquette document.
- The recovery procedure should be concise and copy-paste-ready.

## Existing state

The `Monitored Run Execution` section of `skill/audit/SKILL.md` already documents the launch→monitor→abort pattern with a bullet-point summary, but lacks an explicit mandatory directive and the recovery procedure. The background-job etiquette document exists at `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` and is cross-referenced from the audit skill.

## Desired change

Enhance the `Monitored Run Execution` section with:
1. A bold, explicit mandate: "ALWAYS launch detached; NEVER run in the foreground."
2. A concrete example of the detached launch procedure (using `nohup`, unique log path, PID capture).
3. A recovery procedure section for the interrupted-audit case.
4. A clear cross-reference to the background-job etiquette document.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Monitored Run Execution section (add mandatory directive + recovery procedure)

## Related work

- **SA-0MSL51XSF0086KM5** — "Add timeout, output capture, and progress monitoring to audit skill" (completed, high priority) — this item laid the groundwork for the monitored-run workflow documented in SKILL.md.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** There may be other skills that need similar guidance. Those should be tracked as separate work items, not added here.
- **Assumption:** The existing background-job etiquette document is authoritative; the audit skill should cross-reference rather than duplicate its content.
- **Risk:** If the recovery procedure is too detailed, it bloats the SKILL.md. Keep it concise.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions raised — the work item description was sufficiently detailed.

# Add a session-time-analysis skill ("where does Pi time go") and weave it into agent-log-review

## Objective

Formalise the ad-hoc 2026-10-21 AI_Hell time-attribution methodology (throwaway
scripts in `/tmp/pi_time/`) into a maintained, globally-installed skill under
`skill/` that deterministically answers "where does Pi time go" for any project,
and share its session parser + signal extractors with agent-log-review so its
reports gain a "Where the time went" section — without weakening privacy.

## Problem statement

Operators cannot see where agent-hours go without writing throwaway scripts:
the 2026-10-21 analysis of 25 AI_Hell sessions showed ~8.7 h of ~11.8 h active
wall-clock blocked in `wait_for_job.py` (37 waits, avg ~15 min), a 2.8 h hung
`evaluate.mjs` (mis-bucketed under "git" by a naive classifier), ~1.4 h of test
runs, and >96% of ~123 M tokens as cache reads. That methodology lives in
`/tmp/pi_time/` (lost on reboot); this item makes it a repeatable skill and
weaves its metric extractors into agent-log-review so the diagnosis becomes a
standard, deterministic report section.

## Users

- **Agent operator / producer** — runs one command per project and gets a
  deterministic time-attribution report (window, session counts by kind,
  active vs blocked vs LLM vs tool, per-session and per-theme) plus waste
  flags (long blocked waits, hung commands, error-heavy tools, retry loops).
- **Maintainer of agent-log-review** — reuses the shared v3 JSONL parser and
  signal extractors so time analysis is consistent with pattern analysis.
- **Automation users** — consume `--json` output and `--parent-id` worklog
  integration for dashboards and automated reporting.

### Example user stories

- As an operator I want to run one command per project and get a deterministic
  time-attribution report (window, session count by kind, active vs blocked vs
  LLM vs tool, per-session and per-theme) so I can see where agent-hours go
  without writing throwaway scripts.
- As an operator I want the same skill to flag waste (long blocked waits, hung
  commands, error-heavy tools, retry loops) so I can act on the biggest time
  sinks.
- As a maintainer of agent-log-review I want the v3 JSONL session parser and
  signal extractors shared and reused so time analysis is consistent with
  pattern analysis, and reports gain a "Where the time went" section.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new skill under `skill/session-time-analysis/` with `SKILL.md` plus
   `scripts/` and `tests/` following agent-log-review's structure; a
   deterministic CLI with every flag documented in `--help`.
2. Report covers: window, session count by kind (e.g. audit vs interactive),
   union **and** naive-sum active wall time with the double-counting
   distinction explained (2026-10-21: sum-LLM 10.0 h vs union 6.5 h), LLM vs
   tool split, per-tool time/calls/errors, per-model time, token & cache
   economics (input/output/cacheRead, cache-hit %), blocking classification
   totals, and top-10 longest bash commands with hang flagging.
3. Blocking classification attributes by primary binary / first token
   (not substring match — the 2026-10-21 2.8 h `evaluate.mjs` must not land
   under "git"), flags per-command-family duration outliers as hung, and
   surfaces the top-N longest commands.
4. Union (de-duplicated across concurrent sessions) and naive-sum figures are
   both reported and explained; timezone-correct day windowing, sessions
   spanning midnight, and malformed lines degrade without crashing.
5. agent-log-review reports gain the time-attribution section sourced from the
   shared extractors, and its classification prompt receives time/waste
   signals; privacy/redaction guarantees are preserved (raw logs never sent to
   a model, secrets redacted).
6. Automated tests cover parser/metrics edge cases (malformed lines,
   midnight-spanning sessions, millisecond vs ISO timestamps, empty dir,
   missing usage degrade, no crash) and a golden fixture from the 2026-10-21
   AI_Hell sessions asserting the headline figures (~8.7 h blocked-wait of
   ~11.8 h active; hung tune run 2.78 h; test runs ~1.4 h). Tests run under
   the repo's test policy (test skill).
7. `SKILL.md` documents usage, metric definitions, limitations (provider
   durationMs may skew under slot contention; host-load correlation initially
   out of scope), and the integration contract with agent-log-review.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g.
   `docs/dev/session-time-analysis-skill-reference.md`).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators can run one deterministic command per project to see exactly where
agent-hours go (blocked waits, hung commands, tokens) and get the same
diagnosis automatically inside agent-log-review reports — no throwaway scripts.

## Constraints

- Skills live in `skill/<name>/` with `scripts/` and `tests/`; global install
  via `scripts/install_pi.sh` (symlink of `skill/` → `~/.pi/agent/skills`);
  changes affect every project, so they are tracked here, built, tested, and
  pushed to `dev` before re-install.
- **Privacy:** raw session logs are never sent to a model and never persisted;
  secrets remain redacted (mirror agent-log-review's guarantees).
- Deterministic output: same input directory + flags ⇒ byte-identical report
  (stable ordering, no randomness).
- UK English throughout; follow existing skill conventions and the shared
  test-writing guidelines (avoid self-referential simulations — the golden
  fixture reproduces 2026-10-21 *metrics*, it does not reimplement game logic).
- v3 JSONL session format assumed stable (fields: `session`, `model_change`,
  `thinking_level_change`, `message` with content parts, `toolResult`,
  `usage`, `durationMs`, ISO and/or epoch-ms timestamps).
- Do not depend on the `/tmp/pi_time/` throwaway scripts long-term (gone on
  reboot); the SKILL.md metric definitions are the source of truth.

## Existing state

- Throwaway analysis scripts `/tmp/pi_time/{analyse,deep,final,theme,content}.py`
  (currently deleted; do not depend on them — reference the recorded metrics in
  this item's description instead).
- Session logs at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` (v3 format);
  the 2026-10-21 AI_Hell sample dataset still exists (41 files) and is the
  golden-fixture source.
- agent-log-review skill exists: `skill/agent-log-review/` (SKILL.md,
  `scripts/agent_log_review.py` with `parse_session`/`read_sessions`/session
  dir resolution, `tests/`); epic SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC.
- Related completed parser work: SA-0MV6U4PW4007R7FE (v3 JSONL parser),
  SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY (one-off ste100 `analyze_sessions.py`).
- 2026-11-13 re-evaluation of 36 AI_Hell implement-skill sessions reproduced
  the pattern (668 min summed vs 388 min wall-clock; 37% in wait_for_job;
  88–93% of long-session time inside bash waits) — filed as epic
  SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1; this skill should reproduce those metrics
  deterministically.

## Desired change

Create `skill/session-time-analysis/` (SKILL.md + `scripts/` + `tests/`) with a
deterministic CLI (`--json`, `--output-file`, `--cwd`/`--session-root`,
`--max-sessions`, optional `--parent-id` worklog integration mirroring
agent-log-review's idempotent comments). Factor the v3 session parser and
signal extraction into shared modules consumed by both this skill and
agent-log-review; extend agent-log-review's distilled signals with
time/blocking/waste features, add the time-attribution report section, and add
a time-waste category to its classification prompt — preserving its privacy
guarantees.

Deliberate improvements over the throwaway scripts: union (de-duplicated) vs
naive-sum metrics; primary-binary/first-token blocking attribution with
duration-outlier hang flagging; per-command-family outlier detection; surfaced
top-N longest commands; timezone-correct day windowing; malformed-line
degradation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/session-time-analysis/SKILL.md` — skill definition, usage, metric definitions, limitations, integration contract
- `skill/session-time-analysis/scripts/session_time_analysis.py` — deterministic CLI + report renderer (Markdown/JSON)
- `skill/session-time-analysis/scripts/__init__.py` — package marker (mirror agent-log-review)
- `skill/session-time-analysis/tests/test_session_time_analysis.py` — parser/metrics edge cases
- `skill/session-time-analysis/tests/test_golden_2026_10_21.py` — golden fixture on the AI_Hell sample dataset (or a checked-in fixture snapshot)
- `skill/session-time-analysis/tests/conftest.py` — fixtures (mirror agent-log-review)
- Shared extraction module(s) consumed by both skills — e.g. `skill/shared/session_logs.py` + `skill/shared/session_time_metrics.py` (or a `session_time_analysis/` shared package), to be confirmed at plan time
- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — modified to use the shared extractors and emit the time-attribution section + time-waste signals
- `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md` — updated for the new section/signals
- `docs/dev/session-time-analysis-skill-reference.md` — skill reference docs
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — no change needed (installs `skill/` wholesale); verify

## Related work

- **SA-0MUEKTJRD0010CGC** — Agent log review skill: analyse session logs for repeated confusion patterns (epic; the skill this item integrates with).
- **SA-0MV6U4PW4007R7FE** — Agent log review: session log parser (v3 JSONL format) (completed; parser this item shares/extends).
- **SA-0MU9VSL250092LTY** — Build analysis script for ste100-24h experiment (completed; one-off analysis script, partial overlap on token/duration metrics).
- **SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD** — 24h experiment: measure session length & token use (open; related measurement context).
- **SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1** — Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (in-progress epic; consumed a 2026-11-13 session-time-style measurement — this skill should reproduce those metrics).
- **SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E** — Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out (blocked; measurement methodology overlap).
- **SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E** — Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts (completed; wait_for_job is the dominant blocked time sink this skill measures).

## Risks & assumptions

**Assumptions**
- v3 session log format is stable enough for parsing (fields as in the current
  files); `durationMs` reflects per-call LLM time subject to provider/slot
  variance.
- Default window is the most recent day (local timezone) for which sessions
  exist, overridable via CLI window flags; exact default confirmed at plan
  time (assumption documented here because the seed context did not pin it).
- The 2026-10-21 AI_Hell sessions remain readable at their current path for
  the golden fixture (41 files verified present); if `--session-root` is
  unavailable at test time, snapshot a redacted fixture into `tests/`.
- Shared extraction modules live under `skill/shared/` (or a
  `skill/session-time-analysis/` importable package) — exact location
  confirmed at plan time; agent-log-review's existing parser is factored out
  without behaviour change.

**Risks & mitigations**
- **Provider durationMs skew** — LLM `durationMs` may under/over-state under
  slot contention; report it as approximate and document the limitation (AC7).
- **Misclassification regression** — naive substring blocking attribution
  mis-bucketed the 2026-10-21 hung node run under "git"; AC3 mandates
  primary-binary/first-token attribution plus a regression test.
- **Privacy regression** — adding time/waste signals to agent-log-review must
  not leak raw log content; AC5 pins the redaction/no-raw-log guarantees and
  tests cover the classification prompt input.
- **Golden fixture drift** — if session files change/rotate, the fixture
  becomes stale; mitigate with a checked-in redacted snapshot plus the metric
  assertions (not byte-for-byte log equality).
- **Scope creep** — host-load correlation, live monitoring, and automated
  remediation are out of scope; record any such opportunities as linked work
  items, not additions here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required — the seed context (description with
user stories, design points, six acceptance criteria, context & references,
and a sample dataset with headline figures) suffices to draft a clear brief.
Open items recorded as assumptions above:
- Q: "Default analysis window when no window flags are supplied?" — Answer
  (agent assumption, needs plan-time confirmation): most recent day (local
  timezone) with session data, overridable via CLI flags. Research: the
  2026-10-21 analysis windowed by day (00:52–18:54 local); agent-log-review
  bounds by most-recent-20-sessions, so a "most recent day" default is
  consistent with both. Source: seed description (day-windowing) + sample
  dataset.
- Q: "Where do the shared parser/extractor modules live?" — Answer (agent
  assumption, needs plan-time confirmation): `skill/shared/` or a package
  importable by both skills; agent-log-review's existing parser factored out
  without behaviour change. Research: `skill/shared/` already hosts
  cross-skill helpers (status_lifecycle.py, wait_for_job.py, tree_coverage.py,
  process_semaphore.py); agent_log_review.py currently embeds
  `parse_session`/`read_sessions`. Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Is the golden fixture checked into tests/ or read live?" — Answer
  (agent assumption, needs plan-time confirmation): prefer a redacted checked-in
  snapshot so tests are hermetic; the live 2026-10-21 AI_Hell files are the
  source for producing it. Research: 41 files verified present under
  `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell--/2026-10-21*`.
  Source: filesystem inspection.

data.description:
# Intake Brief (v2) — Echo implement.py's live progress into the Pi client

## Problem statement

When an agent runs `implement.py finish` as a background job and waits on it
with `wait_for_job.py`, the operator in the Pi TUI sees **no feedback about
what the job is doing** for the entire wait — only the final elapsed marker
afterwards. Two distinct defects combine to cause this:

1. **`implement.py` is silently dark during the phases that take the time.**
   `run_build` (npm run build), `run_tests` (the full changed-scope suite),
   and `git_push_to_dev` all run their subprocesses fully captured
   (`capture_output=True` / `Popen(..., stdout=PIPE).communicate()`), so
   nothing is written to the job log while build/tests/push are actually
   running. A 2m36s (or 40-minute) wait sees only a few `LOG.info` phase
   lines — there is nothing for any watcher (TUI or log) to show.
2. **The waiter's relay loses bursty output.** Even when the job *does* write
   output, `JobOutputTail.new_lines()` keeps only the last `--tail-lines`
   (default 10) lines of each poll window and silently drops the earlier
   lines; a poll window that catches 200 build lines shows only 10.
3. **Operators accidentally defeat the streaming that does exist.** Piping the
   wait through `tail -N`/`grep`/`head` buffers everything until EOF — the Pi
   TUI then receives *zero* partial output (it CAN stream: the bash tool emits
   `tool_execution_update` with partial results, verified in
   `pi-coding-agent/dist/core/tools/bash.js`).

## Users

- **Operators / producers** watching an interactive `pi` TUI while the agent
  waits on `implement.py finish` (also audit, ship, epics).
  - *User story:* "As an operator watching a 20-minute `finish`, I want to see
    what the build, tests, and push are printing *as they run*, so I can tell
    whether the job is progressing or silently hung."
- **Agents** running the wait — they need a low-context-cost way to keep the
  waiter's own chattiness bounded without disabling the job-output stream.

## Root cause (verified in source)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: every subprocess is captured —
  `run_cmd(capture=…)` (line ~366), `subprocess.run(capture_output=True)`
  (~672, ~1835, ~4805, ~5431) and `Popen(…).communicate()` for the push
  (~1506–1515). The `logging.basicConfig` (line ~6063) writes `LOG.info`
  phase lines to stderr (→ the job log via `2>&1`), so the log holds phase
  headers but no live payload.
- `skill/test_cache.py::run_cached` → `_default_runner` (line ~405):
  `subprocess.run(shlex.split(command), …)` with stdout/stderr captured.
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py::JobOutputTail.new_lines`: returns
  `lines[-self.tail_lines:]` — silent drop of anything above the cap.
- Pi's bash tool *does* stream partial output (verified in the installed pi
  bundle); nothing in the tool chain prevents a live echo once the job
  actually emits output and the wait is not piped.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **implement.py streams live phase output.** Build, test, and push steps
   relay their subprocess output to implement.py's own stdout/stderr **as it
   is produced** (a tee-style runner: read child stdout incrementally, forward
   each line with flush, still capture the full text for the step report and
   the `--json` contract). Phase transitions are printed as flush banners
   (e.g. `→ Running build (npm run build)…`, `→ Running tests (changed
   scope)…`, `→ Pushing to dev…`), so the log has a continuous, honest
   heartbeat even when a child is quiet.
2. **Test steps stream through the cache runner.** The streamed output path is
   wired through `test_cache.run_cached`'s runner seam (implement.py's
   changed-scope gate uses it), so the finish gate's *real* suite output is
   what appears live — not just the wrapper's banners.
3. **No silent drops in the waiter relay.** `JobOutputTail.new_lines()` no
   longer silently discards lines above `--tail-lines`; it either emits **all**
   new lines or emits an explicit omission marker
   (`… N lines omitted; raise --tail-lines or poll faster`). Default
   behaviour must be lossless for typical poll windows.
4. **Never pipe the waiter.** `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` and
   the `wait_for_job.py` module docstring state explicitly that the waiter's
   output must not be piped through `tail`/`head`/`grep` (it buffers and kills
   live UI streaming); the supported alternatives for bounding context
   (`--tail-lines`, `--interval`) are documented.
5. **Skills carry the rule.** The `implement` skill's `wait_for_job.py`
   example shows the rule at the point of use; remaining skills
   (`audit`/`ship`/`test`/`plan`) reference it.
6. **Behavioural tests.** Unit tests cover: streaming runner forwards child
   lines with flush and still captures; omission marker appears on overflow;
   a single liveness line per wait poll (no duplicate `progress:`+`heartbeat:`
   pair); existing timeout/completion/interrupt and `--json` behaviour
   unchanged.
7. **Docs-lint test.** A test asserts no skill doc shows a recommended
   `wait_for_job.py` invocation piped through `tail`/`grep`/`head`, and that
   the anti-pattern rule exists in the shared doc.
8. **Docs updated.** All related documentation reflects the change (code
   comments, docstrings, shared etiquette doc, skill docs).
9. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility.** `wait_for_job.py` CLI surface and exit codes
  (0/1/2/130) unchanged; `--json` output shape machine-parseable.
- **implement.py CLI contract preserved.** Streamed output is additive
  (stdout/stderr); the `--json` finish report format must not change.
- **No buffering regressions.** Every emitted line flushes; the helper stays
  usable when stdout *is* a pipe (pi's bash tool always pipes stdout — that is
  fine; only an intermediate buffering command breaks streaming).
- **Driven children run `--no-extensions`.** Do not propose a pi extension or
  custom tool as the fix; the repair lives in `implement.py`, `wait_for_job.py`,
  and the skill/doc guidance.
- **Silent degradation preserved** when `HERDR_*` env vars are absent.
- **No ad-hoc full-suite test runs during implementation** (slot contention /
  test-execution policy); changed-scope gate only.

## Existing state

- `wait_for_job.py` already flushes each line, tails the job's log
  incrementally, reports herdr sidebar state and process vitals
  (SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK + SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA).
- `implement.py` logs phase headers but captures all subprocess output;
  nothing streams during build/tests/push.
- `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py` gives the established
  docs-lint pattern.

## Desired change

A finish run whose build/test/push output is **visible line-by-line** in the
Pi TUI (streamed by implement.py → log → waiter → bash-tool partial updates),
with an enforcement layer (docs rule + lint test) so agents do not pipe the
waiter away.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — tee-style live runner for
  build/tests/push; flush phase banners; wire through `run_build`,
  `run_tests`/`run_cached`, `git_push_to_dev`.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` test seam / `skill/test_cache.py`
  runner — streaming runner passed to `run_cached(runner=…)`.
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` — lossless (or explicit-omission) tail;
  single liveness line per poll; anti-pattern docstring.
- `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` — "Never pipe the waiter"
  subsection.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (+ `audit`/`ship`/`test`/`plan`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`) — rule at the point of use.
- `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py` — docs-lint assertion.
- New behavioural tests (streaming runner, tail omission, liveness line).

## Related work

- **SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA** — *User-visible progress feedback in the Pi agent
  interface during long-running waits (wait_for_job)* (completed) — delivered
  the waiter-side streaming (tail, vitals, notification). This item fixes the
  producer side (`implement.py` silence) and the relay's silent drops.
- **SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK** — helper contract preserved by AC6.
- **SA-0MVDP5JTK009HWOT** — *Roll out background-job etiquette* — file list
  extended by AC5/AC7.
- **SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E** — *Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts* —
  wiring table: `implement.py` marked "not appropriate" for *waiting* on a
  background job (unchanged — this item makes implement.py a *producer* of
  streamable output, not a waiter).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (verified in pi source):** the interactive TUI updates its
  pending-tool box on `tool_execution_update`, so streamed output is genuinely
  visible. If a future pi release removes streaming, this item's guidance is
  harmless but the visible benefit disappears.
- **Risk — streaming stdout in implement.py could interleave with `--json`
  report output.** Mitigation: stream to stderr (matching the existing
  "timing goes to stderr" convention, SA-0MT319YGQ002E801) so `--json`
  stdout stays clean. Note: the job log captures both via `2>&1`.
- **Risk — performance.** Tee-streaming adds per-line reads; acceptable for
  build/test/push cadence; keep line-buffered reads, not byte-at-a-time.
- **Risk — test tooling divergence.** `run_tests` delegates to
  `test.scripts.run_tests` / `test_cache.run_cached`; the runner seam must be
  exercised without bypassing the cache or the slot guard.
- **Scope-creep:** a pi-extension `wait_job` tool that renders progress is
  deliberately out of scope (driven children run `--no-extensions`).
- **Enforcement is by docs-lint, not runtime**; a determined agent can still
  pipe. Acceptable, bounded risk.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the missing feedback because pi does not stream bash output, or
  because of how the command was invoked?
  — **Answer (Map):** The invocation (`… | tail -25`) breaks streaming, but it
  is not the whole story. Pi's bash tool emits partial output via
  `onUpdate` → `tool_execution_update` (`dist/core/tools/bash.js`), and
  `wait_for_job.py` flushes each line — so *any* job output would stream. The
  larger cause is that `implement.py` writes almost nothing during build/tests
  (all subprocess output captured).

- **Q:** (v1) So deduplicating the waiter's heartbeat lines and telling agents
  not to pipe would fix the complaint?
  — **Answer (operator correction):** No — that only relays implement.py's
  sparse phase headers. The build/test/push *output* never reaches the log at
  all. v2 re-scopes to make implement.py produce live, streamed output
  (AC1–AC2) plus fix the relay's silent drops (AC3) plus the never-pipe rule
  (AC4–AC5). Verified: all six subprocess sites in implement.py capture
  output; `run_cached`/`_default_runner` capture too.

- **Q:** Should the streamed output go to stdout or stderr?
  — **Answer (Map):** stderr, matching the existing "timing to stderr"
  convention (`_emit_timing`, SA-0MT319YGQ002E801) so `--json` stdout stays
  clean. The nohup invocation captures both (`> log 2>&1`), so the log and
  therefore the waiter/tail see it either way.

- **Q:** Is there any live feedback *today*, before this item lands?
  — **Answer (Map):** Yes, partial: (a) the waiter's own heartbeat lines
  (`progress:`/`heartbeat:` with `state=/cpu=/children=` vitals) stream if the
  wait is unpiped; (b) herdr sidebar `working`/`blocked` when
  `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`+`HERDR_PANE_ID` are exported; (c) `WAIT_NOTIFY=1` →
  `notify-send` on completion. None of these show what implement.py is doing —
  the new capability is a teed child-output stream.
data.title: Echo implement.py's live build/test/push output into the Pi client (stream, don't pipe)

## Goal

Changed-scope test selection (map_changed_to_tests in run_tests.py) maps skill/<skill>/scripts/<module>.py changes to zero tests, because the dotted module name is derived with the literal 'skill/' prefix ('skill.code_review.scripts.linter_runner') while tests import 'code_review.scripts.linter_runner'.

## Evidence

In the SA-0MSTMAPL40019JX5 worktree:

```python
rt.map_changed_to_tests(root, {'skill/code_review/scripts/create_quality_epics.py'})  # -> []
rt.map_changed_to_tests(root, {'skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py'})         # -> []
```

Only the changed test files themselves were selected; tests/test_quality_epic_creation.py, tests/test_code_quality_*.py, tests/test_audit_code_quality.py and skill/audit/tests/* were all skipped despite importing the changed modules.

## Impact

A skill script edit now runs every affected test suite during the changed-scope gate, so regressions surface in seconds instead of waiting for the pre-push full-suite run.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Changing skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py selects tests/test_quality_epic_creation.py, tests/test_code_quality_*.py and tests/test_linter_runner_*.py via import-graph expansion.
2. A unit test in the test-skill suite pins resolution for skill/<name>/scripts/<module>.py -> tests importing that package.
3. Existing full/group selection behaviour is unchanged.

Discovered from: SA-0MSTMAPL40019JX5

## Implementation sketch

Two complementary gaps in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`:

1. **Module aliasing.** `_path_to_module()` derives `skill.code_review.scripts.linter_runner` for `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py`, but the suite puts `skill/` on `sys.path` (`tests/conftest.py`), so tests import `code_review.scripts.linter_runner`. Register every module in the import graph under all trailing dotted suffixes (full name, then each parent-qualified tail down to the basename) and add those aliases to `changed_targets` — the general form of the existing `src/`-layout basename aliasing. Over-matching is acceptable (extra tests run, never fewer).
2. **`from package import name`.** `_ast_imports()` records only `node.module` for an `ImportFrom`, so `from code_review.scripts import linter_runner` registers `code_review.scripts` but not the submodule. Also record `f"{module}.{alias.name}"` for each imported name so submodule imports join the graph (the dominant import style in this repository's tests).

**Test-first:** add a regression test to `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` (class `TestMapChangedToTests`) building a tmp repo laid out as `skill/<name>/scripts/<module>.py` plus `tests/test_things.py` that imports `from <name>.scripts import <module>`, with a transitive-import case; assert `map_changed_to_tests()` selects both. Then change the mapper.

## Risks and assumptions

- Suffix aliasing can over-match modules with a shared dotted tail (e.g. `scripts.foo`). This only adds tests, never removes them, so the fast-feedback gate stays sound.
- AC1's `tests/test_code_quality_*.py` wildcard is read as "every code-quality test that transitively imports `linter_runner`" (auto_fix, scoping, severity). `tests/test_code_quality_detection.py` imports only `code_review.scripts.detection`, which does not import `linter_runner`, so the fix does not select it — see the OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix comment.
data.title: run_tests: changed-scope selection misses skill/<skill>/scripts modules

# implement.py finish reports status changes that the main worklog store does not show

> **Provenance:** transferred from `OSL-0MVFHAT31007ZILJ` (ContentCreator) per operator decision — this SA item carries the full brief; the OSL item is closed as transferred. The fix belongs here because the defect is in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and shared `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`, which live in this repo.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` prints and logs a `completed`/`in_review` transition, but
the work item in the main checkout's worklog store can still read `open` /
`intake_complete` afterwards, so a successful finish can leave an item orphaned
in the queue while the tool claims it is `in_review`.

## Users

- **AI agent driving `/skill:implement`** — needs the post-`finish` state to be
  trustworthy so the next `wl next` does not re-pick a finished item.
  Story: *As an implementing agent, when finish reports `in_review`, a
  subsequent `wl show` from the main checkout must report
  `status=completed, stage=in_review`, so I do not rework a finished item.*
- **Producer/operator auditing the queue** — needs the store to reflect reality.
  Story: *As the producer, I need the queue to show finished items as
  `in_review` without manual repair, so audit does not report phantom open
  work.*
- **Maintainer of the implement skill** — needs the write path to be provable.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test that pins which store
  finish writes to, so future worklog-resolution changes cannot silently
  regress it.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Reproduce deterministically.** On a scratch work item, run the finish
      sequence (claim → commit → push stub → status transition) from a
      worktree, then read the item from the main checkout; capture, per `wl`
      call, the store (`--worklog-dir`) it targeted. Reproduction is recorded
      in the SA item as a comment with the command transcript.
- [ ] **Prove and fix the target store.** Establish which store each status
      write in `finish` targets (the `StatusLifecycle.__exit__`
      `completed`/`in_review` write in particular) and make the transition
      deterministically target the **main checkout** store — resolved from the
      main checkout root (`repo_root`, i.e. the value
      `_resolve_main_repo_root(worktree_path, state)` derives, not the raw
      `state.repo_root` and not cwd) — for the whole finish run.
- [ ] **Unit regression test.** Test that worklog resolution returns the main
      checkout's `.worklog` when cwd is `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>`
      (uninitialised worktree store) and that `finish` passes that explicit
      path to every `wl` status/comment call it makes (injected fake runner,
      no real git).
- [ ] **Integration regression test.** A hermetic test that creates a temp git
      repo plus worklog store, runs the finish status transition from a
      worktree, and asserts the **main store** reads `completed`/`in_review`
      afterwards (no network, stubbed push).
- [ ] **Document the finding** — write ordering (the status transition happens
      at `StatusLifecycle.__exit__`, *after* push and worktree removal) and the
      confirmed root cause — in the implement skill reference
      (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`) and, if the resolution rule changes,
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- [ ] **File the linked pre-push sync gap** as a separate `discovered-from`
      item: a push from a worktree cwd makes the pre-push hook's
      `wl sync --git-branch refs/worklog/data` fail (`wl` reports
      "not initialized"), so a worktree push never publishes worklog data.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments/docstrings in `implement.py` and `status_lifecycle.py`,
      `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, README
      (only where it documents finish status behaviour) and any relevant wiki
      or docs-site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix lands in **SorraAgents** (`skill/` is agent infrastructure); do not edit
  the ContentCreator project-local `.pi/` or any vendored copy. The OSL item is
  tracking only and closes as transferred.
- `StatusLifecycle` and `resolve_worklog_flags` are shared by every skill —
  keep the resolution change narrow; existing tests in
  `skill/shared/tests/test_status_lifecycle.py` and `skill/implement/tests/`
  must keep passing without weakening.
- The integration test must be hermetic: temp dirs, a local bare remote or a
  stubbed `git_push_to_dev`, no network, no real `wl sync`.
- Build → test → commit order; no direct `pytest` invocations (use the test
  skill / `run_tests.py`).
- Do not increase the status blast radius: `open` must never be re-applied to
  an item that already reached `completed`/`in_review`.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- `finish` wraps commit → push → worktree removal → parent-branch sync inside
  `with StatusLifecycle(work_item_id, target_stage="in_review"):`
  (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 4460); the
  `completed`/`in_review` write therefore happens at `__exit__` (~line 4614),
  after the push.
- `git_push_to_dev(cwd=worktree_path, ...)` pushes **from the worktree**, so
  the pre-push hook runs with cwd = worktree.
- A worktree's `.worklog/` holds `config.yaml`, `config.defaults.yaml`,
  `cache/`, `plugins/` only — no DB, no `initialized` marker. Verified:
  `wl show <id> --json` from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>`
  returns `{"success": false, "initialized": false, "error": "Worklog system is
  not initialized…"}`.
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `wl sync --git-branch refs/worklog/data`; from a
  worktree that command has no item id, so no `--worklog-dir` is injected and
  it fails — the hook prints `WARN: worklog sync failed — pushing anyway`.
  `refs/worklog/data` does not exist in ContentCreator.
- `resolve_worklog_flags` / `worklog_dir_flag` (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`)
  do resolve the main checkout store from a worktree (prefix-to-sibling scan
  first, then the nearest *initialized* ancestor), and `wl_show` /
  `wl_add_comment` inject those flags — so "the `__exit__` write went to a
  worktree-local store" is **not yet proven**; the observation
  `Captured original status …: open` (the claim was lost before `finish`)
  points at a separate revert path (stale `wl sync` import, or a late
  in-progress reset).
- The store is SQLite (`.worklog/worklog.db`), so "which store did this write
  to" is directly observable by file path and row state.

## Desired change

1. Finish resolves the main checkout store **once** from `state.repo_root` and
   passes it explicitly to every `wl` call it makes, including the
   `StatusLifecycle` transition and the completion comment — no reliance on
   cwd-derived resolution anywhere in the finish path.
2. Verbose/debug logging records, per `wl` mutation, the resolved
   `--worklog-dir`, so a future regression is diagnosable from the log alone.
3. Tests as described in the ACs pin both the resolution rule and the
   observable end state.
4. A short "status write ordering" note in the implement skill reference: the
   transition is written at `__exit__` after push; worktree pushes cannot sync
   worklog data because the worktree store is uninitialised.

## Verified during planning (code read at plan time)

- `phase_finish` already resolves the main checkout root once:
  `repo_root = _resolve_main_repo_root(worktree_path, state)`
  (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`), and it survives worktree removal.
  The `.worklog` store that owns the item is therefore
  `Path(repo_root) / ".worklog"` — an **initd** store by construction
  (`worklog.db` / `initialized` marker), unlike a worktree's committed copy.
- `StatusLifecycle` currently has **no** explicit-store parameter: its
  `__init__`, `show`, `update_status` and the `__enter__`/`__exit__` writes all
  route through `_run_wl_with_runner(...)`, which calls
  `resolve_worklog_flags(cmd, explicit_dir=None)`. An explicit store can
  therefore only be injected by extending those entry points with an
  `explicit_dir`/`worklog_dir` parameter (additive and defaulted, so existing
  call sites and tests are unaffected).
- `implement.py` already carries a module-level run-state pattern
  (`_worktree_path_global`, `_work_item_id_global`, `_repo_root_global`, set by
  `_record_run_state` and consumed by the signal handler). The finish path's
  resolved store can ride the same pattern so the SIGTERM/SIGINT cleanup
  (`_safety_reset_if_in_progress`) writes to the same store as the run.
- Every `wl` mutation reachable from `phase_finish` — `wl_add_comment`,
  `StatusLifecycle.update_status`, `_assert_terminal_status`,
  `_safety_reset_if_in_progress`, `_work_item_comment_bodies`,
  `_record_interruption_comment` — resolves through
  `resolve_worklog_flags`, so threading one explicit dir through those helpers
  covers the whole finish path (single seam, no cwd dependence).
- Related completed precedent: `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (worktree `cwd`-chain
  resolution) and `SA-0MUI78ROQ005B37N` (prefix-to-sibling injection).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — resolve `--worklog-dir` from `repo_root` for the finish path; log the target store per mutation; pass it through `StatusLifecycle`.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the resolution rule needs tightening (e.g. explicit `worklog_dir` support on the context manager); otherwise unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_status_store.py` — new unit + integration regression tests.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_status_lifecycle.py` — extend resolution assertions for the worktree cwd case.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the finding and the write ordering in the reference section.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — cross-reference the worktree-store behaviour if the rule is documented there.

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVFHAT31007ZILJ` — source item, transferred to this item (observed during `OSL-0MVE0A51L0072XSJ`).
- `OSL-0MUI78ROQ005B37N` — *Fix cross-repo worklog resolution in implement.py wl_* helpers (OSL items unfetchable from SorraAgents)* (completed) — precedent: the `resolve_worklog_flags` injection this item builds on.
- `OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT` — *implement.py: symlink nested package node_modules into worktrees* (completed) — worktree environment setup.
- Related docs: `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (SorraAgents), `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.

**Automated related-work check** (find-related run on the source OSL item):

## Problem

The audit merge gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) mines every hex token from the work item's description and comments and keeps those that resolve to **any** git object in the owning repo (`_commit_object_exists`). It does not filter by which ref the commit is reachable from.

When an item's text cites commits that exist only on `refs/worklog/data`, its backup refs, or other non-`dev` refs (e.g. a worklog history-rewrite item quoting incident-era SHAs), `_verify_merged_in_dev` finds no ancestor of `origin/dev` among the candidates and the gate proceeds to `_integrate_into_dev`, which cherry-picks those commits onto a worktree at `origin/dev` — conflicting and failing the audit closed with a spurious `Ready to close: No` merge-gate blocker.

## Observed (2026-10-23, SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC)

- Audit run 1: `git cherry-pick 345ea154a -> rc=1` conflict; verdict `Ready to close: No` (merge-gate blocker). `345ea154a` is a `refs/worklog/data` commit, never a `dev` commit.
- Workaround applied: the item description now records a real `dev` commit (`92fee5c30`, an ancestor of `origin/dev`), so the ancestor scan short-circuits to merged before any cherry-pick. Fragile — it depends on authors remembering to cite a `dev` commit and on the scan order.
- Related (already completed): SA-0MTQAF62U0085BEV (foreign hex that is not an object at all) and SA-0MTECRNGR000VKLV (decimal literals mined as SHAs). This is a third variant: the token **is** a commit object, but not on the delivery ref.

## Desired behaviour

- Restrict integration-evidence candidates to commits reachable from the item's delivery surface (branches matching `wl-<id>-*`, and any commit that is an ancestor of `origin/dev` or of a referenced feature branch) — or, at minimum, skip candidates not reachable from any `refs/heads/*` / `origin/*` ref of the owning repo, recording the skip as evidence.
- Commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/backup/*` or unreachable objects must never be cherry-picked onto `dev`.
- Keep fail-open behaviour for evidence-less items and fail-closed behaviour for genuinely unmerged feature work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** A work item whose description cites commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/data` (or a backup ref) does NOT trigger `_integrate_into_dev`; the gate records a skip note naming each excluded candidate and its non-delivery ref.
2. **AC2:** Regression test (in `skill/audit/tests/`) builds a fixture repo with a `dev` branch, a `refs/worklog/data` commit and a description citing that commit, and asserts `_phase_merge_gate` passes without invoking cherry-pick (no stray worktree, no blocker).
3. **AC3:** Existing behaviour is unchanged for: the real delivered commit (ancestor of `origin/dev` → merged), genuinely unmerged feature-branch work (still integrates), and evidence-less items (fail-open).
