# Add near-duplicate test detection to find redundant test coverage

## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want the test-value tooling to report
near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured
and redundant coverage pruned with evidence instead of suspicion.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines, +384
files on the reference project) against a **low** rewrite ratio (14.0%
modified-only), so the suite grows by *additive accumulation*, not churn. The
only existing redundancy check — `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`'s
"duplicate coverage" veto — matches test *names* containing `again|also covers|
duplicate|already covered` inside a single file. It cannot see a copy-pasted
test with renamed identifiers, nor the same behaviour re-tested through a
different import path, so redundancy accumulates with nothing forcing a
re-examination.

## Users

- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants the *size* of the redundancy, not
  just total growth, to decide whether pruning is worth runtime.
- **Implementer of the test-value refactor epic** (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`) —
  needs block-level, line-range evidence for the Classify and Prove steps; the
  epic's AC3 forbids deleting a test on suspicion alone.
- **Agent working a prune pass** — needs a deterministic, read-only command
  whose JSON can be joined with churn and usefulness data.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want a ranked list of duplicate test clusters with redundant
  line counts so I can see how much of the growth is redundancy.
- As the refactor implementer, I want each cluster to name the file and line
  range of every member so a prune candidate can be proven, not guessed.
- As an agent, I want `expected-repetition` (parametrised/table-driven cases)
  excluded by the tool so I do not file bogus prune items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — **Detection is structural, not textual.** Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via `ast` (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure.
- [ ] AC2 — **Clusters are reported with location and score.** Each cluster lists every member's file path, start–end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both `test_duplicates.json` (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and `test_duplicate_report.md` (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to `--output-dir`.
- [ ] AC3 — **Conservatism and legitimate repetition.** Parametrised/table-driven repetition is classified `expected-repetition`, not redundancy: `pytest.mark.parametrize`, `unittest.subTest`, `test.each`/`it.each`, and blocks whose sweep is a data loop over case literals are detected and excluded. Similarity bands are explicit (`duplicate` ≥ threshold, default 0.85; `near-duplicate` between the lower band, default 0.65, and the threshold), every cluster carries a `report-only` verdict, and the tool never edits, deletes or renames anything.
- [ ] AC4 — **Performance is bounded and documented.** Defaults skip trivial blocks (`--min-lines`, default 10) and bound the candidate set; comparison uses an inverted shingle index plus optional MinHash banding rather than all-pairs O(n²). Scope options `--changed-only <base-ref>` (git diff), `--max-files N`, `--min-lines N`, `--threshold` and `--min-shared-tokens` are documented with the complexity they imply, and a measured runtime figure for a ~500-test-file suite is recorded in the docs and in the report preamble.
- [ ] AC5 — **Behaviour is pinned by tests.** Unit tests cover: normalisation invariance (a copy with renamed identifiers still scores ≥ threshold), distinct behaviour staying below the band, `expected-repetition` exclusion for parametrised and table-driven cases, threshold boundary behaviour, cluster ordering and redundant-line arithmetic, JSON and Markdown schema/content, an empty or single-block suite, a non-Python file set, and one end-to-end run over a fixture suite. Every test asserts one documented behaviour and no test re-implements the similarity algorithm under test.
- [ ] AC6 — **Documentation is updated.** `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` gains a "Near-duplicate detection" section wired into the existing pruning workflow (step 2 "inspect candidates" gains the command as the evidence source for the duplicate-coverage bullet); `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` records the method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example and limitations; the `README.md` skill line mentions it; and the docs state that this analyser supersedes `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s name-marker heuristic for near-duplicates. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] AC7 — **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A maintainer can see — ranked by redundant line count — exactly which test
blocks duplicate each other and prune them on recorded evidence, instead of
inferring redundancy from a raw growth number.

## Constraints

- **Read-only.** No automatic deletion, editing or renaming of test files; no
  writes outside `--output-dir`.
- **Conservative thresholds.** A false "duplicate" verdict is worse than a
  miss: uncertainty reports, never removes.
- **No hardcoded project paths.** Test/source classification and language
  handling follow the configurable, language-neutral approach already used by
  `ChurnConfig`; extend it rather than forking it.
- **Python standard library only.** The repository has zero third-party
  dependencies (`package.json` `dependencies: {}`, no `requirements.txt`); no
  tree-sitter/esprima/acorn dependency may be added.
- **No network, no per-block subprocess.** The analyser must not shell out to
  `node`, `pytest` or a language server; all parsing is in-process.
- **Deterministic output.** Same tree and flags ⇒ byte-identical JSON, so
  results are comparable over time (the churn analyser's existing property).

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` (1,586 lines) — history-based
  churn: `ChurnConfig`, `is_test_file`, `classify_area`, `build_report`,
  `write_outputs`, CLI (`--project-root --branch --since --max-commits
  --output-dir --config --format --stdout --quiet`). It measures *how test code
  changes over time*; it contains no similarity analysis and never reads test
  bodies.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` (279 lines) — per-file verdicts.
  `_detect_duplicate` is a name-marker regex plus "imports production code";
  `VERDICT_REPORT` is always used for duplicate-only findings.
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — anti-pattern 4 "duplicates of
  existing core coverage" (same behaviour via a different import path) is prose
  with no automated check; the churn skill's pruning workflow names it but
  offers only a manual grep.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::jaccard_similarity` — word-token Jaccard over
  *text* strings; precedent for the metric, unusable for code ASTs (no
  normalisation, no block boundaries).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/` — `conftest.py` loads the analyser by path
  (`test_churn_analysis_under_test`) so it is not collected as a test module;
  `.pi/test-config.json` has no `test-churn` group, so these tests currently run
  only under `full`.

## Desired change

A new read-only analyser `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py`
with a CLI shaped like its churn sibling:

1. **Collect** test files using the existing classification (`is_test_file` +
   `ChurnConfig`), honouring `--changed-only <base-ref>` / `--max-files`.
2. **Extract blocks** with file + line range: Python via `ast` (top-level
   functions/classes/methods plus `with`-wrapped test bodies), JS/TS and other
   languages via comment-stripped tokenisation with brace/paren matching. Blocks
   smaller than `--min-lines` are skipped.
3. **Normalise** (docstrings and comments dropped, identifiers mapped to
   positional placeholders per scope, literals canonicalised by type, whitespace
   collapsed) so renamed copies remain identical while different behaviour does
   not.
4. **Fingerprint and compare**: token k-gram shingles (k default 5) → Jaccard
   similarity; candidates from an inverted shingle index (optionally MinHash
   banding) instead of all pairs; file-level rollup reports the strongest block
   pair per file pair.
5. **Classify** each pair as `duplicate`, `near-duplicate` or
   `expected-repetition` (parametrisation/data-loop detection), then cluster
   transitively and order clusters by redundant lines.
6. **Write** `test_duplicate_report.md` + `test_duplicates.json` with method,
   thresholds, limitations and measured runtime in the preamble; print a
   one-line summary to stderr.

The script is wired into the churn skill's pruning workflow and reference docs;
`evaluate_usefulness.py` keeps its heuristic unchanged (it answers a different,
per-file question) but its duplicate-coverage reason cross-references the new
tool.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py` — **new** analyser: block extraction, normalisation, shingling/Jaccard, clustering, JSON + Markdown writers, CLI.
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` — reuse `ChurnConfig`/`is_test_file`/`classify_area`; factor any shared helpers rather than duplicating them (no behaviour change to existing metrics).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py` — **new** unit + end-to-end suite for the analyser.
- `skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py` — add a path-loaded fixture for the new module (same pattern as `churn`).
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — new "Near-duplicate detection" section; pruning-workflow step 2 gains the command.
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example, limitations.
- `README.md` — extend the test-churn bullet to name near-duplicate detection.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` — docstring/reason cross-reference to the new tool (no behaviour change).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — anti-pattern 4 gains the automated-evidence pointer.
- `.pi/test-config.json` — optional: add a `test-churn` group (`skill/test-churn/**`) so changed-scope runs execute these tests instead of falling through to `full`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **False-positive duplicates** (shared boilerplate, fixture setup, mechanical
  parameter sweeps) are the dominant risk and the reason for report-only
  verdicts: mitigation is the `expected-repetition` classifier, a conservative
  default threshold of 0.85 with a separate `near-duplicate` band, `--min-lines`
  skipping trivial blocks, and a documented limitations section.
- **Parser fragility outside Python** — brace matching on JS/TS is approximate;
  mitigation is conservative fallback (a block that cannot be delimited is
  reported as "unparsed" in the JSON summary rather than silently compared as a
  whole file), plus a non-Python fixture in the tests.
- **Performance on large suites** — shingle construction is linear in tokens,
  but candidate pairing can still blow up; mitigation is the inverted index,
  `--max-files`/`--changed-only` scope options and a measured runtime figure
  recorded in the docs.
- **Scope creep** — "also fix the duplicated tests" is explicitly out of scope:
  remediation belongs to the epic's prune/rework children. Any duplication the
  tool finds in this repository is reported as evidence in a comment or a
  follow-on item, not fixed here.
- **Assumption A1** — the detector belongs beside the churn analyser in
  `skill/test-churn/` rather than inside `evaluate_usefulness.py`, because it is
  suite-wide measurement, not a per-file verdict, and the churn skill is where
  the pruning workflow lives.
- **Assumption A2** — no new third-party parser dependency (stdlib only), so
  JS/TS detection is token-based rather than AST-based; Python gets exact AST
  normalisation.
- **Assumption A3** — the item stays `discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`
  rather than being re-parented under `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`; the epic's
  Classify/Prove children consume its output, and re-parenting a
  `plan_complete` epic would change that epic's scope.
- **Assumption A4** — a `test-churn` test group does not exist in
  `.pi/test-config.json` today; adding one is a small, separable improvement
  that keeps these tests out of the `full`-only path (optional within this
  item).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic; additive accumulation is its
  stated failure mode and this analyser feeds its Classify and Prove steps.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing; a direct fault-detection signal that
  complements this cheap redundancy signal (discovery source for this item).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over
  `toHaveBeenCalledWith`; overlapping "rework" direction, different evidence.
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill:
  a natural consumer of this output.
- Code: `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`,
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (anti-pattern 4),
  `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Duplicate-work check performed with `wl search` over "duplicate test", "clone
detection", "test redundancy" and "near-duplicate … coverage" — no completed or
open item overlaps these acceptance criteria (the nearest hits are intake
duplicate-work detection `SA-0MTWMCJ37000485M` and the refactor skill's
`consolidate_duplicates.py`, both different problems: work-item duplication and
duplicated *work items*, not duplicated test blocks).

No interactive interview round was held: the seed description already carried a
problem statement, six acceptance criteria, constraints and related work, so the
intake was driven by repository research instead of questions. The four open
design decisions were resolved as documented assumptions for review:

- Q: "Where should the near-duplicate detector live — extend
  `evaluate_usefulness.py`, or a new script beside the churn analyser?" —
  **Answer (agent assumption A1, pending producer confirmation):** new script
  `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py`. Research: inspected
  `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` (per-file verdict, name-marker
  duplicate heuristic) and `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`
  (suite-wide measurement, `ChurnConfig`, report writers); the new capability is
  suite-wide, so it follows the churn analyser's shape. Source: repository
  inspection.
- Q: "May a parser dependency (tree-sitter/esprima) be added for exact JS/TS
  ASTs?" — **Answer (agent assumption A2, pending producer confirmation):** no.
  Research: the repository carries zero third-party dependencies
  (`package.json` `dependencies: {}`, no `requirements.txt`), so JS/TS detection
  uses token normalisation and Python uses stdlib `ast`. Source: repository
  inspection.
- Q: "Should this item be re-parented under the test-value epic?" — **Answer
  (agent assumption A3, pending producer confirmation):** no; keep
  `discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` and cross-reference the epic, whose
  Classify/Prove children consume the output. Source: `wl show
  SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO --json`.
- Q: "Is a `test-churn` test group worth adding so these tests run on
  changed-scope gates?" — **Answer (agent assumption A4, optional within this
  item):** yes if it stays a one-line config addition; `.pi/test-config.json`
  currently has no group covering `skill/test-churn/**`. Source: repository
  inspection.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQEEOK5N003ILYB** – [CRITICAL] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_smell_detection.py:963 — Local variable `file_paths_in_findings` is assigned to but never used (F841) (completed)
- **SA-0MRMB6P6M008H4U4** – Fix legacy skill/ path reference in planall SKILL.md (completed)
- **SA-0MQZZ93110003MBU** – Add review of affected files in plan review stages (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+467 more)

## Goal

As a producer, I want per-test runtime and flake history so I can express test value as fault detection per second of suite runtime and bound the cost of periodic mutation campaigns.

## Problem statement

Test value is currently measured without its cost. The test runner reports suite-level timing, but there is no per-test timing or flake history, so a valuable-but-slow test and a worthless-but-slow test are indistinguishable, and mutation-campaign runtime cannot be allocated sensibly. The test-value epic (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`, AC7) also needs before/after runtime evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test runner records per-test duration and a bounded flake history across runs.
- [ ] Emits a machine-readable report consumable by the test-value aggregator (churn/mutation/runtime join).
- [ ] Overhead is bounded and documented; normal runs stay within the existing runtime budget.
- [ ] Flake detection is deterministic for repeated failures and does not hide genuine failures.
- [ ] Integrated into the existing `skill/test` runner rather than a new measurement skill.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the pass/fail semantics of the test runner.
- History storage is bounded (retention policy documented).
- Follows the test-execution policy: agents still invoke tests only via the test skill; infrastructure gates are out of scope.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (AC7 runtime).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing (runtime bound).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.

# Intake Brief: Repeat producer actions in red on the final report conclusion

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report`) lists blocking producer
actions in `## Producer Actions`, but the `## Conclusion` — the last thing the
operator reads — does not repeat them. When a session ends with something the
producer must do (answer a question, make a decision, grant an approval), the
operator can miss it in the body of a long report. Repeating any genuine
producer action in the Conclusion in red makes the blocking call-to-action
impossible to overlook.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports in the pi TUI: wants the
  blocking action to stand out at the end of the report, not be buried mid-page.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: keeps passing
  blocking actions via `--producer-actions`; the renderer handles the red
  repetition deterministically (no per-skill change).

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill session needs a decision from me, I want that
  decision repeated in red in the conclusion so I cannot miss it."
- "As a producer, when nothing is required of me, I do not want a red warning in
  the conclusion."
- "As an agent, I want the renderer to do this automatically so every skill
  behaves the same way."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the normalised producer actions are a genuine, non-`None needed`
   action, `render_report()` appends the action text **verbatim** to the
   `## Conclusion` section, wrapped in ANSI SGR red (`\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`) with a
   `⚠️ Producer action required:` lead-in. Verified by unit test asserting the
   escape sequences and the exact action text inside `## Conclusion`.
2. When no producer actions are supplied, or the supplied text is routine
   workflow progression that normalises to `None needed`, the Conclusion
   contains no ANSI escape sequences and no repeated action text. Verified by
   unit tests (absent actions; `Proceed to /skill:plan`; `Review the brief, then
   run /skill:plan`).
3. Colour can be disabled with a new `--no-colour` CLI flag **or** the standard
   `NO_COLOR` environment variable (non-empty). In that mode the Conclusion
   still repeats the action in plain text with the `⚠️` marker and contains no
   ANSI escape sequences. Verified by unit tests for both opt-outs.
4. Multi-line / multi-action producer text is repeated verbatim (line breaks
   preserved) and the rest of the report is unchanged: section order,
   `## Producer Actions` → `## Notes` → `## Conclusion`, the existing
   completed/incomplete conclusion sentences, and the `</end_session>`
   terminator. Verified by regression tests.
5. `skill/report/SKILL.md` documents the conditional red repetition in the
   canonical template, the layout rules, and the colour opt-out
   (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`) alongside the existing icon opt-out. Verified
   by document review.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Implement in the shared renderer only (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  plus a small shared colour helper — do not fork report logic into the ~17
  calling skills.
- Repeat **after** routine-next-step normalisation (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW): a
  routine next step must never produce red text.
- Do not use TTY detection to decide colour: the CLI's stdout is captured/piped
  by agents before being pasted into the final response, so TTY detection would
  disable the feature exactly where it is needed. Opt-out must be explicit
  (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`).
- Colour is decorative: the `⚠️` marker and the plain action text must carry the
  meaning when colour is unavailable, so the report stays readable in
  non-ANSI consumers (GitHub, plain-text logs).
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.
- Do not change `## Producer Actions` semantics, the pane-status derivation, or
  the existing conclusion wording.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` renders `## Producer Actions` from the normalised
  `producer_actions` string (`None needed` when absent), then `## Notes`, then
  `## Conclusion`.
- The Conclusion currently emits one of two fixed sentences based on AC
  verdicts (`_derive_session_status`): completed → "This completes … Ready for
  `<next_action>`."; incomplete → "… is incomplete. Requires attention
  (`<next_action>`)." Nothing else is appended.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` already provides `icons_enabled(no_icons, env)`
  honouring `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` — the convention to mirror for
  colour, but colour must be a separate switch (`WL_NO_ICONS` must not disable
  colour).
- No ANSI/colour handling exists anywhere in the report renderer today (the
  only ANSI in the repo is in `tests/integration/test-worktree-workflow.sh`).

## Desired change

- Add `colour_enabled(no_colour=False, env=None)` (and `RED`/`RESET` constants)
  to `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`: enabled by default; disabled by
  `--no-colour` or a non-empty `NO_COLOR`.
- In `render_report()`, after the existing conclusion sentence(s), when the
  normalised producer actions are not `None needed`, append a blank line and a
  red line: `⚠️ Producer action required: <verbatim action text>`. Apply
  `RED … RESET` only when colour is enabled.
- Thread an optional `no_colour: bool = False` parameter through
  `render_report()`, `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()` and the
  CLI, adding the `--no-colour` flag.
- Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` (template, layout rules, example, colour
  opt-out) and the `README.md` report-helper bullet to mention the red
  repetition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — conditional red repetition in the
  Conclusion; `no_colour` plumbing and `--no-colour` flag.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` helper + `RED`/`RESET`
  constants mirroring `icons_enabled()`.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — new tests: red repetition,
  no-repetition for absent/routine actions, `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR` fallback,
  multi-line preservation, structure regression.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` unit tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — template/layout/example + colour opt-out docs.
- `README.md` — report-helper bullet: note the red repetition of blocking
  producer actions in the Conclusion.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** — "Don't include producer actions that are next steps"
  (completed): established normalisation to `None needed`; the red repetition
  must run after it.
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — "Misleading completion message on LLM summaries"
  (completed): made the Conclusion reflect session status; this item extends the
  same section.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion" (completed): established the ✅/⚠️/🚫 status colour semantics this
  feature reuses for a red call-to-action.
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill" (completed): origin of the canonical report contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "red font" means ANSI SGR red in terminal output.** The report
  is rendered to stdout and pasted into the pi TUI; ANSI is the only mechanism
  that reliably colours that path. If the producer expects Markdown/HTML
  colouring, the brief should be revised before implementation (documented in
  the Appendix).
- **Assumption — red repeats blocking actions only.** Because routine workflow
  progression is normalised to `None needed` first, it can never trigger red;
  this avoids the false "producer is blocking" signal fixed by
  SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW.
- **Assumption — no TTY detection.** Explicit opt-out only, because agent-captured
  stdout is not a TTY.
- **Risk — ANSI leakage into non-terminal consumers** (GitHub, PRs, plain logs).
  Mitigation: `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR`, plus the `⚠️` marker and plain text so the
  meaning survives even if escapes are stripped or shown literally.
- **Risk — colour-blindness / theme contrast.** Mitigation: the `⚠️` marker and
  the words "Producer action required" carry the signal; colour is decorative.
- **Risk — multi-line producer text.** Mitigation: wrap the whole block once and
  test line-break preservation rather than prefixing each line.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas (colouring the `## Producer Actions` section,
  colourising AC verdicts, HTML-export colour) are out of scope — record as
  separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'red font' mean for a Markdown report rendered by the LLM/TUI —
  ANSI escape codes, HTML `<span style=\"color:red\">`, or plain emphasis?"
  — **Answer (repo research + design analysis):** ANSI SGR red. The report is
  printed to stdout and pasted into the terminal-rendered TUI; raw ANSI passes
  through and colours the terminal, whereas inline HTML styles are not honoured
  by the Markdown→terminal path and GitHub strips `style` attributes. Recorded
  as an assumption; the producer can request an HTML/bold variant at review.
  No interactive round was required for the rest of the brief.
- Q: "Should routine next-step actions (e.g. 'Proceed to /skill:plan') also be
  repeated in red?" — **Answer (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW contract):** No. Routine
  workflow progression is normalised to `None needed` and must never be shown as
  a blocking red action; only genuine, current-stage actions are repeated.
- Q: "Should colour be auto-detected (TTY) or explicitly opt-out?" — **Answer
  (design analysis):** Explicit opt-out only. Agent-captured stdout is not a
  TTY, so TTY detection would silently disable the feature on the exact path
  that needs it. `--no-colour` and `NO_COLOR` are the opt-outs.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ1QM9L0083KAW** – Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates (completed)
- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** – Don't include producer actions that are next steps (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: action, actions, conclusion, final, llm, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
data.title: Repeat producer actions in red font on final LLM action report

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — regression test

# Intake brief — re-filed from OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ (ContentCreator worklog)

**Headline:** Add a consumption mechanism to the refactor skill so that `# <!-- REFACTOR-<id> ... -->` marker blocks are automatically detected as stale and flagged (or removed) when their recorded smell is fixed.

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `# <!-- REFACTOR-<work-item-id> ... -->` blocks into source files to record code smells. The expectation is that whoever fixes the smell also deletes the block. Nothing checks that this happened. Three stale blocks were found in a single sweep, and one live marker remains — proving the gap is ongoing, not a one-off.

## Users

- **Maintainer opening a file.** A stale marker asserts a live smell; disproving it requires a worklog lookup and wastes time.
- **The refactor skill itself (next run).** A stale block reads as a live smell and invites a duplicate work item.
- **The operator running periodic sweeps.** Currently they must manually delete each stale block (OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW).

**User story:** "As a developer running the refactor skill or reading a file, I want stale REFACTOR markers to be flagged or removed automatically, so that the tree only contains markers for unfinished work."

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The refactor skill writes markers via `comment_injection.py`; no corresponding consumption code exists.
- Markers contain: `REFACTOR-<id>`, `smell: <type>`, `severity: <level>`, `description: <text>`, and optionally `# status: resolved — <reason>`.
- OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW removed three stale blocks by hand (completed). The consumption gap was recorded as this item (discovered-from:OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW).
- One live marker remains in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:2` (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, ruff C408) — this is correct and should stay until the smell is fixed.
- The `# status: resolved` line exists in at least one marker (`scripts/tidy_residual_links.py`) but is not parsed by any tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The refactor skill exposes a reusable function `reap_stale_markers()` (or similar) that scans files for `# <!-- REFACTOR-... -->` blocks and returns a list of stale markers — each entry identifying the file path, line range, work item ID, and the reason the marker is stale (work item terminal / `# status: resolved` present / work item missing).
2. A new CLI entry point `python3 -m skill.refactor.scripts.reap_stale_markers` invokes the function, prints a summary of stale markers found, and exits non-zero if any are discovered — suitable for pre-commit or CI.
3. When invoked with `--dry-run` (default), the tool reports stale markers without modifying files; when invoked with `--remove`, it deletes the marker blocks in-place and preserves all other file content exactly.
4. The function correctly classifies a marker as stale when: (a) the referenced work item's status is `completed` or `deleted` (soft-deleted), or (b) the marker block itself contains `# status: resolved`, or (c) the referenced work item cannot be found (missing or inaccessible) — reason `work-item-missing`. It must NOT flag a marker as stale if the smell is still unfixed (work item is `open` and no resolved line).
5. `python3 -m ruff check` stays clean over all affected files; no `noqa` or config suppression is added.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`./scripts/run_tests.sh`).

## Constraints

- Keep it out of `comment_injection.py` — that mechanism is correct; the gap is consumption.
- The tool must work with the Worklog CLI (`wl show --json`) to check item status; do not add a direct database dependency.
- Do not modify marker copies inside `.worklog/worktrees/*` — only process files in the source tree.
- The `# status: resolved` line format is `# status: resolved — <reason>`; parse this conservatively (presence of `status: resolved` is sufficient).
- If a marker references a work item that cannot be found (item does not exist or is inaccessible), treat it as stale with reason `work-item-missing`.

## Desired change

Add a new module `refactor/reap_markers.py` (or `refactor/consumption.py`) with the detection logic, a CLI entry point, and tests. The refactor skill's main scan should optionally invoke this as a pre-flight or post-flight check.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — reference only; own the marker format, do not modify
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reference only; understand `REFACTOR_PATTERN` matching
- `skill/refactor/reap_markers.py` — new module: detection logic + public API (`reap_stale_markers()`)
- `skill/refactor/scripts/reap_stale_markers.py` — new CLI entry point
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document the reaper and its place in the scan lifecycle
- `tests/test_refactor/test_reap_markers.py` — new test file (mirrors `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py`)

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — Remove stale REFACTOR- marker blocks left in tests and scripts (completed) — manual sweep of three blocks
- `OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L` — Live marker in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py` (ruff C408) — should remain until fixed
- `OSL-0MVM96NMG002ZAMZ` — Recover orphaned refactor-batch edits (completed) — same marker mechanism, different problem
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — Marker-above-shebang near miss (completed) — edge case for comment placement

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the Worklog CLI (`wl show`) is available and reliable for checking item status during the refactor skill's run. **Mitigation:** handle CLI errors gracefully (treat unreachable items as potentially stale with a warning).
- **Risk — false positive:** a marker could reference a completed item that is still relevant as historical context. **Mitigation:** default to `--dry-run` mode; require explicit `--remove` to delete.
- **Risk — scope creep:** turning this into a full repo-wide cleanup sweep. **Mitigation:** scope is the detection/reporting mechanism only; bulk removal is a separate concern.
- **Assumption:** `# status: resolved` is the canonical in-marker resolution signal. **Mitigation:** documented in the new module's docstring; the operator can update if the convention changes.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

No interview round was run: the problem, scope, constraints, and related work were answerable by repo and worklog search.

- **Q (resolved by search):** What markers currently exist in the repo? — **Answer:** one live marker in `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:2` (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, ruff C408, smell still unfixed) and three stale markers that were deleted by OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW. Source: grep, this session.
- **Q (resolved by search):** Is `# status: resolved` a real convention or just an ad-hoc line? — **Answer:** it appears on at least one marker (`scripts/tidy_residual_links.py`) and was noted in the OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW implementation report as evidence the smell was fixed. It is a convention worth formalising in the reap module. Source: `wl show OSL-0MVM4UWDI001GZNY`, this session.
- **Q (resolved by search):** Can the refactor skill invoke `wl`? — **Answer:** yes — the refactor skill's scripts already use the Worklog CLI (e.g., `wl list --tags Refactor`). Source: inspection of `comment_injection.py`, `workitem_creation.py`, this session.
- **Duplicate check:** `wl search "REFACTOR marker reap consumption stale"` returned only OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ itself and OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW (the manual sweep). No item covers automated consumption.

## Appendix: plan-session questions (plan skill)

Planning stopped at the interview step: the item cannot be decomposed into
implementation tasks until repository ownership is settled.

- **OPEN QUESTION (blocking; directed to the producer):** Which repository
  should the reap implementation land in? The item's ACs and Key Files target
  the shared/global refactor skill (AC1 "The refactor skill exposes a reusable
  function", Key Files `.pi/agent/skills/refactor/...`, AC2
  `python3 -m refactor.reap`), but that skill is developed in the **SorraAgents**
  repository (`skill/refactor/`, installed as the symlink
  `~/.pi/agent/skills -> ~/projects/SorraAgents/skill`) and every refactor-skill
  change is tracked there under SA- IDs (e.g. SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F,
  SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD). This item is filed in the **ContentCreator** worklog
  (OSL-). **Why it matters:** it decides which repo the code, tests and commits
  go into, and the implement skill's worktree isolation normally forbids
  editing outside the ContentCreator worktree.
  - Options: **(a)** re-file as an SA- item in the SorraAgents worklog and
    redirect/close this OSL item — *recommended*, matches every other
    refactor-skill change; **(b)** keep the OSL item and author cross-repo
    changes into SorraAgents from it — needs explicit authorisation;
    **(c)** rescope this OSL item to a ContentCreator-local reap tool (e.g.
    `scripts/reap_stale_markers.py` over ContentCreator's own tree) and relax
    AC1's skill wording.
  - Evidence gathered: `git ls-files | grep refactor` in ContentCreator returns
    0 paths; `.pi/agent/` does not exist in ContentCreator;
    `.pi/skills_extensions/` supports only `SKILL_PREFIX.md` / `SKILL_POSTFIX.md`
    / `extension.json` (prose and data, not Python modules).
  - **Preferred option: (a).**
  - **ANSWER (producer, this session): (a)** — re-file as an SA- item in the
    SorraAgents worklog and redirect this OSL item. FINAL. That re-filing is
    this work item; `OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ` was deleted after it was created.
- **Q (resolved by inspection, no operator input needed):** Where are the live
  REFACTOR markers today? — **Answer:** two. `tests/test_rss_freshness.py:1`
  (OSL-0MVY7WI0K009WE4L, `complexity`, C408, item `open` — correctly *not*
  stale) and `tests/test_rss_regenerate.py:1` (OSL-0MVYHBV60007WKHK,
  `ruff_specific`, RUF059, item `open` — also not stale). Source: grep over
  the ContentCreator tree, this session. Note the second marker's work item
  records a *worktree* path (`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>`),
  which is relevant to the "do not modify marker copies inside
  `.worklog/worktrees/*`" constraint.
- **Q (resolved by inspection):** Does the marker format match what
  `comment_injection.py` writes? — **Answer:** yes — `# <!-- REFACTOR-<id>`,
  `# smell:`, `# severity:`, `# description:`, `# -->`. The optional
  `# status: resolved — <reason>` line is *not* produced by
  `_build_comment_block()`; it is added by hand, so the reap module must treat
  it as an optional extra line inside the block.

## Re-filing record

Re-filed from `OSL-0MVXZOWSL007VREJ` in the ContentCreator worklog. The producer
chose option (a): the reap implementation belongs to this repository, because
the refactor skill is developed here (`skill/refactor/`) and every
refactor-skill change is tracked under an SA- ID. The ContentCreator item was
deleted after this item was created.

Consequences applied to this brief:

- **Key Files** rewritten from the ContentCreator-relative
  `.pi/agent/skills/refactor/...` (which does not exist there) to this
  repository's real layout, and `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` added.
- **AC2** now names `python3 -m skill.refactor.scripts.reap_stale_markers`,
  matching this repository's invocation convention.
- **AC7** names the suite invocation (`./scripts/run_tests.sh`).

Planning status carried over from the ContentCreator session: the effort/risk
pre-check returned **skip** (Small / Low), the six automated review stages ran
against the brief, one unambiguous AC gap was closed (AC1/AC4 now include the
`work-item-missing` case that the Constraints already required), and the
acceptance-criteria coverage review returned **proceed**.

## Objective

Add the read-only, unit-testable **bump preflight helper** used by the ship skill's new version-bump evaluation step. It gathers the release candidates and renders a compact review packet. It performs **no judgement and no mutation** — the agent judges, the producer approves.

## User Story

As the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`, I want a single helper that gathers every release candidate and renders the evidence I need to judge the release's importance, so that my patch/minor/major call is based on the items' content rather than guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- New module `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` exports a `gatherReleaseCandidates` (name may vary) that resolves candidates through an **injectable fetch boundary** (default `getCandidateItems()` from `check-audit-gate.js`); tests inject fakes and never read the live worklog.
- The helper enriches each candidate with the fields needed to judge importance: `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, the `## Impact` section or user story, and a truncated description excerpt. It tolerates missing fields (falls back to the title/id and an empty excerpt) without throwing.
- The helper renders a review packet (Markdown or plain text) that includes: the current version, the three candidate outcomes computed via the **existing** `bump-version.js` arithmetic (`bumpVersion`), and the per-item evidence listed above. It reuses `resolveVersionSource`/`bumpVersion` (no duplicated semver arithmetic).
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics (`bumpVersion`) rather than duplicating version arithmetic anywhere in the new helper.
- An **empty or unreadable candidate set** fails safe: the helper reports `patch` as the proposal, logs a warning explaining why, and never throws or blocks a release.
- Gathering/rendering is **purely read-only** — the helper performs no `git`, tag, PR, or `wl` mutation.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` covers: candidate gathering via the injected boundary, rendering of every packet field, the empty candidate set (patch + warning), and that `minor`/`major` outcomes reset the lower components correctly (delegated to `bumpVersion`).
- Tests pass via the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope changed`, node suite) and touch no live worklog or real git state.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the failing test file first (`test_bump_preflight.mjs`, `node:test`).
2. Add `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` with an exported preflight function accepting `{ getCandidateItemsFn, repoRoot }` injection.
3. Project `version` from the resolved version source; compute `patch`/`minor`/`major` outcomes with `bumpVersion`.
4. Render the packet with a stable, agent-readable layout; truncate description excerpts (e.g. ~200 chars).
5. Return a structured result (`{ candidates, currentVersion, proposals, proposedBump, warning }`) as well as the rendered text, so tests can assert fields directly.
6. Export a small render/format function so the workflow contract test can rely on a stable API.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (reuse `getCandidateItems`)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` (reuse `resolveVersionSource`, `bumpVersion`)

## Constraints

- No issue-type or priority classifier — the helper only gathers/renders evidence.
- No mutation and no new git side effects.
- Empty/unreadable candidates default to `patch` with a warning.

## Deliverables

- `bump-preflight.js` with tests, passing the changed-scope suite.

## Goal

Pin the spawn-failure classifier's vocabulary and fail-safe **before** any retry code exists, so the drive loop can only ever retry a genuine provider/model-resolution failure.

User story: As an implement-skill maintainer, I want the spawn-failure classification to be table-driven and tested first, so extending the infrastructure-retry budget to spawn-time failures can never silently retry a real defect.

## Context

`CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) reports driven child sessions dying at startup with `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` and aborting the drive chain. Upstream plan: features F1–F3 + F5 live in this repository; the config half is folded into `SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN`. This item is **F1 — test-first**.

Findings from the planning session (code-grounded):

- `_default_session_spawner` reports a non-zero exit as `Child session for <id> exited with code N: <5-line tail>` — the provider text arrives **inside `reason`**.
- `_pane_session_spawner` reports `Failed to start the pane agent for <id>: …` or `Pane agent for <id> did not complete: …`.
- `classify_finish_failure` + `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` is the existing table-driven infra vocabulary, but it is **finish-only**; there is no spawn-side classifier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `classify_spawn_failure(reason)` helper exists in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` returning `{kind, reason, provider, remedy}` and is driven by an explicit allow-list table (mirroring `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS`), never by prose sniffing in `phase_drive`.
- Tests (written first, failing before the helper exists) assert: a headless `Child session for X exited with code 1: … No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` reason classifies as `kind == "infrastructure"` with `provider == "MunitoAI"` and a non-empty remedy.
- The pane flavours (`Failed to start the pane agent for X: …` and `Pane agent for X did not complete: …`) carrying the same provider text classify as `infrastructure`.
- Fail-safe is pinned: an unclassified reason (a Python traceback tail, an arbitrary message, an empty string, `None`) classifies as `kind == "unknown"` — never `infrastructure`.
- A `timed out` reason is not reclassified as provider-infrastructure (the timeout path keeps its own reconciliation semantics).
- The remedy text names the concrete action (drop the unservable pattern from `enabledModels`, or provide the missing API key) and is asserted by at least one test.
- Tests live in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` (the existing home for drive classification tests).

## Implementation sketch

1. Add the failing tests in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`.
2. Add `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` (allow-list of provider/model-resolution fragments) and `classify_spawn_failure(reason)` beside `classify_finish_failure`.
3. Reuse the existing `_describe_*`-style description idiom so F2 can surface `step`/`reason` in `children_driven`.

## Notes

- Test-first ordering is mandatory: this item lands before F2 so the vocabulary is fixed by tests.
- Do not widen `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS`; no secret may reach `pane split --env`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

A maintainer can extend the drive loop's infrastructure retries to spawn-time provider failures knowing the classifier can only ever match a real model-resolution error, so a genuine defect still hard-stops the chain.

discovered-from:CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J

## Goal

A provider/model-resolution failure at child spawn is retried **inside the same `drive` invocation** on the existing bounded infra-retry budget instead of stopping the chain with `failed_child`.

User story: As an operator running `implement.py drive <epic>`, I want a transient model-routing failure in a child session to be retried automatically, so a healthy child is not abandoned and the chain does not stop.

## Context

`CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) reports five child-session aborts across one drive run (children `CUR-0MWKPMVRH00780TO` ×2, `CUR-0MWKPMWGL005EKZF`, `CUR-0MWKPMX3M0052ZOL` ×2); each child completed on the next `drive` invocation with no code change. This item is **F2** of the upstream plan and depends on **F1** (`classify_spawn_failure` + its tests).

Current behaviour: `phase_drive`'s non-success branch runs `_reconcile_spawn_failure` → `record_spawn_failure` → `_release_orphaned_child_claim` → `report["failed_child"]` + `break`. The existing infra-retry path (`--infra-retry-limit`, `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT = 5`, `_drive_infra_backoff_delay`) covers **only** `finish` refusals and deliberately never spawns a session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `_reconcile_spawn_failure` reports **non-terminal**, a spawn failure classified `infrastructure` by `classify_spawn_failure` consumes one slot of `--infra-retry-limit` (default 5), sleeps `_drive_infra_backoff_delay(attempt)` and re-spawns the same child within the same invocation — no manual re-run.
- The `children_driven` entry for the retry is `result: "infra-retry"` and carries `step`, `reason`, `attempt` and a `message` naming the provider and model, reusing the additive reporting shape of the finish infra-retry.
- Budget exhaustion produces a chain-stop message naming the provider/model **and an actionable remedy**, instead of a bare `No models match pattern …`; the remedy directive is asserted in a test.
- Ordering is correct and pinned by a test: a child reconciled `completed-late` (already terminal) is **never** retried and no second session is spawned.
- Fail-safe preserved and pinned by a test: an unclassified spawn failure still hard-stops with `report["failed_child"]` and is never retried.
- Retrying does not duplicate side effects: the per-child lock is not re-acquired while held, no second worktree is created, and `record_spawn_failure` evidence is not re-written for an attempt that never produced work.
- The shared budget is documented: `infra_retries[child_id]` is one counter across finish-refusals and spawn retries, and the counter plus `infra_retry_limit` remain present in the drive report.
- Tests use a fake spawner that fails with the provider reason twice and then succeeds on a 5-slot budget, plus the exhaustion, completed-late and unclassified cases (`tests/test_implement_drive.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`).

## Implementation sketch

1. Extract the retry decision from the finish infra-retry block and call it on the spawn-failure path, **after** reconciliation and before `failed_child`/`break`.
2. Reuse `infra_retries` / `_drive_infra_backoff_delay`; record the `children_driven` entry with the classified provider reason.
3. Re-enter the loop for the same child (`continue`) rather than spawning a different one.

## Constraints

- `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` stays `(DRIVE_RECURSION_ENV, WORKTREE_ENV, ENV_LOCK_TOKEN)` — no new secrets in argv.
- The commit-preservation gate, `reset-for-retry`, the spawn-failure evidence record (`SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G`), the per-child lock and the terminality reconciliation keep their current semantics; this extends them.
- No session may be spawned for a child that reconciliation proved terminal.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

An operator running a driven epic no longer loses a multi-minute child session — or the whole chain — to an intermittent model-routing error, so a `drive` run becomes self-healing.

# ruff ISC004 in test_run_tests_failure_notices.py:897 — candidate false positive

## Problem statement

The audit's candidate-false-positive screen filed this chore for ruff ISC004
(`unparenthesized implicit string concatenation in collection`) at
`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py:897`: a deliberately split
long expected test-name string inside a list literal on the left of an
equality assertion. The concatenation is intentional and unambiguous, and the
same finding is currently tracked by **three** open work items, so resolving it
required one producer decision plus consolidation. The producer has decided
(**Option B**): make the intent explicit in code by parenthesising the
concatenated string, rather than waiving the finding.

## Users

- **Producers / operators triaging audit output** — they need each candidate
  false positive decided once, after which it stops re-entering the review
  queue.
- **Developers reading the test** — an explicit parenthesised concatenation
  (or a waiver) removes the ambiguity ISC004 warns about (a missing comma
  silently merging two list elements).

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I decide once between "waive" and "fix in code" and the
  finding stops generating chores and review-queue entries.
- As a developer, I can see at a glance that
  `"...> main-street tutorial part 1 " "> step 3"` is one intentional string
  and not a missing comma.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Producer decision recorded (topic answered 2026-11-18): **Option B — wrap
   the implicitly concatenated string in parentheses**. No audit waiver is
   added; the finding is fixed in code so it stops reproducing.
2. Consolidation (producer: "as recommended"): this item
   (`SA-0MWMOCL1Y004I9OR`) is the decision-of-record and the duplicate items
   for the same finding — `SA-0MWMK06OU004AUPB` (line 897) and
   `SA-0MWMBFRTG00793NN` (line 891, same
   `Refactor-Finding-Key: ISC004:<file>`) — are closed as superseded once the
   finding stops reproducing (dry-run then `--apply` of
   `skill/refactor/scripts/reverify.py`, each closure recording which item
   supersedes it).
3. Verification: `ruff check --isolated --select ISC004
   skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` exits clean after a
   code fix, or the waiver resolves via `python3 $(skill_path
   audit)/scripts/audit_waiver.py list <audited-item-id>` showing an `ISC004`
   waiver for the file while the finding is excluded from chore creation and
   the producer-review queue.
4. No behavioural change: if Option B is chosen, `test_run_tests_failure_notices.py`
   still passes with identical assertions (the concatenated string value is
   unchanged).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The ISC004 warning at `test_run_tests_failure_notices.py:897` stops firing
because the intentional multi-line string split is now explicitly parenthesised
— readers and tooling alike can see it is one string, not a missing comma — and
the three duplicate tracking items are closed as a single accepted resolution.

## Constraints

- ISC004 is an optional ruff rule (`flake8-implicit-str-concat`), not a core
  rule, and the repository has **no ruff configuration file** — the only
  source of this finding is the audit's isolated scan
  (`ruff check --isolated --select ISC004 <path>`).
- Any code change must not alter the semantics of the test strings or the
  test's assertions.
- A waiver recorded with no `--line` accepts ISC004 for the **whole file**
  (it survives line drift but would also suppress genuine future ISC004
  findings in that file); a line-pinned waiver matches line 897 only and
  drifts if the file is edited above it.
- The audit chore is never auto-suppressed or auto-closed by the audit itself;
  closure comes from the re-verification sweep or an explicit close.

## Existing state

Finding (reproducible now):

```
$ ruff check --isolated --select ISC004 skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py
ISC004 Unparenthesized implicit string concatenation in collection
   --> skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py:897:13
896 |         assert [f["test_name"] for f in result["failures"]] == [
897 | /             "tests/e2e/tutorial-1.browser.test.ts > main-street tutorial part 1 "
898 | |             "> step 3"
899 |         ], "only the tutorial failure is a suite failure"
```

The two literals form one string (`"tests/e2e/tutorial-1.browser.test.ts >
main-street tutorial part 1 > step 3"`) — this is a single-element list, and
the split is purely for line length (`test_retry_failed_is_red_and_never_discards`,
introduced in commit `a49476c63f`, CG-0MWEHG69O005VM17).

Ruff's own guidance (ISC004 docs) says: *"If the concatenation is intentional,
wrap it in parentheses to make it explicit."* Ruff offers exactly that as an
unsafe (semantics-preserving) autofix:

```python
        assert [f["test_name"] for f in result["failures"]] == [
            (
                "tests/e2e/tutorial-1.browser.test.ts > main-street tutorial part 1 "
                "> step 3"
            )
        ], "only the tutorial failure is a suite failure"
```

`ruff --diff --unsafe-fixes` produces a slightly tighter, less readable
variant (`("...` / `"> step 3")` with mismatched continuation indentation), so
a manual 3-line wrap is preferable.

### Duplicate tracking of the same finding

`python3 skill/refactor/scripts/reverify.py --json` attributes all three of
these open items to the same `ISC004` / same-file finding, each currently
`still-reproduces`:

| Item | Family | Anchor | Stage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MWMOCL1Y004I9OR` (this item) | audit CFP chore | line 897 | idea |
| `SA-0MWMK06OU004AUPB` | code-quality item | line 897 | intake_complete |
| `SA-0MWMBFRTG00793NN` | refactor item (`Refactor-Finding-Key: ISC004:<file>`) | line 891 | intake_complete |

The audit chore is the only one that carries the producer-decision
requirement; the other two are "fix it" items. The audit chore's description
also embeds `Refactor-Twin: SA-0MWMBFRTG00793NN` (cross-family link added by
SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO).

### Waiver target

The chore description's one-off acceptance recipe targets
`SA-0MWB8W06O005FQHC` — the work item that was under audit when the screen
ran, not this chore. Audit waivers are stored as `AUDIT-FP-WAIVER:` comments
on the audited item, so Option A must be applied to that audited item (or to
the audited item of the next audit run), not to this chore, for the waiver to
take effect.

## Desired change

**Producer decision (2026-11-18): Option B — make the intent explicit by
wrapping the implicitly concatenated string in parentheses; Q2 "as
recommended" (this item is decision-of-record, the twins close as superseded).**

Concretely, in `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py`
(`test_retry_failed_is_red_and_never_discards`, line 896-899), turn

```python
        assert [f["test_name"] for f in result["failures"]] == [
            "tests/e2e/tutorial-1.browser.test.ts > main-street tutorial part 1 "
            "> step 3"
        ], "only the tutorial failure is a suite failure"
```

into

```python
        assert [f["test_name"] for f in result["failures"]] == [
            (
                "tests/e2e/tutorial-1.browser.test.ts > main-street tutorial part 1 "
                "> step 3"
            )
        ], "only the tutorial failure is a suite failure"
```

No audit waiver is recorded, nothing is excluded project-wide, and the
concatenated string value is unchanged — the only difference is that the
intentional multi-line split is now explicit. Once the finding stops
reproducing, `skill/refactor/scripts/reverify.py --apply` closes this chore
and the two duplicate items with evidence.

Rejected alternatives (for the record): **Option A** — accept as false
positive via `audit_waiver.py add` on the audited item (no code change); it
silences the audit chore only, leaves the two refactor/code-quality items
reproducing, and a file-wide waiver would mask future genuine ISC004
(missing-comma) hits. **Option C** — exclude ISC004 project-wide in a new
ruff config; too broad for one finding and introduces repository-wide config
for an optional rule.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` — line 897-898; wrap the
  implicitly concatenated string in parentheses (Option B) or leave untouched
  (Option A).
- `skill/refactor/scripts/reverify.py` — dry-run, then `--apply`, to close
  the three items once the finding stops reproducing (not modified; run only).
- Not touched under the chosen Option B: no audit waiver
  (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_waiver.py`), no ruff configuration file.

## Related work

- `SA-0MWMK06OU004AUPB` — `[LOW] …test_run_tests_failure_notices.py:897 —
  Unparenthesized implicit string concatenation in collection (ISC004)`
  (open, intake_complete). Same line; duplicate tracking item.
- `SA-0MWMBFRTG00793NN` — `Refactor: Unknown in
  skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` (open, intake_complete).
  Same rule + file (`Refactor-Finding-Key: ISC004:<file>`, anchor line 891);
  also referenced here as `Refactor-Twin`.
- `SA-0MWB8W06O005FQHC` — ruff PLW1510 in
  `skill/report/tests/test_check_producer_actions.py:249` (open). The audited
  item named in this chore's waiver recipe; a precedent for the
  "fix in code" resolution (`check=False`, commit `b2980e1943`).
- `SA-0MWB8VZKO0050NZE` (completed) — the ISC004 waiver precedent in
  `skill/report/tests/test_check_producer_actions.py` (producer chose
  Option A, waiver on the parent audit item). Companion waived siblings:
  `SA-0MWB8VYAP008H6VX`, `SA-0MWB8VYY1002VH47`.
- `SA-0MWB1AYW0003DKQR` / `SA-0MWMOCFHU007PLOZ` — other ISC004 candidate
  false positives in this audit batch (`scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`), same
  decision shape.
- Related framework work: `SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42` (audit CFP chores),
  `SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO` (refactor-twin cross-reference),
  `SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3` (re-verification sweep),
  `SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG` (finding identity + fingerprints).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — waiver breadth (Option A).** A file-level waiver suppresses future
  genuine ISC004 (missing-comma) findings in this file; a line-pinned waiver
  drifts on edits above line 897. *Mitigation:* prefer Option B.
- **Risk — waiving does not clear the twins.** The two refactor/code-quality
  items keep `still-reproduces` under a waiver, so a producer who returns to
  the lint queue sees the finding again. *Mitigation:* close them explicitly
  as superseded, or choose Option B.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Sibling ISC004 items (`SA-0MWMOCFHU007PLOZ`,
  `SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI`, `SA-0MWMOCAIK001RKZ6` in `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`)
  are separate findings with separate anchors; they are recorded as related
  work, never folded into this item's scope.
- **Assumption.** The project has no policy requiring ISC004 enforcement, and
  no ruff config selects it; the finding exists only because the audit scans
  with `--isolated --select ISC004`.
- **Assumption.** The concatenated value is exactly the single expected test
  name; parenthesising preserves it byte-for-byte (assertion unaffected).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (answered): Option A (waive), Option B (parenthesise in code), or
  Option C (exclude ISC004 project-wide) for ISC004 at
  `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py:897`?**
  Options offered: (A) accept as false positive via `audit_waiver.py add` on
  the audited item; (B) wrap the string in parentheses (3-line, semantics
  preserving); (C) exclude ISC004 project-wide in a new ruff config.
  **Recommended (offered):** B — removes the finding instead of suppressing
  it, keeps a file-wide waiver from masking future genuine hits, and clears
  all three duplicate items in one pass.
  **Answer (producer): "B" — parenthesise the string in code; no waiver.**
  Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-18. Recommendation accepted.
- **Q2 (answered): how should the two duplicate items
  (`SA-0MWMK06OU004AUPB`, `SA-0MWMBFRTG00793NN`) be consolidated?**
  Options offered: (A) keep this audit chore as decision-of-record, close
  both twins as duplicates of it after the fix reproduces clean (via
  `reverify.py --apply`); (B) make `SA-0MWMK06OU004AUPB` (already
  `intake_complete`, same line) the implementation item and close this chore
  as superseded; (C) leave both to close themselves on the next sweep.
  **Recommended (offered):** A — this item already carries the producer
  decision and the fix recipe, and the sweep closes the twins with evidence
  for free once the finding stops reproducing.
  **Answer (producer): "as recommended" — Option A.** Source: interactive
  reply, 2026-11-18.
- **Q3: does the waiver target discrepancy matter (waiver recipe names
  `SA-0MWB8W06O005FQHC`, the audited item, not this chore)?**
  Resolution (agent research): audit waivers are `AUDIT-FP-WAIVER:` comments
  **on the audited item**
  (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_chore_description_for_cfp_decision`
  renders `waiver_target = issue_id or "<audited-item-id>"`), so under
  Option A the `audit_waiver.py add` call must name the audited item, not this
  chore. Recorded as background, not a blocking question.

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles
- Failing commit: 6dafa2d4d983ef9e4df6cffc7f20152e1b85e730
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
def test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles() -> None:
        """Live syntax check: the committed template must produce no parse errors.
    
        Runs ``systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run`` against the template.  The
        dry-run never modifies the filesystem.  Parse failures surface as
        ``Invalid …`` diagnostics on stderr (e.g. a mistyped age or missing
        field); the exit code alone is not asserted because unprivileged runs
        report unrelated permission errors (e.g. root-owned private dirs).
    
        Skipped when the binary is unavailable (e.g. non-systemd hosts).
        """
        binary = shutil.which("systemd-tmpfiles")
        if binary is None:
            import pytest
    
            pytest.skip("systemd-tmpfiles not available on this host")
    
>       proc = subprocess.run(
            [
                binary,
                "--clean",
                "--dry-run",
                "--graceful",
                "--exclude-prefix=/tmp/snap
```

## Root Cause

The test runs `systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run` against the real `/tmp`, which contains ~538k inodes. Under host load this can take >120s (the test's timeout budget), causing `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` before any parse assertion is reached. The audit session confirmed: the identical command on this host takes 12.8s idle; under suite+parallel load it exceeds 120s.

## Plan

**Fix:** Replace `--clean` with `--root=/tmp/pi-probe-root` (a synthetic empty directory) in the subprocess call. This runs systemd-tmpfiles against an empty filesystem tree — the template path is still parsed and validated (same parsing path as `--clean`), but no /tmp directories are scanned, so the call completes in ~5ms regardless of host load. Verified: `--root` correctly detects parse errors (\"Unknown command type\", \"Invalid age\") in synthetic templates.

**Changed file:** `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` — one-line edit to the `subprocess.run()` call in `test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles`.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 6dafa2d4d983ef9e4df6cffc7f20152e1b85e730`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

The suite no longer stalls for minutes or times out when run on a loaded host — the tmpfiles syntax check now completes in milliseconds, so users can trust the test result instead of dismissing it as a flake.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py::test_template_parses_with_systemd_tmpfiles` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

# Problem statement

`audit_runner.py issue <id> --code-root <CODE_REPO>` (cross-repo audit, LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR) builds the Phase 1/Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest from the **code root**, then validates it against the **worklog owning root**, so validation always fails for a genuine cross-repo item — and the parent AC screen aborts with a scope error, leaving the persisted report with an **empty Acceptance Criteria table** while still recording `Ready to close: No`.

# Reproduction (verified 2026-11-19)

Item `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (worklog: games_curator, code: SorraAgents at `0c41811c67`):

```bash
python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU --force \
  --code-root /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
```

Log (`~/.audit_debug/games_curator/audit-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU-20261119-221941.log`):

```
[checkpoint] Phase 1 parent screening started
Error: Audit scope error: the Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest does not contain the work item repository files (owning project: /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator). The resolved scope is the audit skill's own tree or another repository; re-launch the audit from /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator and re-run.
[checkpoint] Phase 1 child screenings started
```

# Root cause

- `_phase_parent_screen` builds the manifest with `project_root=ctx.execution_root` (the code root) — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~line 15375.
- It then calls `_validate_file_scope_manifest(file_scope, owning_root, touched_files=...)` (~line 15383) — the worklog owner, not the code root. `_validate_file_scope_manifest` compares `_distinctive_project_top_levels(owning_root)` against the manifest text, so a manifest legitimately built from the code repo can never contain the worklog repo's distinctive top-level entries.
- The same mismatch exists in the Phase 2 path (~line 11230, `owning_root = _resolve_owning_project_root(...)` when `owning_root is None`).
- Secondary defect: the phase-1 scope error is printed and the screen returns 1, but `audit_runner()` continues into child screening / Phase 2 and persists a report whose AC table is empty — a fail-closed scope error should abort the run (non-zero exit, no persisted verdict) per the skill contract, never persist an AC-less verdict.
- The skill documentation already specifies that `--code-root` scopes "the file-scope manifest": only the validation root was left un-threaded.

# Desired change

- When `--code-root` / `AUDIT_CODE_ROOT` resolves a code root, validate the FILE SCOPE manifest against **that** root (i.e. the per-audit/code root, same value used to build it), keeping the owning root as the validation root only when no code root is given.
- Treat a Phase 1 parent-screen scope error as fatal for the run: abort before persisting any report, restore the pre-audit lifecycle, exit non-zero.
- Keep same-repo behaviour byte-for-byte identical (`--code-root <owning-root>` remains a no-op).

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A cross-repo item audited with `--code-root` reaches Phase 1 parent AC screening with no `Audit scope error`, and the persisted report contains one row per AC (non-empty `## Acceptance Criteria Status` table).
- AC2: A same-repo item audited with `--code-root <owning-root>` yields an identical manifest, validation outcome and verdict to the same audit without `--code-root` (regression-safe).
- AC3: A genuine mis-scoped launch (manifest built from the audit skill's own tree) still fails closed.
- AC4: A Phase 1 parent-screen scope error aborts the run with a non-zero exit, persists no audit report, and leaves the item's pre-audit status/stage restored.
- AC5: Unit tests cover the cross-repo validation root, the same-repo no-op and the fatal-abort path; the full project suite passes.

# Evidence

- Failing run log: `~/.audit_debug/games_curator/audit-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU-20261119-221941.log`
- Persisted report with empty AC table: `wl --worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/games_curator/.worklog audit-show CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU --json`

# Impact

Cross-repo work items can be audited with real acceptance-criteria verdicts instead of a report that says "not ready" without ever assessing a criterion.

# Related work

- discovered-from: `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU`
- Sibling defect: the F3 execution worktree is likewise hosted under the worklog owner (filed separately).
- Feature that introduced `--code-root`: LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR.

# Problem statement

For a cross-repo audit (`audit_runner.py issue <id> --code-root <CODE_REPO>`), the F3 full-suite execution worktree is created under the **worklog owning project's** `.worklog/worktrees/`, even though it is a worktree of the **code repository**. Any test in the code repo that resolves the repository root or the worklog by walking up from its cwd then resolves the *worklog project*, and fails — producing spurious blocking test failures and spurious critical `test-failure` triage children against the audited item.

# Reproduction (verified 2026-11-19)

Item `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (worklog: games_curator, code: SorraAgents at `0c41811c67`):

```bash
python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU --force \
  --code-root /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
```

Creates the execution worktree at `/home/rgardler/projects/games_curator/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU` (a SorraAgents worktree nested inside the games_curator checkout). The suite then reports two failures that do **not** occur in a correctly-scoped SorraAgents worktree:

| Test | Audit run (nested worktree) | `SorraAgents/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>` |
|---|---|---|
| `skill/shared/tests/test_resolve_repo_root.py::TestResolveRepoRootRealRepo::test_framework_root_resolves_to_main_checkout_here` | FAIL — `assert PosixPath('…/games_curator/.worklog/worktrees/repro-timing') == PosixPath('/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents')`, and `hidden`| PASS |
| `tests/test_timing_integration.py::TestHumanModeTiming::test_render_report_emits_timing_on_stderr` | FAIL — `render_report.py` exits 1: `wl show failed … database at games_curator/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=9 …` / `Work item not found: SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S` | PASS |

Reproduction commands (both verified): `git -C /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents worktree add --detach <path> HEAD` then `pytest -q skill/shared/tests/test_resolve_repo_root.py tests/test_timing_integration.py -k "…"` from `<path>`.

Consequence on the audited item: the timing failure was classified `integration / affected / blocking` (never excusable) so the audit reported `Ready to close: No`, and the triage path created a critical child work item from a failure that is purely an artifact of worktree placement.

# Root cause

`_create_execution_worktree(owning_root, runner, issue_id)` — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~line 12414:

```python
worktree_path = (
    owning_root / ".worklog" / "worktrees"
    / f"{_EXECUTION_WORKTREE_PREFIX}-{issue_id}"
)
```

`owning_root` is the worklog owning project. With `--code-root` the git commands resolve to the code repo (`runner` is cwd-aware via `git -C <code root>`), so a *code-repo* worktree is created inside the *worklog project's* `.worklog` — a path whose ancestor chain resolves to the wrong worklog store and the wrong "main checkout". Same class of defect as the FILE SCOPE validation root (filed separately).

# Desired change

- Host the execution worktree under the **code root** when `--code-root` is set (`<code-root>/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-<id>`), falling back to the owning root otherwise; keep the existing submodule-before-symlink ordering and node_modules symlink conventions.
- Optionally prefer a neutral location (e.g. system temp dir) when the code root is not writable.
- Same-repo behaviour must stay byte-for-byte identical.

# Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A cross-repo audit with `--code-root` creates its F3 execution worktree under the code root (evidence line names that path), and tests that resolve repo root / worklog by walking up from cwd pass.
- AC2: The two tests above pass in the audit's execution worktree for a SorraAgents-code audit launched from games_curator — no spurious `test-failure` child is created.
- AC3: A same-repo audit (no `--code-root`) keeps its current execution-worktree path and behaviour (regression-safe).
- AC4: The execution worktree is still removed after the run (no orphaned worktrees), including on the failure path.
- AC5: Unit tests cover the code-root worktree path, the same-repo path and cleanup; the full project suite passes.

# Evidence

- Audit log: `~/.audit_debug/games_curator/audit-CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU-20261119-221941.log`
- Spurious child created from the artifact: `CUR-0MWO4XL190016LFQ`

# Impact

Cross-repo audits stop inventing red-tree failures (and blocking critical children) that only exist because the test worktree was hosted in the wrong project.

# Related work

- discovered-from: `CUR-0MWIBGLIL00774EU`
- Sibling defect: FILE SCOPE validation root under `--code-root`.
- Feature that introduced `--code-root`: LP-0MVZ6R5H8007NYLR.
