## Goal

A recurring post-push verification refusal with `verdict=missing` (no full-suite cache entry for the pushed tree) is filed as a **critical `[test-failure]` item named "… — failing test"**, whose acceptance criteria no agent can satisfy, and every recurrence creates a *new* item because the triage dedupe only looks at critical items. Route such refusals as **gate/cache artefacts** and dedupe the signature **across priorities**.

## Root cause

1. **Mislabelling.** `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_post_push_failure_test_name()` falls back to `post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry` when no entry is `verdict=red`, and `_route_post_push_failure_to_triage()` files it through the triage helper exactly like a real regression. A cache miss therefore becomes a critical, agent-blocking "test failure" whose ACs ("the test … passes") cannot be met, and which only a human may close (false-positive rule in the runbook).
2. **Dedupe gap.** `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py::list_critical_issues()` queries `wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure` only, so all three match heuristics are blind to an identical signature at any other priority. Evidence: the same signature already existed as `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ` (commit `8169e29`, priority **high**) yet a second item, `VC-0MWOI6V8J000FHFL` (commit `af9370f`, critical), was created. The helper's documented "an existing matching critical `test-failure` item is enhanced instead of duplicated" contract consequently only holds among critical items.

## Producer decisions (2026-11-20)

- **Routing:** the fix lives in this repo (`SorraAgents`); the video_compiler item was a routing shell and was deleted after this item was filed.
- **Behaviour:** **keep the fail-closed refusal.** This item adds **no** self-heal and no finish-time suite runs; the cache-miss root cause remains with `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` (key the pre-push gate verdict on the pushed tree) and `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L` (cache key ignores worktree/env identity).
- **Duplicate:** `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ` was closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Scope (test-first ordering)

1. **Tests first** (`skill/triage/tests/`, `skill/implement/tests/`):
   - cross-priority signature match: an identical signature on a `high`-priority existing item is matched, a comment is added, and no second item is created;
   - gate-artefact routing: a `verdict=missing` refusal produces a gate-artefact title/tag with agent-satisfiable ACs;
   - regression guard: `verdict=red` still names the failing test from suite output and files a critical `[test-failure]` item.
2. `check_or_create.py`: match across all priorities (and by signature/commit), keeping "enhance, never duplicate"; record the recurrence as a comment on the existing item.
3. `implement.py`: name and route a `verdict=missing` refusal as a gate/cache artefact — distinct title prefix, tag, and ACs an agent can satisfy. The refusal itself stays fail-closed.
4. Runbook: add a "Gate/cache artefacts" subsection beside "Environmental failure signatures" in `skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md`, including the remediation (`run_tests.py --scope full`, then re-run `finish`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A post-push `verdict=missing` refusal is filed with a gate-artefact title prefix and tag, never as `[test-failure] … — failing test`, and its acceptance criteria are satisfiable by an agent.
2. An identical failure signature matches regardless of the existing item's priority: a recurrence adds a comment to the existing item and creates no second item (regression test covers a `high`-priority existing item).
3. `verdict=red` routing is unchanged: a red entry still names the failing test from its output and files a critical `[test-failure]` item.
4. The triage runbook documents the gate/cache-artefact signature and its remediation.
5. The full project test suite passes.

## Impact

A cache-miss refusal stops masquerading as a critical test failure, so agents are no longer blocked by an item nobody can close and operators see one tracker per signature instead of one per commit.

## Key Files

- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`
- `skill/triage/tests/`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/`
- `skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md`

## Evidence

- `_post_push_failure_test_name()` / `_route_post_push_failure_to_triage()` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (near line 5631).
- `list_critical_issues()` in `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` (near line 51).
- Commit `af9370f` on `origin/dev` was verified green (build, changed-scope finish gate, full suite: 51 files / 905 tests) — the reported "failure" carried no assertion, no stack trace and no test name.

## Links

- Origin (routed here, then deleted): `VC-0MWOI6V8J000FHFL`
- Duplicate closed: `VC-0MWO58KVE000I7XZ`
- Cache-miss root cause: `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV`, `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L`

# Epic drive cannot spawn headless child sessions — `pi -p` fails model resolution

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MWMPAW9P002DGZF (face-off parity epic), while driving its children on 2026-11-20. Replaces the tce-the-rising report RISE-0MWOIAJZJ002QYUO, which was re-homed here because the fix belongs to this repository.

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive <parent>` spawns a fresh headless child session per child, but on this machine every child session dies at startup because its model cannot be resolved (`No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` / provider `finish_reason: error`). The driver then burns its entire infrastructure-retry budget (5 attempts, 2 s doubling to 30 s) before stopping the chain, so an epic cannot be advanced by `drive` at all.

## Users

- **Operator driving an epic** (`/skill:implement <epic>` or the herdr downtime worker): "I want `drive` to spawn child sessions that actually run, so an epic progresses without me opening one session per child."
- **Operator diagnosing a stalled drive:** "I want an immediate, actionable failure naming the unresolvable pattern and the available providers, instead of five identical retries and a vague stop."

## Impact

An epic can be driven to completion by `drive` again — children spawn on a real model, and a genuinely unresolvable model pattern fails in seconds with a message that says what to fix, rather than stalling the whole chain for minutes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `drive` resolves the child session's model to a concrete, available `provider/model` pair before spawning and passes it explicitly (`--provider`/`--model`), **and** pre-validates that resolved model against the available model catalogue, refusing to spawn when it cannot be resolved. A permanently-unresolvable pattern fails fast (no infrastructure retries consumed) with a message naming the pattern and the available providers.
- A regression test drives the spawn-argument / pre-spawn validation path with an unresolvable pattern and asserts the fast-fail message and that no infra retries are consumed; a resolvable pattern still produces a correct argv that explicitly names the resolved concrete model, pinned by test.
- A manual verification records a `drive` run on a two-child parent completing both children on a machine configured with the local proxy.
- Documentation (implement skill reference → drive failure recovery, and the spawn-failure classification section) records the fast-fail behaviour and how to set a concrete model for driven sessions.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing spawn-failure semantics from SA-0MWLDZBTF004LJFP: an *unknown* failure still hard-stops the chain; only a genuinely transient provider/credential failure may use the bounded infra budget.
- Do **not** duplicate the configuration-side fix. Removing the unservable `MunitoAI/*` glob from the tracked Pi config is owned by SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN; this item is the drive-side resilience that makes any such pattern fail fast and spawn a concrete model.
- Pi does not consume `PI_PROVIDER`/`PI_MODEL` for its own model selection (they are exported to bash tools as session context), so relying on the child to "inherit the driver's resolved model" is not a valid fix — the model must be resolved and passed explicitly, and/or the child's own resolution validated before spawning.
- Scope-creep risk: do not attempt a general rewrite of Pi model resolution; confine changes to the drive spawner, the pre-spawn validation and the spawn-failure classifier. Record anything larger as a separate linked item.

## Existing state

- `_default_session_spawner` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` builds `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions` and passes **no** `--provider`/`--model` flag.
- `_child_session_env` removes only `PI_SESSION_ID`/`PI_SESSION_FILE`; it keeps `PI_PROVIDER`/`PI_MODEL`, but Pi does not consume those for its own model selection, so the child re-resolves from `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (`defaultProvider`/`defaultModel`/`enabledModels`).
- The live `enabledModels` contains the glob `MunitoAI/*`, which matches nothing because `MUNITOAI_API_KEY` is absent; `pi` emits `Warning: No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` on every invocation, and the child can select a model that errors at request time (`Provider finish_reason: error`).
- `classify_spawn_failure` correctly labels this `infrastructure` and retries it up to the shared budget; it cannot recover from a pattern that will never resolve.
- Related features already shipped: SA-0MWLDZBTF004LJFP (bounded infra retry for spawn-time provider failures), SA-0MWLDZ8ZN0030T15 (spawn-failure classification tests), SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN (remove invalid/stale model ids and the `MunitoAI/*` glob from the tracked Pi config).

## Desired change

Make the drive child spawn deterministic about its model: resolve and pass a concrete available `provider/model`, pre-validate it against the catalogue, and if it cannot be resolved, fail fast with an actionable message naming the pattern and the available providers — instead of exhausting five retries.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_default_session_spawner` / `_pane_session_spawner` spawn argv, `_child_session_env`, `classify_spawn_failure`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — spawn-argument / pre-spawn validation regression tests
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — drive failure recovery and spawn-failure classification sections

## Related work

- **RISE-0MWOIAJZJ002QYUO** — the original tce-the-rising report (deleted; re-homed to this item).
- **RISE-0MWMRBRFR0094KR0** — Face-off beat parity matrix (VFX): the child whose spawn failed, reproducing the defect.
- **RISE-0MWMPAW9P002DGZF** — Face-Offs initiated by the adversaries should be identical: the parent epic whose `drive` run surfaced this.
- **RISE-0MWOIAXAG008HMK3** — drive's sibling-worktree guard fails closed on pre-existing dirt: a separate `drive` robustness defect.
- **SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN** — Remove invalid and stale model ids from the tracked Pi configuration: owns removing the unservable `MunitoAI/*` glob (config-side root cause). Not a duplicate — complementary.
- **SA-0MWLDZBTF004LJFP** — Bounded infra retry for spawn-time provider failures: the retry behaviour this item makes fail fast on a permanent pattern.
- **SA-0MWLDZ8ZN0030T15** — Tests for spawn-failure provider classification.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (work-item home / cross-repo dispatch):** Options were (A) keep in `RISE` with manual SorraAgents-checkout implementation; (B) re-home/re-file as a SorraAgents `SA-*` item; (C) file a SorraAgents child and link. **Answer (producer, this session): "recreate the item in ../SorraAgents and delete this one."** Accepted: option (B). This item is the recreation; the `RISE` item is deleted.
- **Q2 (fix approach):** Options were (A) explicit `--provider/--model`; (B) pre-validate the child's resolved model and fail fast; (C) both. **Answer (producer, this session): "as you recommend"** → option (C), both. The AC1 phrase "or omits the flag so the child inherits the driver's resolved model" has been removed because Pi does not consume `PI_PROVIDER`/`PI_MODEL` for its own model selection.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MWM88J2D001HFMS** – Fix: session-baseline lifecycle across start/parent/drive (blocked)
- **SA-0MVLJWMQ8007EDW0** – Reconcile terminal child after spawn failure (completed)
- **SA-0MQ533A3M003N3ER** – Document how to execute skills via CLI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mwldzbtf004ljfp, absent, ac1, acceptance, accepted (+283 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mwldz8zn0030t15, 0mwldzbtf004ljfp, absent, ac1, acceptance (+282 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absent, ac1, acceptance, accepted, actionable (+271 more)

## Goal

Red-first regression coverage for the drive pre-spawn model validation path: a permanently-unresolvable model pattern must fail fast with an actionable message and consume **no** infrastructure retries.

User story: As the agent implementing this epic, I want the fast-fail behaviour pinned by failing-first tests, so the implementation in F3/F4 is driven by an executable specification rather than prose.

## Context

Parent: SA-0MWOUI3Q0006TTSY. Sibling F2 covers the spawn-argv assertions; F3/F4 land the implementation. Today `_default_session_spawner` spawns `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions` with **no** explicit model, `classify_spawn_failure` classifies the resulting `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` stderr as `infrastructure`, and `phase_drive` burns five retries (`--infra-retry-limit`, backoff `[2, 4, 8, 16, 30]`) before stopping.

Empirical facts to encode in the tests (verified on this machine):

- `pi -p … --model "MunitoAI/*"` exits **1** and writes to stderr: `Warning: No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"`, `Warning: Model "*" not found for provider "MunitoAI". Using custom model id.`, then a `404 … "code": "model_not_found"` line.
- `pi --list-models` exits **0** and prints a fixed-width `provider  model  context  max-out  thinking  images` table (the authoritative available-model catalogue).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test drives the spawn-argument / pre-spawn validation path with an unresolvable pattern and asserts the fast-fail message and that no infra retries are consumed.
- The same test asserts no child session is spawned (spawner call count is zero) and `infra_retries` stays empty, so the failure is charged to nothing.
- The fast-fail message under test names both the unresolvable pattern and the available providers.
- Catalogue parsing is unit-tested from a captured `pi --list-models` fixture, with no subprocess and no reliance on the host's model configuration.
- Tests are written first and observed red against the current code, then green after F3/F4 (the red observation is recorded in a comment on this item).
- Tests live in `tests/test_implement_drive.py` (or `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` when they exercise the retry accounting) and use the existing fake-spawner harness.

## Implementation sketch

1. Capture a `pi --list-models` sample as a test fixture string (Local Proxy / deepseek / MunitoAI rows plus the `No models match pattern` warning line).
2. Write the fast-fail test: patch the spawner, run `phase_drive`/the pre-flight entry point with an unresolvable pattern, assert the refusal message, `sessions_spawned == 0`, and the infra-retry counter untouched.
3. Write the catalogue-parse and resolution-precedence unit tests (they will reference the helpers F3 introduces — coordinate the helper names with F3 before merging).

## Constraints

- Tests must not shell out to `pi` or read the host's `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; everything is injected via fixtures and monkeypatched spawners.
- No new test-only seams in production code beyond what F3/F4 already introduce.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`

## Impact

Nothing user-visible on its own; it is the executable specification that keeps a stalled drive from silently regressing to five retries.

## Goal

Red-first regression coverage that pins the exact child-session argv for **both** drive transports: a resolvable model must produce an argv that explicitly names the resolved concrete `provider/model`.

User story: As the agent implementing this epic, I want both spawners' argv pinned by tests, so a future refactor cannot silently drop the explicit model and reintroduce the headless default-resolution defect.

## Context

Parent: SA-0MWOUI3Q0006TTSY. F1 covers the fast-fail/pre-validation tests; F4 implements the argv change.

The two spawn paths are:

- Headless (`_default_session_spawner`): `[pi_bin, "-p", "/skill:implement <child>", "--approve", "--no-extensions"]`.
- Pane (`_pane_session_spawner`, opt-in via `--pane-sessions`): `herdr agent start <agent> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve --no-extensions`.

Neither passes `--provider`/`--model` today, so the child inherits the machine's default model selection — which resolves the unservable `MunitoAI/*` glob on the affected machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test asserts that a resolvable pattern still produces a correct argv that explicitly names the resolved concrete model (`--provider <provider> --model <model>`) for the headless `pi -p` spawner.
- An equivalent test pins the pane spawner argv: the resolved `--provider`/`--model` pair is present in the `herdr agent start … -- <args>` argument list, alongside the existing `--approve --no-extensions`.
- The pane-transport test asserts `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` is unchanged and no model/credential material is added to the pane environment (authority stays in argv, not env).
- A test asserts the child argv carries a concrete pair with no glob or wildcard characters (`*`, `?`), so a pattern can never be forwarded literally.
- Tests are written first, observed red against the current spawners, and green after F4 (the red observation is recorded in a comment on this item).

## Implementation sketch

1. Extend the existing spawner tests to capture `cmd` via a monkeypatched `subprocess.run` (headless) and a fake herdr client (pane).
2. Assert the model flags and their order/value; assert absence of wildcards.
3. Add the pane env invariant assertion.

## Constraints

- No live `pi`/`herdr` invocation: both transports are exercised with fakes only.
- Assert on argv contents, not on log output.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`

## Impact

Nothing user-visible on its own; it locks the fix at the argv level so a driven child session can never again start on an unservable default model.
data.title: F2: Spawn-argv model pinning tests (headless and pane)

data.description:
## Goal

`drive` resolves each child session's model to a concrete, available `provider/model` pair **before** spawning and pre-validates it against the available model catalogue, refusing to spawn — in seconds, with no infrastructure retries — when it cannot be resolved.

User story: As an operator driving an epic, I want `drive` to fail immediately and tell me which model pattern is unresolvable and which providers are available, instead of burning five retries and minutes of wall-clock before stopping the chain.

## Context

Parent: SA-0MWOUI3Q0006TTSY. Depends on F1 (fast-fail tests). F4 wires the resolved pair into both spawners; this item owns **resolution + validation + fast-fail**.

Root cause on the affected machine: drive spawns `pi -p … --approve --no-extensions` with no explicit model. Pi then resolves the child's model from the ambient configuration, whose `enabledModels` contains the unservable glob `MunitoAI/*`; Pi emits `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"`, selects the literal model `*`, and exits 1 with a `404 model_not_found`. `classify_spawn_failure` matches the `No models match pattern` fragment, classifies the failure `infrastructure`, and `phase_drive` retries it on `--infra-retry-limit` (5 attempts, backoff `[2, 4, 8, 16, 30]`) — retrying a pattern that can never resolve.

Available-model catalogue on this machine: `pi --list-models` (exit 0, fixed-width table `provider  model  context  max-out  thinking  images`; the `No models match pattern` warning goes to stderr and must be ignored). Providers present: `Local Proxy`, `MunitoAI`, `deepseek`, `github-copilot`, `opencode`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `drive` resolves the child session's model to a concrete, available `provider/model` pair before spawning and pre-validates that resolved model against the available model catalogue, refusing to spawn when it cannot be resolved.
- A permanently-unresolvable pattern fails fast (no infrastructure retries consumed) with a message naming the pattern and the available providers.
- Resolution precedence is explicit, implemented once and pinned by unit tests: `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PROVIDER` + `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_MODEL` (must be supplied together; a half-set pair is an actionable error) → the driver's own `PI_PROVIDER`/`PI_MODEL` → Pi settings `defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` (project `.pi/settings.json` in the child worktree, else the global Pi config) → fail closed.
- A candidate resolves only when it maps to exactly one concrete catalogue entry; a glob candidate (`MunitoAI/*`, `deepseek/deepseek*`) must match exactly one concrete model, and zero or multiple matches are unresolvable (never a literal wildcard forwarded to `pi`).
- The catalogue is fetched at most once per `drive` invocation (a single `pi --list-models` call) and parsed by a pure, unit-testable function; a catalogue that cannot be fetched or parsed fails fast rather than spawning on an unvalidated model, and a missing Pi executable keeps the existing manual-instruction failure.
- The refusal is durable in the report and the log: `--json` carries the resolution attempt (pattern, precedence source, available providers, error), and no child entry is recorded as spawned.
- `classify_spawn_failure`, `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` and the infra-retry budget keep their current semantics: the fail-fast path stops the chain before the retry loop is ever entered.
- Changed-scope tests and the dev-push full suite pass.

## Implementation sketch

1. Add `_parse_model_catalogue(text) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]` (pure: split fixed-width/whitespace rows, drop the header, skip malformed lines) and `_available_providers(catalogue)`.
2. Add `_resolve_child_session_model(candidates, catalogue) -> {"resolved": "provider/model" | None, "source": ..., "pattern": ..., "error": ...}` implementing the precedence list and the exactly-one-concrete-match rule (reuse `fnmatch`; reject wildcards in the result).
3. Add `_resolve_drive_model(env, worktree_path)`: build candidates in precedence order, fetch the catalogue once via `_resolve_pi_bin` + `subprocess.run([pi, "--list-models"], capture_output=True)` (stdout only), cache the resolution for the invocation, and return the same dict shape.
4. Call it in `phase_drive` **before** the child loop and before any lock/spawn work; on `resolved is None`, log and return a failure report carrying `model_resolution` and a message naming pattern + providers (`sessions_spawned: 0`).
5. Export the resolved pair to the spawner (F4 consumes it) and record `resolved_model` on each driven child entry.

## Constraints

- Fail closed, never guess: no silent fallback to "whatever pi picks" — an unresolved model is a hard refusal.
- No new secrets in argv or in the pane environment; `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` stays `(DRIVE_RECURSION_ENV, WORKTREE_ENV, ENV_LOCK_TOKEN)`.
- One `pi --list-models` call per invocation (cached), never per child.
- Do not weaken `classify_spawn_failure`: a spawn that fails for an unrelated reason still follows today's classification and retry rules.
- Preserve the existing `--json` report's additive-only shape (new fields, no renamed/removed keys).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`

## Impact

A drive run that cannot serve its configured model now stops in seconds and names the pattern and the providers that do work, so an operator can fix the configuration instead of watching five identical retries.
data.title: F3: Resolve and pre-validate the drive child model

data.description:
## Goal Both drive transports spawn the child with the resolved model named explicitly on the command line (`--provider

--model `), so the child never depends on ambient default-model resolution. User story: As an operator driving an epic, I want every driven child session to start on the model the driver resolved and validated, so a child session cannot die at startup on an unservable default. ## Context Parent: SA-0MWOUI3Q0006TTSY. Depends on F2 (argv tests) and F3 (resolution/pre-validation). This item is the argv half of the fix: F3 decides *which* model, this item makes both spawners *use* it. Affected call sites in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: - `_default_session_spawner` — headless `[pi_bin, "-p", "/skill:implement ", "--approve", "--no-extensions"]` (`--verbose` optional). - `_pane_session_spawner` — `herdr agent start --kind pi --pane -- --approve --no-extensions`, then `herdr agent prompt "/skill:implement " --wait --until done --until blocked`. ## Acceptance Criteria - Both the headless `pi -p` spawner and the pane spawner pass the resolved concrete model explicitly as `--provider --model ` in the child argv. - The spawner callable signature carries the resolved pair (one new optional parameter, defaulting to `None` for direct/manual callers) and every production call site in `phase_drive` supplies it; a caller that omits it keeps today's behaviour rather than crashing. - A spawn attempted with an unresolved model is refused rather than silently spawning without the flags (F3's pre-flight already prevents this; the spawner asserts it as a fail-safe). - The model pair is never passed through the environment: `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` is unchanged and no credential material enters argv. - Each `children_driven` entry records the `resolved_model` actually used, so a drive report names the model per child. - The argv is documented in the docstrings of both spawners; the pane and headless paths stay behaviourally identical apart from transport. - Changed-scope tests and the dev-push full suite pass, including the F1/F2 regression tests written first. - Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (the dev-push gate enforces the whole suite, so a red tree cannot be pushed). ## Implementation sketch 1. Add `model: str | None = None` (or an explicit `provider`/`model` pair) to both spawner signatures and to `_select_session_spawner`'s forwarding. 2. Append `["--provider", provider, "--model", model]` to the headless `cmd` and to the pane `agent start` `args` (before `--approve`/`--no-extensions`), splitting the resolved `provider/model` string at its first `/`. 3. Pass the resolved pair from `phase_drive`; stamp `resolved_model` on the child entry. 4. Update both docstrings. ## Constraints - Pane/headless parity: the two transports must not diverge in what they pass to the child session (see the repository's game/Gym parity spirit — identical semantics, one shared helper for the argv extension). - `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` and `ENV_LOCK_TOKEN` propagation are out of scope and must not change. - Additive-only change to the `--json` drive report. **Key Files:** - `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` - `tests/test_implement_drive.py` - `tests/test_drive_child_session.py` ## Impact Driven child sessions start on a model that was verified to exist, so an epic drive no longer dies at startup because of an unrelated default-model setting.

## Context

- The **drive flags/environment table** (≈ line 3879) — add `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PROVIDER` / `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_MODEL` with their precedence.

## Implementation sketch

1. Extend the drive failure recovery section with a "Model resolution fails fast" subsection.
2. Update the flags/environment table and the pane-transport paragraph.
3. Update the spawn-failure classification narrative (retryable vs permanent), keeping the existing `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` wording intact.

data.description:
## Goal

A recorded, manual end-to-end verification that `drive` completes a two-child parent on the operator's local-proxy machine, plus a recorded negative check that an unresolvable pattern refuses in seconds with no retries.

User story: As the producer, I want evidence from a real machine — not a fake spawner — that the epic can be driven again, so the fix is trusted before the parent goes to review.

## Context

Parent: SA-0MWOUI3Q0006TTSY. Depends on F3, F4 and F5. Automated tests use fake spawners; this item is the only check that a real `pi -p` child session starts on the resolved model and completes its work item.

This item needs the operator/producer: it runs real child sessions (minutes of wall-clock, real model calls) on a machine whose Pi config points at the local proxy (`Local Proxy/code`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A manual verification records a `drive` run on a two-child parent completing both children on a machine configured with the local proxy.
- The recorded evidence is a `--json` drive report showing `resolved_model` per child, `sessions_spawned: 2`, zero `infra-retry` entries and both children reaching a terminal stage; it is attached as a comment on this item.
- A recorded negative check shows `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_MODEL=MunitoAI/*` (with `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PROVIDER=MunitoAI`) refusing in seconds with a message naming the pattern and the available providers, with `sessions_spawned: 0` and no infra retries.
- The two-child parent is a throwaway item created for the verification (not an in-flight epic) and is deleted or closed afterwards, so no stray items or worktrees are left behind.
- Any behavioural surprise found during the manual run is captured as a comment and, if it is a defect, filed as a child work item before this item is closed.

## Implementation sketch

1. Create a throwaway parent with two trivial children (each with a one-line AC set that a child session can satisfy and close).
2. Run `python3 $(skill_path implement)/scripts/implement.py drive <parent> --json` and capture the report.
3. Run the negative check with the unresolvable pair and capture the refusal.
4. Paste both reports into a comment, clean up the throwaway items and worktrees.

## Constraints

- Manual verification only; no new automated test is required here (F1/F2 already pin the behaviour).
- Do not run this against an in-flight epic — a failure would burn real child sessions.
- Clean up: remove the throwaway worktrees and items (see the worktree hygiene playbook).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`

## Impact

The producer has direct evidence that an epic can be driven to completion again on their own machine.

- Sequencing & dependencies review: test items (F1, F2) precede implementation items (F3, F4), which precede docs (F5) and manual verification (F6); dependency edges match that order; no cycles.
- Scope sizing review: each child is one production file plus its tests (F3/F4 share `implement.py` but are separable: resolution/validation vs argv wiring); every child is a deliverable increment.
- Acceptance & testability review: every AC is pass/fail checkable; the single manual item (F6) states concrete evidence (drive `--json` report with `resolved_model`, `sessions_spawned: 2`, zero `infra-retry` entries).

Interview outcome this session: **no new questions were asked.** The two open decisions from the originating session were already answered by the producer in this item's own Appendix (Q1: re-home to SorraAgents as a `SA-*` item; Q2: fix approach (C) — both explicit `--provider/--model` and pre-spawn validation), and the remaining choices are implementation detail that the parent ACs constrain. Three decisions were therefore taken as documented agent assumptions rather than silent invention:

- **A1 — Resolution precedence:** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PROVIDER` + `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_MODEL` (must be set together) → the driver's own `PI_PROVIDER`/`PI_MODEL` → Pi settings `defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` (project `.pi/settings.json`, else global) → fail closed. Rationale: an explicit operator pin wins; otherwise the driver's own working model is the safest known-good choice; the settings default is the last non-guessed fallback. Recorded in F3.
- **A2 — Catalogue source:** `pi --list-models` (exit 0; the `No models match pattern` warning goes to stderr) parsed by a pure function and fetched at most once per `drive` invocation. Recorded in F3/F1 (fixture-only tests).

Rationale: satisfies "no infrastructure retries consumed" without weakening the retry path that exists for genuinely transient refusals. Recorded in F3.
